translations.hypothesis: One of the Christian denominations' core beliefs is that words must be used to glorify God and that church funds are used for that purpose.

translations.source: Àṣe nlá ìjọ ti wà ní Rómù ó lé ní ęgbẹ̀rún ọdún, ìkójọpọ̀ agbára àti owó yí tí jẹ́kí àwọn èyàn ma ṣèyemẹ́jì pé bóyá a gbọ́ràn sí òfin yí.
translations.reference: The central authority of the church had been in Rome for over a thousand years and this concentration of power and money led many to question whether this tenet was being met.
translations.hypothesis: The church in Rome has been around for over 2,000 years, and the accumulation of power and money has caused some to question whether it is still in compliance with the original vision.

translations.source: Láìpẹ́ tí ìfúngunmọ́ni bẹ̀rẹ̀, Ilẹ̀ Britian bẹ̀rẹ̀ síní fi ikọ̀ ológun ojú omi dá ilẹ̀ Germany dúró.
translations.reference: Soon after the outbreak of hostilities, Britain initiated a naval blockade of Germany.
translations.hypothesis: Within a few days of the invasion, Britain began to mine German ports.

translations.source: Ọgbọ́n náà dára, yíyọ àwọn ǹkan èlò tí ológun àti àwọn ènìyàn, ṣùgbọ́n ìdènà yìí kò tọ̀nà fún òfin orílẹ̀èdè tí wọ́n fọwọ́sí tí àwọn tó wà ní òkè òkun fọwọ́sí fún ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọdún sẹ́yìn.
translations.reference: The strategy proved effective, cutting off vital military and civilian supplies, although this blockade violated generally accepted international law codified by several international agreements of the past two centuries.
translations.hypothesis: The tactic was effective, destroying military assets and equipment, but the blockade was a violation of international law and had been largely ignored by the international community for decades.

translations.source: Britain ma ń wa omi òkun tí àwọn ọka ojú omi ma ń gbà kọjá láti má jẹ́ kí èyíkèyí okọ̀ ojú omi wo gbogbo abala òkun náà, tó ma fa ewu fún àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi tí kò mọ ǹkankan.
translations.reference: Britain mined international waters to prevent any ships from entering entire sections of ocean, causing danger to even neutral ships.
translations.hypothesis: The British used to patrol the seas to stop pirates from attacking ships, but now the Royal Navy is too small to protect all the sea lanes, leaving some ships to fend for themselves.

translations.source: Torí pé èsì sí ìgbésẹ̀ náà ò pọ̀, Jamani retí irú èsì bẹ́ẹ̀ sí ìjàkadì ọkọ̀ abẹ́ omi t’aláìhámọ.
translations.reference: Since there was limited response to this tactic, Germany expected a similar response to its unrestricted submarine warfare.
translations.hypothesis: Given the limited response to the action, Germany expected a similar reaction to the naval rearmament.

translations.source: Ní ìgbà 1920, àwọn ìwà àwọn ènìyàn àti orílẹ̀ èdè tó borí ní alòdì sí ogn àti ìdáwà.
translations.reference: During the 1920s, the prevailing attitudes of most citizens and nations was that of pacifism and isolation.
translations.hypothesis: In the 1920s, the attitudes of people and governments towards drugs began to change.

translations.source: Lẹ́yìn wíwo ìbẹ̀rù àti oríṣìí aburú tí ogun àgbáyé àkọ̀kọ́ fa, gbogbo àgbáyé ti ń gbìyànjú láti yẹra fún irú ìṣẹlẹ̀ aburu bẹ́ẹ̀ ni ọjọ́ iwáj.
translations.reference: After seeing the horrors and atrocities of war during World War I, nations desired to avoid such a situation again in the future.
translations.hypothesis: In the aftermath of the devastation and destruction caused by the First World War, the world committed to prevent such a global catastrophe from ever happening again.

translations.source: Tesla kó lọ sí ilẹ̀ America ní ọdún 1884, láti lọ gba iṣẹ́ pẹ̀lú ilé-iṣẹ́ Edison tó wà ní New York Cit.
translations.reference: In 1884, Tesla moved to the United States of America to accept a job with the Edison Company in New York City.
translations.hypothesis: Tesla emigrated to the United States in 1884 to take up a position with Edison's company in New York City.

translations.source: O de si orile ede US, pelu senti 4, to je owo to ni laye lorun, pelu iwe ewi, pelu iwe akosile oniduro lati odo Charles Batchelor (oga re ni ise ti o se gbeyin) si Thomas Edison.
translations.reference: He arrived in the US with 4 cents to his name, a book of poetry, and a letter of recommendation from Charles Batchelor (his manager in his previous job) to Thomas Edison.
translations.hypothesis: He arrived in the US with only 4 cents in his pocket, a notebook, and a letter of introduction from Charles Batchelor (his former employer) to Thomas Edison.

translations.source: Ìlú China àdáyébá ní ọ̀nà ọ̀tọ̀ láti sàfihàn àwọn àkókò ìgbà; ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan ìlú China tàbí ìdílé tó wà ní ẹka agbára jẹ́ ìjọba tó dá yàtọ̀.
translations.reference: Ancient China had a unique way of showing different time periods; each stage of China or each family that was in power was a distinctive dynasty.
translations.hypothesis: China is unique in how it displays time; each Chinese city or region is a separate time zone.

translations.source: Bákan náà, láàárin àkókò ilẹ̀ ọba kan, ọjọ́ orí tí kìí dúró llójú kan, tí ó pín ìgbèríko.Eyí tí a mọ̀ ju nínú irúfẹ́ àkokò yìí ni ìbẹ̀ẹ̀rẹ̀ ìjọba mẹ́ta tí ó wáyé fún ọgọ́ta ọdún láàárin ogún ọba Han àti Ji.
translations.reference: Also between each dynasty was an unstable age of divided provinces. The best-known of these periods was the Three Kingdoms epoch taking place for 60 years between the Han and the Jin Dynasty.
translations.hypothesis: Also within a single dynasty, there was the custom of dividing the empire into provinces, each ruled by a prince. The most famous of these was the Three Kingdoms period which took place about 60 years between the Han and Jin dynasties.

translations.source: Lákòókò ìgbà ogun líle tó wáyé láàrin àwọn ọlọ́lá tó ń jà fún ipò.
translations.reference: During these periods fierce warfare took place between many nobles fighting for the throne.
translations.hypothesis: During the intense battles for position, a fierce hand-to-hand combat erupted between the soldiers.

translations.source: Ìjọba ilẹ̀ mẹ́ta jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára àwọn àkókò ẹlẹ́jẹ̀ nínú itàn àdáyébá ilẹ̀ China, ẹgbẹ̀lẹ́gbẹ̀ àwọn èèyàn ló kú nínú ìjà láti gba ìjókòó ààfin ńlá Xi’an.
translations.reference: The Three Kingdoms was one of the bloodiest eras in Ancient China’s history thousands of people died fighting to sit in the highest seat in the grand palace at Xi’an.
translations.hypothesis: The Three Kingdoms period was one of the most romanticized periods in Chinese history, with many people dying in battles to win the precious seat in the capital of Xi'an.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn àbájádẹ tí òsèlú ti àwújọ wa, bíi lílo ètò métíríkì, ìsípòpadà làti ìsẹ ìjọba ipá sí ìjọba àwa ara wa, jíjé ọmọ orílè-èdè àti ìgbàgbọ pé orílè-èdè jé ti tàwọn ènìyàn rẹ láìsẹ ti àdánìkànjọpọ́n aládarí kan ṣoṣo.
translations.reference: There are a lot of social and political effects such as the use of metric system, a shift from absolutism to republicanism, nationalism and the belief the country belongs to the people not to one sole ruler.
translations.hypothesis: Many of our social and political achievements, such as the use of metrics, the shift from welfare to rights-based approaches, the concept of the nation-state and the belief in the sovereignty of the people over the dictates of a single leader, are all products of this tension.

translations.source: Síwáájú si lẹ́yìn ìsọ̀tẹ̀ náà àyè láti sisé si´ sílè fún gbogbo àwọn òlùbèwò okùnrin èyí tó fi àyè gba àwọn to ní ìtalára àti pẹgẹdẹ́ jùlọ láti sẹ àsèyor.
translations.reference: Also after the Revolution occupations were open to all male applicants allowing the most ambitious and successful to succeed.
translations.hypothesis: Immediately after the screening, there was a seminar for all male participants, which provided an opportunity for the high-risk and priority cases identified during screening to receive counselling.

translations.source: Bákan na ni fún àwọn ajagun nítorí pẹ kàkà kí wọn fi kíláàsi sẹ ìwọ̀n ipò ajagun, wọn fi agbára sẹ e.
translations.reference: Same goes for the military because instead of army rankings being based on class they were now based on cailaber.
translations.hypothesis: The same applies to soldiers, as they are now more likely to be given a class of their own.

translations.source: Ogun àyípadà ìjọba ní ilẹ̀ Faransé ní ó jẹ́ kóríyá fáwọn òsìṣẹ́ ilẹ̀ míràn tí wọ́n ń fúngun mọ́ láti bẹ̀rẹ̀ àyípadà ti wọn.
translations.reference: The French Revolution also inspired many other repressed working class people of other country's to began their own revolutions.
translations.hypothesis: The French Revolution was partly inspired by the desire of other workers to begin their own revolutions.

translations.source: Àwọn ohun tó kọjá ayé yìí jẹ Muhammad lógún. Ó má ń lọ síbi ihò kan tí ó di ohun tí wọ́n mọ̀ sí “iHira” lórí òkè “Noor” (ìmọ́lẹ̀) fún àsàrò.
translations.reference: Muhammad was deeply interested in matters beyond this mundane life. He used to frequent a cave that became known as “Hira‘” on the Mountain of “Noor” (light) for contemplation.
translations.hypothesis: The following events are associated with Muhammad. He would go to a cave on Mount Hira for meditation.

translations.source: ó dé ara rẹ̀ pamọ́, ó sì yè, èyí fún wa ní àwòrán ìfa ọkàn nípa ti ẹ̀mi Mohammad.
translations.reference: he cave itself, which survived the times, gives a very vivid image of Muhammad’s spiritual inclinations.
translations.hypothesis: It was a physical blow, and it robbed us of a dear life, Mohammed's.

translations.source: Ìsinmi lórí ọ̀kan lára àwọn òkè àríwá Mecca, ihò àpáta náà ni a yàsọ́tọ̀ sí ìyókù lágbàáyé.
translations.reference: Resting on the top of one of the mountains north of Mecca, the cave is completely isolated from the rest of the world.
translations.hypothesis: Located in the north of the holy city of Mecca, the cave is one of the most important landmarks in the world.

translations.source: Kódà kò rọrùn láti wárí rárá tí èyàn bá tiẹ̀ mọ̀ pé ó wà. Tóba ti wà ní òkúta àpámọ́, o ma dáwà pátá pátá.
translations.reference: In fact, it is not easy to find at all even if one knew it existed. Once inside the cave, it is a total isolation.
translations.hypothesis: It is not even easy to find if you know where to look. Once it is in the landfill, it is gone forever.

translations.source: Kòsí ǹkan tí a lè rí ju ojú ọ̀run tó rẹwà tó sì mọ́lẹ̀ lókè àti ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn orí òkè tó yiká. Díẹ̀ lára àgbáyé yìí ní a lè rí tàbí gba láti inú ihò.
translations.reference: Nothing can be seen other than the clear, beautiful sky above and the many surrounding mountains. Very little of this world can be seen or heard from inside the cave.
translations.hypothesis: There are few sights more awe-inspiring and humbling than a clear starry sky overhead and a dark horizon all around. Some of the most beautiful things on Earth can only be seen or experienced in the dark.

translations.source: Pírámìdì ńlá tó wà ní Giza ni ọ̀kan péré nínú àrà méje tó sì ń fẹsẹ̀ múnlẹ̀ lónìí.
translations.reference: The Great Pyramid at Giza is the only one of the seven wonders that is still standing today.
translations.hypothesis: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

translations.source: Awọn ara Íjíbì́tì ni wọ́n kọ́ ọ ni ṣẹ́ńtúri kẹta sáájú ìbí Jesu, ibi ìsìnkú pàtàkì yìí jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ibi ìsìnkú tí wọ́n gbé kalẹ̀ láti yẹ́ òkú Pharaoh sí.
translations.reference: Built by the Egyptians in the third century BCE, the Great Pyramid is one of many large pyramid structures built to honor dead Pharaoh.
translations.hypothesis: The Egyptians were building pyramids in the third century before the birth of Jesus Christ, and this particular tomb is one of many royal tombs that were built in the desert to protect the bodies of the pharaohs.

translations.source: Giza Plateau àbí “Giza Necropolis” ní òkè Egypt àwọn tí ó ti kú ní àkópọ̀ onírúurú pírámíìdì (èyí tí ó jẹ́ pé pírámìdi ńlá ló tóbi jù) onírúurú ibojì kéékèké, tẹ́m̀pìlì lọ́pọ̀lọpọ̀ àti sphinx ńlá.
translations.reference: The Giza Plateau, or "Giza Necropolis" in the Egyptian Valley of the Dead contains several pyramids (of which the great pyramid is the largest), several small tombs, several temples, and the great Sphinx.
translations.hypothesis: The Giza Plateau or "Giza Necropolis" in Egypt is home to a group of structures including the Great Pyramid (the largest in the group) and several smaller pyramids, temples and the Great Sphinx.

translations.source: Wọ́n se àgbékalẹ̀ pírámìdì ńlá láti dá Pharaoh Khufu lọ́lá àtàwọn pírámìdì kékéèké, ibòjì àtàwọn ilé tẹ́ḿpìlì ni wọ́n kọ́ láti dá àwọn ìyàwó àti mọ̀lẹ́bí Khufu lọ́wọ́.
translations.reference: The great pyramid was created to honor the Pharaoh Khufu, and many of the smaller pyramids, tombs, and temples were built to honor Khufu's wives and family members.
translations.hypothesis: The Great Pyramid was built to house the tomb of the Pharaoh Khufu and the smaller pyramids, temples and tombs were built to house the wives and family of Khufu.

translations.source: Àmì “up bow” jọ bí V nígbàtí àmì “down bow” dàbí staple ti kò ní ìdí.
translations.reference: The "up bow" mark looks like a V and the "down bow mark" like a staple or a square missing its bottom side.
translations.hypothesis: The up bow is similar to a V and the down bow is similar to an inverted V.

translations.source: Òkè túmọ̀ sí wípé kí o bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní etí góńgó kí o sì taari ọrún, àti pé ìsàlẹ̀ túmọ̀ sí pé kí o bẹ̀rẹ̀ nísàlẹ̀ (níbití ọwọ́ rẹ ti di ọrún mún.
translations.reference: Up means you should start at the tip and push the bow, and down means you should start at the frog (which is where your hand is holding the bow) and pull the bow.
translations.hypothesis: The top is where you start at the bottom (where your feet are) and the bottom is where you end up (where your head is).

translations.source: Orun-oke ma n saba dun kelekele, orun-isale ma n dun ni ohun lile to lase.
translations.reference: An up-bow usually generates a softer sound, while a down-bow is stronger and more assertive.
translations.hypothesis: The upper atmosphere is usually much colder than the lower atmosphere.

translations.source: O ní àǹfànní láti fi gègé kọ àwọn àmì tìrẹ, sùgbọ́n rántí wípé ìlà àtẹ̀jáde tó wà níbẹ̀ wà fún iṣẹ́ orin, nítorínà wọ́n gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ bíbọ̀wọ̀ fún.
translations.reference: Feel free to pencil in your own marks, but remember the printed bowing marks are there for a musical reason, so they should usually be respected.
translations.hypothesis: You are allowed to use any of the provided stickers, but keep in mind that the comments section is primarily for music-related discussions and should be treated with respect.

translations.source: Ọba búburú Louis XVI, Queen Marie Antoinette àwọn ọmọ wọn kékèké méjì ( Marie Therese, ọmọ ọdún mọ́kànlá àti Louis-Charles ọmọ ọdún mẹ́rin) àti àbúrò ọba obìnrin Madam Elizabeth, ní ọjọ́ kẹfà, oṣù kẹwa ọdún 1789, ni ọ̀gọọrọ̀ àwọn ìyá ọlọ́jà lé jáde pada sí Paris láti Versailles.
translations.reference: The terrified King Louis XVI, Queen Marie Antoinette their two young children (11 year old Marie Therese and four year old Louis-Charles) and the King's sister, Madam Elizabeth, on the 6th October 1789 were forced back to Paris from Versailles by a mob of market women.
translations.hypothesis: King Louis XVI, his wife Queen Marie Antoinette, their two children (Marie Therese, aged 10 and Louis-Charles, aged 4) and his sister-in-law, Madame Elizabeth, were taken from Paris to Versailles on the night of June 20, 1789, by a large crowd of market women.

translations.source: Nínu kẹ̀kẹ́ ẹṣin, wọ́n rìrìn àjò padà sí Paris àwọn ènìyàn sí yí wọn kà , wọ́n han, wọ́n sì ń pariwo ìdérùba Ọba àti Aya ọba.
translations.reference: In a carriage, they traveled back to Paris surrounded by a mob of people screaming and shouting threats against the King and Queen.
translations.hypothesis: In carriages, they made their way back to Paris, where they were greeted by cheering crowds and a lavish royal welcome.

translations.source: Àwọn èèyàn tínú ń bí tí kan ọba àti olorì nípá láti má a ṣí fèrèsé ohun èlò tó ń gbé wọn lọ sílẹ̀.
translations.reference: The mob of people forced the King And Queen to have their carriage windows wide open.
translations.hypothesis: The people then asked the king and his ministers to please provide them with a means to cross the sea.

translations.source: Nígbà tóyá, ọ̀kan lára àwọn èrò ju orí olórí ẹ̀ṣọ́ tí wọ́n sekúpa ni Versaille síwájú ayaba tẹ́rù ti ń bà.
translations.reference: At one point a member of the mob waved the head of a royal guard killed at Versailles in front of the terrified Queen.
translations.hypothesis: Meanwhile, one of the most famous of the chateaux, the Palace of Versailles, was being prepared for the Queen's visit.

translations.source: Ogun tí àwọn ikọ̀ ogun Amẹ́rikà jà fún àwọn are Filipini ní àwọn ara Filipi fúnra wọn san páta.
translations.reference: The war expenditures of U.S. imperialism in the conquest of the Philippines were paid for by the Filipino people themselves.
translations.hypothesis: The war that the American army waged against the Filipino people was a war against the Filipino people themselves.

translations.source: A ro won lati san owo ori fun ijoba amunisin ti U.S. lati se akojopo awon koko ninu eto isuna ati ere lori idokoowo eyi ti a se loruko ijoba Philippine lati ipase awon ile ifowopamo ni Wall Street.
translations.reference: They were compelled to pay taxes to the U.S. colonial regime to defray a major part of the expenditures and the interest on bonds floated in the name of the Philippine government through the Wall Street banking houses.
translations.hypothesis: They were thought to be paying the U.S. government taxes on the earnings from a betting syndicate that was operating under the auspices of the Philippine Overseas Gaming Corporation (POGC), a company owned by the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR).

translations.source: Beeni, awon ere pupo ti a rigba lati ilokulo awon ara Filipini fun ojo pipe maa je ere ijoba ijegaba ilu Amerika.
translations.reference: Of course, the superprofits derived from the protracted exploitation of the Filipino people would constitute the basic gains of U.S. imperialism.
translations.hypothesis: Of course, many games won by Filipino players are games regulated by the United States.

translations.source: Láti lè jẹ́ kí Templers yé ọ o ní láti mọ ǹkan tó fa ìṣẹ́dá náà.
translations.reference: To understand the Templars one must understand the context that prompted the creation of the order.
translations.hypothesis: To help Templers understand you, you need to tell them what the transaction entails.

translations.source: Akoko ti awon isele naa ti sele ni won maa n saba pe ni Akoko Aarin Giga, akoko ninu itan abalaye Yuropi ni senturi 11th, 12th ati 13th (AD 1000-1300).
translations.reference: The age where the events took place is commonly referred as the High Middle Ages the period of European history in the 11th, 12th, and 13th centuries (AD 1000–1300).
translations.hypothesis: The period during which these actions took place is often referred to as the High Middle Ages, a period in European history from the 11th century to the 13th century (c. 1000–1300).

translations.source: Akoko Aarin Nla lo gbeyin Ibere Akoko Aarin, lo tun saaju Ipari Akoko Aarin, ti o pari ni bi 1500 nilana itan igbalode.
translations.reference: The High Middle Ages were preceded by the Early Middle Ages and followed by the Late Middle Ages, which by convention ends around 1500.
translations.hypothesis: The Middle Ages succeeded the Late Antiquity, and were succeeded by the Early Modern Period, lasting from about 1500 to the present day.

translations.source: Ìpinnu tí ìmọ̀-ẹ̀rọ jé asayan ọ̀rọ̀ gbogbogbò fún orísirísi àwọn ìlóyẹ fún ìmúsisé to´ gbòòro, kíkànípá ìmò-ẹ̀rọ tábì pàtàkì ìmò-ẹ̀rọ sí ìwòyẹ tàràtà wípé àwọn àmúyẹ ìwòyẹ tó nísẹ pèlú àwọn òfin ìmọ̀ sayenisi àti ìfarahàn wọn nípa ìmò-ẹ̀rọ gẹ́gẹ́ bí atọ́kùn kádàrá éníyán.
translations.reference: Technological determinism is a term that encompasses a wide range of ideas in practice, from technology-push or the technological imperative to a strict sense that human destiny is driven by an underlying logic associated with scientific laws and their manifestation in technology.
translations.hypothesis: The term “technology” is a general term for all applications of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, including engineering and applied sciences, but also for any intellectual or technical skill or means to achieve a goal, such as the scientific method or a specific technology.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ìtunmọ̀ ìpinu ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ pín àbá méjì, pé ìdágbàsóké ìms ẹ̀rọ fún rarẹ̀ fàyègba ọ̀nà tó jù àṣà àti òṣèlù lọ, ìms ẹ̀rọ nà ní “ipa” lóri àwùjọ tí a jogúnbá, jú àwùjọ ìlóniníyè lọ.
translations.reference: Most interpretations of technological determinism share two general ideas: that the development of technology itself follows a path largely beyond cultural or political influence, and that technology in turn has "effects" on societies that are inherent, rather than socially conditioned.
translations.hypothesis: Much of the debate over the social implications of technology divides into two camps, with the optimists and futurists arguing that technology provides the means to overcome many of the challenges and problems of the present day, while pessimists and neo-luddites see technology as a destructive force in society.

translations.source: Fún àpęrę à lè sọ pé ọkọ ló ń sokùnfà àtúnse àwọn ojú ọ̀nà.
translations.reference: For example, one might say that the motor car necessarily leads to the development of roads.
translations.hypothesis: For argument's sake, let's assume the roads are bad.

translations.source: Síbẹ̀síbẹ̀, ojú pópó jákèjádò orílẹ̀-èdè fún àwọn awakọ ayọ́kẹ́lẹ́ péréte kò le di síse pẹ̀lú bí ètò ọrọ̀ ajẹ́ sẹ rí, nítorínà àwọn ọ̀nà titun fùn ìselọ́pọ́ tó ń jẹyọ láti dín owó ríra ọkọ̀ kù.
translations.reference: However, a nationwide road network is not economically viable for just a handful of cars, so new methods of production are developed to reduce the cost of car ownership.
translations.hypothesis: However, the country's road network, which is primarily designed for pedestrians and cyclists, is not very accommodating to motorists, necessitating the development of new infrastructure to justify the expense of purchasing a vehicle.

translations.source: Bi opo eyan se ni moto ma n mu ki ijamba oko oju ona po si, iyen naa ma n muu ki aseda awon ona titun ni iwosan ara eyan to ti kolu ijamba.
translations.reference: Mass car ownership also leads to a higher incidence of accidents on the roads, which leads to the invention of new techniques in healthcare for repairing damaged bodies.
translations.hypothesis: As more people own cars, traffic accidents increase, which stretches the capacity of the existing trauma care system.

translations.source: Romantisimi ma n sába dá àṣà láti àwọn akosile awọn akọ̀wé bío Gọẹ́tì, Fíṣtì àti Ṣlegel.
translations.reference: Romanticism had a large element of cultural determinism, drawn from writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel.
translations.hypothesis: Romanticism drew on the literary traditions of the Gotic, Physiologic and Sturm und Drang schools.

translations.source: Ní ìlànà tí àkójọpọ̀ ẹgbẹ́ oníse, ẹ̀kọ́ nípa ìpìlẹ̀ ayé tún oníkálukú dá, bí ọjọ́ se ń gorí ọjọ́, ìṣe àti àṣà tí ó lọ́ mọ́ àgbéǹde ìpìlẹ̀ ayé, pẹ̀lú bí èyí se wà nísọ̀kan pẹ̀lú ipò àwùjọ èyí tó dára ju àwọn òfi àfipá gbé kalẹ̀.
translations.reference: In the context of Romanticism, the geography molded individuals, and over time customs and culture related to that geography arose, and these, being in harmony with the place of the society, were better than arbitrarily imposed laws.
translations.hypothesis: In a nutshell, anthropology is the study of human kinds, their cultures, and their development, both as individuals and as social groups, and their relation to the environment, with the aim of understanding the diversity of human experience and the ways in which people create meaning in their lives.

translations.source: Bí a ti ṣe mọ ìlú Paris gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìlú tó ma ń ṣàralóge ní àgbáyé, A mọ Constantinople gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìlú aṣaralógé tí feudal Europe.
translations.reference: In the manner that Paris is known as the fashion capital of the contemporary world, Constantinople was regarded as the fashion capital of feudal Europe.
translations.hypothesis: As Paris is known as the most romantic city in the world, Constantinople is known as the most romantic city of feudal Europe.

translations.source: Òkìkí rẹ̀ kàń̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí nǹkan ìjayé tí ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ ni nǹkan bí 400 A.D. tí ó sì gbòde tihtí di nǹkan bí 1100 A.D.
translations.reference: Its renown for being an epicenter of luxury began in about 400 A.D. and lasted up until about 1100 A.D.
translations.hypothesis: Its origins lie in a movement that began around 400 A.D. and lasted until about 1100 A.D.

translations.source: Ipò rẹ̀ dïnkù ní senturi 16th pápá jùlo nítorí pé àwọn Kruseda ti padà pẹ̀lú ẹ̀bùn bíi aṣọ síkì èròjà oúnjẹ́ tí wọ́n níwọ̀n tó pọ̀ ju nkan tó wà ní ọjà Bisantaini.
translations.reference: Its status declined during the twelfth century mainly due to the fact that Crusaders had returned bearing gifts such as silks and spices that were valued more than what Byzantine markets offered.
translations.hypothesis: Its position declined in the 16th century in part because the Crusaders brought back a taste for goods like silk and spices that were more easily obtained from the East than from the markets of Byzantium.

translations.source: Ní àsìkò yí ní gbígbé àkọlé tí olú ìlú oge láti Constantinople sí Paris di sísẹ.
translations.reference: It was at this time that the transfer of the title of Fashion Capital from Constantinople to Paris was made.
translations.hypothesis: At this time the official capital was moved from Constantinople to Paris.

translations.source: Àrà ìkọ̀wé Gothic lé téńté ní àkókò séńtúrì kẹwàá sí ikọkànlá àti ikẹrìnlá.
translations.reference: Gothic style peaked in the period between the 10th - 11th centuries and the 14th century.
translations.hypothesis: The Gothic script was developed in the tenth to twelfth centuries.

translations.source: Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ àṣà Bisantini ni apá ìlà orùn ni ipá púpọ̀ lórí aṣọ.
translations.reference: At the beginning dress was heavily influenced by the Byzantine culture in the east.
translations.hypothesis: In the Byzantine Empire in the east had a great influence on clothing.

translations.source: Àmọ́ṣá, látàrí ìlànà ìbáraẹnisọ̀rọ̀ tó falẹ̀, àwọn àrà lẹ́kùn ìwọ̀ oòrùn le wà lẹ́yìn pẹ̀lú bí i ọdún márùndínlọ́gbọ̀n sí ọgbọ̀n ọdún.
translations.reference: However, due to the slow communication channels, styles in the west could lag behind by 25 to 30 year.
translations.hypothesis: However, due to the curvature of the Earth, the southern lights may be seen as far north as 40°S.

translations.source: ní ìparí Middle ages western Europe bẹ̀rẹ̀ láti ṣàgbéga àrà wọn, ìkan lára ìdàgbàsókè tó tóbi jùlọ látàrí crusades àwọn ènìyàn bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí ní lo àwọn bọ́tìnnì láti de aṣọ.
translations.reference: towards the end of the Middle Ages western Europe began to develop their own style. one of the biggest developments of the time as a result of the crusades people began to use buttons to fasten clothing.
translations.hypothesis: Towards the end of the Middle Ages, Western Europe began to develop its own styles, one of the major developments being the use of buttons to fasten clothing.

translations.source: Ètò ọ̀gbìn aládàáni jẹ́ ètò ọ́gbìn tí a má ń se láti pèsè oúnjẹ tí yíò fún àìní àgbẹ̀ àti àwọn ará ilé rẹ̀.
translations.reference: Subsistence agriculture is agriculture carried out for the production of enough food to meet just the needs of the agriculturalist and his/her family.
translations.hypothesis: A kitchen garden is a small garden grown to provide vegetables for the grower and his family.

translations.source: Kò sí nǹkan tó lágbára nípa ètò ọ̀gbìn ohun jíjẹ, lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà ọ̀gáníìkì, ìlànà lílo irúgbìn nínú àkùrọ̀ kí a wá paápọ̀ mọ́ àwọn ìlànà tí kò ga ni lára púpọ̀, tí yóò sí mú èrè púpọ̀ w.
translations.reference: Subsistence agriculture is a simple, often organic, system using saved seed native to the ecoregion combined with crop rotation or other relatively simple techniques to maximize yield.
translations.hypothesis: There is little that is inherently wrong with the agricultural commodity chain, often the issue is with the policies that govern how we produce, distribute and consume food, leading to more negative outcomes.

translations.source: Nínú ìtàn, àwọn àgbẹ̀ ma ń siṣẹ́ àgbẹ̀ alábọ́dé nìkan, èyí náà ni wọ́n sì ń lò láwọn orílẹ̀ tóti gbèrú kan.
translations.reference: Historically most farmers were engaged in subsistence agriculture and this is still the case in many developing nations.
translations.hypothesis: Historically, smallholder farms have been more common, and this is still the case in some developed countries.

translations.source: Àṣà kekeke ma n so àwọn tó ní èrò bákanaa papọ̀ to n ṣe wọ́́n bii pé gbendeke awujo ti kọ̀ wọ́́n sílẹ̀ ó dẹ̀ ma n jẹ́kí wọ́́n ní idaraenimo.
translations.reference: Subcultures bring together like-minded individuals who feel neglected by societal standards and allow them to develop a sense of identity.
translations.hypothesis: The little traditions that bind people together and make them feel like they belong are often the most important to people.

translations.source: Àwọn ẹka àṣà ní ìyàtọ̀ nípasè ọjọ́ orí,èyà, kílaàsì, agbègbẹ̀ àti/tàbí jíjẹ́ akọ tàbí ab.
translations.reference: Subcultures can be distinctive because of the age, ethnicity, class, location, and/or gender of the members.
translations.hypothesis: Cultural groups are defined by age, gender, ethnicity, geographic region and/or socioeconomic status.

translations.source: Awon nkan to ma n mu ki asakekeke da yato ni ede, irisi, esin, oselu, ibalopo, agbegbe abi apapo gbogbo won.
translations.reference: The qualities that determine a subculture as distinct may be linguistic, aesthetic, religious, political, sexual, geographical, or a combination of factors.
translations.hypothesis: The causes of infertility are diverse, varying by region and country, and include biological, structural, hormonal, genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors.

translations.source: Awon ara asa-kekere maa saba fihan pe won je omo elegbe nipase ilo ara ti o dayato ati ti o ni ami, die ninu apeere re je ara aso wiwo, isesi ati agooti.
translations.reference: Members of a subculture often signal their membership through a distinctive and symbolic use of style, which includes fashions, mannerisms, and argot.
translations.hypothesis: Guinea-worm larvae are sometimes visible in the tissue of the affected area, which is usually a swollen and painful area under the skin, sometimes with an open sore and sometimes with an ulcer.

translations.source: Ìkan lára awọn ìlànà tí a n lò láti fi júwe bí ìdarapọ̀ ṣe ṣe pàtàkì ni kí a fi àpẹrẹ àwọn ọmọ tí ò kópa nínú ìdarapọ̀ mó èyàn nígbàtí wọ́n dàgbà nítorí àidásí, oríburúkú àti iṣilò.
translations.reference: One of the most common methods used to illustrate the importance of socialization is to draw upon the few unfortunate cases of children who were, through neglect, misfortune, or wilful abuse, not socialized by adults while they were growing up.
translations.hypothesis: One of the main reasons given for the importance of this early integration is the example of children who do not participate in integration efforts and struggle with addiction, depression and unemployment later in life.

translations.source: Won ma n pe awon omo kan ni “odaju” tabi alaileko. Awon eyan (nigba pupo obi won ni) a ti de awon odaju omo; nigba miin won fi omo naa sile nitori pe obi o gba aarun agbari ati idagbasoke ti omo naa nii.
translations.reference: Such children are called "feral" or wild. Some feral children have been confined by people (usually their own parents); in some cases this child abandonment was due to the parents' rejection of a child's severe intellectual or physical impairment.
translations.hypothesis: Some babies are referred to as “failure to thrive” or “faltering growth”. (Sometimes the mothers are blamed.) In some cases the child is left to die because the mother is sick and unable to care for the child or because the child is sick and the mother is unable to obtain medical care for the child.

translations.source: Awo omo to buru le ti ni iriri ijiya omode tabi isele buburu ki won to ja won sile tabi sisalo.
translations.reference: Feral children may have experienced severe child abuse or trauma before being abandoned or running away.
translations.hypothesis: Neglected tropical diseases can also cause severe morbidity and disability, even when successfully treated.

translations.source: Wọ́n sọ pé ẹranko ni ó wo àwọn mìíràn dàgbà; àwọn kan gbé inú aginjù fúnra wọn.
translations.reference: Others are alleged to have been brought up by animals; some are said to have lived in the wild on their own.
translations.hypothesis: Some animals are said to have grown to enormous sizes; some even ate people for breakfast.

translations.source: Nígbàtí ó bá jẹ́ ẹrànko tí kìí ṣe ènìyàn lo tọ́ ọ, ọmọ-Feral a máa hu irúfẹ́ àwọn ìwà kan (tí ó jẹ́ mọ ìrínisí)ó fẹ́rẹ̀ jẹ́ pé bí gbogbo ìwà tí àwọn ẹranko náà ń hu ló ń hù, bí í bíbèrù ènìyàn tàbí kí wọ́n má bìkítà ènìyà.
translations.reference: When completely brought up by non-human animals, the feral child exhibits behaviors (within physical limits) almost entirely like those of the particular care-animal, such as its fear of or indifference to humans.
translations.hypothesis: When it is a non-human animal that is the target, a feral child may exhibit similar behaviors (such as screaming) and vocalizations, while the animal's natural behaviors (such as fleeing or attacking) are suppressed.

translations.source: Niwọn bi eto ikẹkọ ti o dalẹ lori iṣẹ akanṣe ba mu ẹkọ rọrun ati ladun, atẹlẹsẹ mu u rọrun si.
translations.reference: While project based learning should make learning easier and more interesting, scaffolding goes a step beyond.
translations.hypothesis: Since learning through projects makes learning easy and fun, implementation should be easy.

translations.source: Ètò ní ṣíṣe n tẹ́lẹ̀ kì í se ọ̀na kíkọ́ ẹ̀kọ́ ṣùgbọ́n ìrànlọ́wọ́ tó ń pèsè àtilẹ́yìn fún olúkúlukú tó ń ní ìrírí ẹ̀kọ́ titunn bí èyí tó ń lo ètò titun lórí kọ̀m̀pútà tàbí bẹ̀rẹ̀ iṣẹ́ àkànṣe tiitun.
translations.reference: Scaffolding is not a method of learning but rather an aid that provides support to individuals whom are undergoing a new learning experience such as using a new computer program or beginning a new project.
translations.hypothesis: The programmes are not designed as a replacement for formal education but as a helping hand for individuals who want to gain a specific skill and experience, such as programming or starting a startup.

translations.source: Scaffolds lè jẹ́ àfojúrí ó sì lè jẹ́ gidi, a lè sọ pé olùkọ lè jẹ́ scaffolds ṣùgbọ́n bẹ́ẹ̀ ni ọkùrin kékeré kílípù bébà nínu Microsoft Office.
translations.reference: Scaffolds can be both virtual and real, in other words, a teacher is a form of scaffold but so is the little paperclip man in Microsoft Office.
translations.hypothesis: Scaffolds can be formal or informal, we could say that teachers are often the ones who provide the most obvious scaffolds, but a young boy learning Microsoft Office is also being scaffolded.

translations.source: Ìlànà ìkọ́ni tó fún àwọn akẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ ní àǹfànní láti lóye kíkún tíwọ́n kó sínú ohun èlò ni láti fi bèèrè ìbéèrè àti ìsàlàyé àwọn ọ̀nà àátọ̀ tí ó lè jẹ́ ìpènijà fáwọn àkẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ láti dá ṣe.
translations.reference: Virtual Scaffolds are internalized in the software and are meant to question, prompt, and explain procedures that may have been to challenging for the student to handle alone.
translations.hypothesis: An instructional strategy that gives students opportunities to explore a topic in depth by asking questions and investigating answers in a variety of ways that appeal to different learning styles.

translations.source: Wọ́n fi àwọn ọmọdé sí ilé ìtọ́jú àwọn ọmọdé fún ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìdí, bẹ̀ẹ̀rẹ̀ láti ìpatì, sí ìfìyàjẹni àti ìlọ́nilọ́wọ́gbà.
translations.reference: Children are placed in Foster Care for a wide variety of reasons that range from neglect, to abuse, and even to extortion.
translations.hypothesis: Children are placed in orphanages for many reasons, including disability, abandonment and poverty.

translations.source: Kò yẹ kí ọmọ kankan dàgbà sí agbẹ̀gbẹ̀ tí kò ní rí ìtọ́jú, ìkẹ́, àti ẹ̀kọ gba sùgbọn o má n sẹlẹ̀.
translations.reference: No child should ever have to grow up in an environment that is not nurturing, caring, and educational, but they do.
translations.hypothesis: No child should have to grow up without the care, protection and education they deserve but all too often they do.

translations.source: A wòye Ilànà Ibùdó Itọ́jú là ń wòye pé ó jẹ́ ibi ààbò fáwọn ọmọ wọ̀nyìí.
translations.reference: We perceive the Foster Care System to be a safety zone for these children.
translations.hypothesis: We see the Therapeutic Community Approach as a safe space for these children.

translations.source: Ó yẹ kí ìlànà ètò ìgbanitọ́ pèsè ilé tó ní ààbò, àwọn olùtọ́jú tí ó nífẹ̀ẹ́, ètò ẹ̀kọ́ tó dúró re àti ètò ìtọ́jú tó se é gbáralé.
translations.reference: Our foster care system is supposed to provide safe homes, loving caregivers, stable education, and reliable health care.
translations.hypothesis: The quality of the care environment should provide safe, clean and stimulating surroundings, with well-trained and caring staff and a focus on family and community engagement.

translations.source: O ye ki mojuto omolomo pese gbogbo ohun elo pataki ti o to ni ile ti won yo won tele.
translations.reference: Foster care is supposed to provide all the necessities that were lacking in the home they were previously taken from.
translations.hypothesis: It is assumed that the infant has access to all the necessary resources to thrive in the home environment.

translations.source: Ìtàkùn ayélujára ṣe àgbájọ ìbáraẹ́nisọ̀rọ̀ gbogbogbò àti ọlọ́danni.
translations.reference: The Internet combines elements of both mass and interpersonal communication.
translations.hypothesis: The Internet brings together all the world's telephones and computers.

translations.source: Ìṣesí arà ọ̀tọ̀ tí ayélujára ni ó fa ọ̀nà àrà ọ̀tọ̀,ní ti ìlò rẹ̀ àti ọ̀nà ìtẹ́nilọ́rùn.
translations.reference: The distinct characteristics of the Internet lead to additional dimensions in terms of the uses and gratifications approach.
translations.hypothesis: The unique nature of online gambling creates unique challenges for the industry, its users and society at large.

translations.source: Fún àpẹrẹ, “Kíkọ́ ẹ́kọ́” àti “jíjáde” ní a mọ̀ sí ìwúrí tó ṣe pàtàki fún ìlò íńtánẹ́ẹ̀tì (James et al., 1995.
translations.reference: For example, “learning” and “socialization” are suggested as important motivations for Internet use (James et al., 1995).
translations.hypothesis: For example, “learning” and “information seeking” have been described as key motivations for Internet use (James et al., 1995).

translations.source: “Ìlọ́wọ́sí ara ẹni “ àti “ìbásepọ̀ tó tèsíwajú” wà lára ìdanimọ̀ fún àwọn abala ìwúrí titun nípasẹ̀ Eighmey ati McCord (1998) nígbà tí wón ṣe ìwádìí ìhà ohun olumulo ojú opòpó wẹ́ẹ̀bù.
translations.reference: “Personal involvement” and “continuing relationships” were also identified as new motivation aspects by Eighmey and McCord (1998) when they investigated audience reactions to websites.
translations.hypothesis: “Self-help” and “interactive” were two of the defining characteristics of the early online support groups identified by Eighmey & McCord (1998) in their research on the history of the World Wide Web.

translations.source: Ìlò gbìgba fídíò sílẹ̀ tí gbé dé àwọn àwárí tó ṣe pàtàkì nínu ìsọ̀tumọ̀ micros expression, yíyí ojú, èyí tí kò pẹ́.
translations.reference: The use of video recording has led to important discoveries in the interpretation of micro-expressions, facial movements which last a few milliseconds.
translations.hypothesis: The use of video recording has enabled breakthrough in the analysis of subtle facial expressions, the so-called micro-expressions, that occur unconsciously and reveal a person's true feelings.

translations.source: Ní pàtó a lè se àwárí̀ bóyá ènìyàn ń parọ́ nípa títú àmì ara tó keré jùlọ.
translations.reference: In particular, it is claimed that one can detect whether a person is lying by interpreting micro-expressions correctly.
translations.hypothesis: In particular, we can now detect if a person is blinking by analyzing the subtle movements of the facial landmarks.

translations.source: Ninu iew re Oro Aare, Olifa Saksi toka si bi awon eya ti o le gbo oro nitori ijamba opolo le sagbeyewo ododo mo dara dara. .
translations.reference: Oliver Sacks, in his paper The President's Speech, indicated how people who are unable to understand speech because of brain damage are nevertheless able to assess sincerity accurately.
translations.hypothesis: In his view, the King's English, a standard variety of English based on the speech of London, is just as valid as any other variety of English.

translations.source: Ó tilẹ̀ tún fi kún un pé òye láti túmọ̀ ìwà ọmọ ènìyàn ni àwọn ẹranko bí ajá ilé náà le ní.
translations.reference: He even suggests that such abilities in interpreting human behavior may be shared by animals such as domestic dogs.
translations.hypothesis: He also added that the ability to mimic human behaviour is not exclusive to animals like parrots.

translations.source: Iwadi ní senturi 20th ti fi hàn wípé a lẹ̀ dá iyato jenetiki sí odò mẹ́jì: eyi to pamọ́ àti eyi tó han.
translations.reference: Twentieth century research has shown that there are two pools of genetic variation: hidden and expressed.
translations.hypothesis: Studies in the 21st century have revealed a more complex genetic architecture, with both rare and common variants contributing to risk.

translations.source: Àṣìṣe tí o wáyé ṣe àfikún àti ìyípadà sí ìmọ̀ orírùn, nígbàtí ìyàsọ́tọ̀ sì yọ ọ́ kúrò nínú agbami ìyípadà.
translations.reference: Mutation adds new genetic variation, and selection removes it from the pool of expressed variation.
translations.hypothesis: Mistakes are made, and edits introduce new errors, while censorship removes material from the flow of revision.

translations.source: Ìpínyà àti àtúnlò ìyàtò síwájú àti sẹ́yìn láàrin igun méjèèjì pẹ̀lú ìran kọ̀ọ̀kan.
translations.reference: Segregation and recombination shuffle variation back and forth between the two pools with each generation.
translations.hypothesis: The exchange and adaptation of innovations between the two ends and among different regions.

translations.source: Ní gbangba sàfánà, ó ṣòro fún pírámètì tí ęya ara oúnjẹ́ jíję rẹ̀ jọ ti èyàn, láti rí ásìdì amino tí ara rẹ̀ ní lò láti ara ewé.
translations.reference: Out on the savanna, it is hard for a primate with a digestive system like that of humans to satisfy its amino-acid requirements from available plant resources.
translations.hypothesis: In general, it is more difficult for the human body to get the amino acids it needs from plant sources.

translations.source: Sibe si, ti o ba ko lati se, o leyin: idiwo idagbasoke, ailounje, ati iku bopeboya.
translations.reference: Moreover, failure to do so has serious consequences: growth depression, malnutrition, and ultimately death.
translations.hypothesis: However, if you must, here are the pros and cons.

translations.source: Ohun inu ẹwẹ́ tó máà wà nílè jú Iọ je àwọn oúnje ìdàgbàsókè tinú ẹwẹ́ àti ti ìrísí èwà, sùgbọn kọ rọgbọ fún àwọn prímẹ́ẹ̀tì bìí tàwa láti gba sára àfi tí a ba se e.
translations.reference: The most readily accessible plant resources would have been the proteins accessible in leaves and legumes, but these are hard for primates like us to digest unless they are cooked.
translations.hypothesis: The only things you get from eating raw fish are the nutrients in the fish and the taste, but not much more unless it is prepared in a way to obtain the oil.

translations.source: Níyàtọ̀ ó rọgbọ láti gba ẹran (èrà, tambolo ati ẹ̀yin sára, wọ́n tún ma n pèsè ounje idagbasoke púpọ̀ tó ní àwọn asidi amino pàtàkì.
translations.reference: In contrast, animal foods (ants, termites, eggs) not only are easily digestible, but they provide high-quantity proteins that contain all the essential amino acids.
translations.hypothesis: In contrast, animal products (meat, poultry, fish, eggs and dairy) are highly digestible and provide the essential amino acids.

translations.source: Láì fi nkankan sílẹ̀, kò yẹ kó jẹ́ ìyàlénu tí àwọn babanla wa wá èsì fún “ìṣòro ounje ìdàgbàsókè” lọ́nà tó fẹ́ jọ bíi ti àwọn ọ̀bọ sàfánà ṣe n ṣe tiwọn.
translations.reference: All things considered, we should not be surprised if our own ancestors solved their "protein problem" in somewhat the same way that chimps on the savanna do today.
translations.hypothesis: Quite frankly, it should not be surprising that our leaders have responded to the "developmental nutrition challenge" in such a self-serving manner.

translations.source: Dídá orun mọ́yàn lójú ní ètò títají nígbàtí o bá ń sun orun tàbí nígbàtí o bá ń tòǹgbé tóbáyá (ìṣẹ́jú mẹwàá sí ọgọ́ta.
translations.reference: Sleep interruption is the process of purposefully awakening during your normal sleep period and falling asleep a short time later (10–60 minutes).
translations.hypothesis: Wear clothing that covers as much of your body as possible while still allowing you to sleep comfortably (10–60 minutes).

translations.source: Eleyi le seese ni bonkele nipa lilo aago itaniji ti ko pariwo lati muni ni ooye ohun ti o n sele laiji patapata.
translations.reference: This can be easily done by using a relatively quiet alarm clock to bring you to consciousness without fully waking you.
translations.hypothesis: This can be eased by using a regular expression to match the beginning of the line.

translations.source: Tí o bá rí ara rẹ pé ò ń yí ọwọ́ ago padà ní ojú àlá rẹ, o le è gbé sí òdi kejì yàrá ní ibi tí ọwọ́ rẹ̀ kò tí ni to o láti pa á.
translations.reference: If you find yourself resetting the clock in your sleep, it can be placed on the other side of the room, forcing you to get out of bed to turn it off.
translations.hypothesis: If you find yourself in a situation where you are being threatened, it may be best to give up your wallet and other valuables so that you can live to fight another day.

translations.source: Àwọn àṣàyàn mín tó dá lóri bayoritimi ma n nílo mimu nkan olomi (pápá jùlọ omi àbi tí tí a n pè ní diuretiki) ki o tó sùn, o ma n mú kí èyàn maa jítọ̀ dandandan.
translations.reference: Other biorhythm-based options involve drinking lots of fluid (particularly water or tea, a known diuretic) prior to sleep, forcing one to get up to urinate.
translations.hypothesis: Some of the more common medical treatments for bedwetting involve the use of fluids that reduce the amount of urine produced overnight.

translations.source: Iye àláfíà àtinúwá tí ẹnìkan ní jẹ́ ìdàkejì si iye ẹ̀dọ̀fún tó wà nínu rẹ.
translations.reference: The amount of inner peace a person possesses correlates oppositely to the amount of tension in one’s body and spirit.
translations.hypothesis: The amount of information a person is exposed to is inversely related to the amount of attention they are able to give to it.

translations.source: Bí ẹ̀dọ̀fun ṣe lọlẹ̀ tó, ni bí rere ayé ṣe ṣe ara rẹ̀. Gbogbo ènìyàn ní agbára láti ní aláfíà àti ìtẹ́lọ́rùn.
translations.reference: The lower the tension, the more positive the life force present. Every person has the potential to find absolute peace and contentment.
translations.hypothesis: The more positive you are, the better your life will be. Everyone has the ability to be happy and peaceful.

translations.source: Gbogbo eyan lo le de ipo imo ijinle, nkan soso to n dinna aleba yi ni irora wa ati ilodi si w.
translations.reference: Everyone can achieve enlightenment. The only thing standing in the way of this goal is our own tension and negativity.
translations.hypothesis: Everyone is capable of reaching a high level of knowledge, the only limits are our curiosity and our will to learn.

translations.source: Tibetan Buddhism dá lórí kíkọ́ Buddha, ṣùgbọ́n mahayana fàágùn nípasẹ̀ àwọn oríṣi ọ̀na láti Indian Yoga.
translations.reference: The Tibetan Buddhism is based on the teachings of Buddha, but were extended by the mahayana path of love and by a lot of techniques from Indian Yoga.
translations.hypothesis: Tibetan Buddhism is based on Mahayana Buddhism, but incorporates tantric practices from the Vajrayana tradition of Indian Yoga.

translations.source: Ní ti àlàkalẹ̀, Buddhism ti ilẹ̀ Tibetan rọrùn. Ó ní àṣàrò Kundalini Yoga,àtipa àgbélárugẹ ìfẹ́.
translations.reference: In principle the Tibetan Buddhism is very simple. It consists of Kundalini Yoga, meditation and the path of all-embracing love.
translations.hypothesis: In its purest form, Tibetan Buddhism is very simple. It has the Kundalini Yoga, and the tantric path of the upward surge of love.

translations.source: Pẹ̀lú Kundalini Yoga àgbàrá yìí (àgbàrá ìmòye) máa ń di jìjì dìde nípasẹ̀ àwọn ìdúró Yoga, àwọn ẹré ìdárayá mímí, àwọn èrò àtúnwí àti ìwọran.
translations.reference: With Kundalini Yoga the Kundalini energy (enlightenment energy) is awakened through yoga postures, breathing exercises, mantras and visualizations.
translations.hypothesis: With Kundalini Yoga this subtle energy (Kundalini) is awakened through the practice of Yoga postures, breathing techniques, mantras and meditation.

translations.source: Ibùdó àṣàrò Tibetan ni Òòṣà Yoga. Látara lílo àfihàn àwọn onírúurú òòṣà, wọ́n ń sàtúnfọ̀ agbára, wọ́n pe àwọn chakras síta, ìtají sì wáyé.
translations.reference: The center of Tibetan meditation is the Deity Yoga. Through the visualization of various deities the energy channels are cleaned, the chakras are activated and the enlightenment consciousness is created.
translations.hypothesis: The Tibetan Buddhist deity Padmasambhava is a wrathful god. Through the visualization of various deities, energies are manipulated, chakras opened, and ultimately enlightenment is achieved.

translations.source: Jámánì jẹ ọ̀tá gbogbo ní àsìkò ogun àgbáyé kejì, èyí tó yọrísí ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ láàrin ilẹ̀ USSR àti USA. Pẹ̀lú òpin sí ogun náà, ifigagbaga ètò, ìlànà àti àṣà ló mú àwọn orílẹ̀-èdè náà túká .
translations.reference: Germany was a common enemy in World War 2, leading to cooperation between the USSR and USA. With the end of the war the clashes of system, process and culture led to the countries falling out.
translations.hypothesis: Germany was the battleground for much of World War II, and the subsequent division of Germany into East and West Germany reflected the political and ideological divide that had developed between the Soviet Union and the United States.

translations.source: Pẹ̀lú ọdún méjì tí ogun náà fi parí, àwọn tó jẹ́ ọ̀rẹ́ tẹ́lẹ̀ ti wá di ọ̀tà, Ogun abẹ́lé náà wá bẹ̀rẹ̀.
translations.reference: With two years of the end of the war, the former allies were now enemies and the Cold War began.
translations.hypothesis: Two years after the end of the war, old friendships had been replaced by mutual suspicion, and the cold war began.

translations.source: Ó yẹ kí ó pẹ́ tó ogójì ọdún tó ń bọ̀ àti pé a ó ja ìjà òtítọ́ nípasẹ̀ asojú àwọn ọmọ ogun ní ojú ogun láti ilẹ̀ adúláwọ̀ lọ sí Asia, ní Afghanistan, Cuba àtàwọn ibòmíràn.
translations.reference: It was to last for the next 40 years and would be fought for real, by proxy armies, on battlefields from Africa to Asia, in Afghanistan, Cuba and many other places.
translations.hypothesis: It will be at least another decade before there is a credible chance of a negotiated settlement through the representatives of the warring parties to the conflict in Africa, in Afghanistan, in the Balkans, in Cuba and elsewhere.

translations.source: Bí yíó ba fi di ọjọ́ kẹtàdínlógún oṣù kẹsàn án, 1993, ikọ̀ alábòbò ilẹ̀ Poland àti ìrètí tó wà ni láti sàtúnse ìpàgọ́ àti àtúngbékalẹ̀ pẹ̀lú ilẹ̀ Ròòmù.
translations.reference: By September 17, 1939, the Polish defense was already broken, and the only hope was to retreat and reorganise along the Romanian bridgehead.
translations.hypothesis: By September 21, 1993, the Polish Border Guard and hope of restoring order and cooperation with Italy had faded.

translations.source: Amóò, àwọn ètò wọ̀nyí kúròláṣà mọ́jú nígbàtí bíi ajagun 800,000 láti Egbe Ajagun Pupa tì Ìgbìmọ̀ Sofieti wọlé, wọ́n díbọ́n Belarusi àti Yukireni léhin tí wọ́n ṣẹ́gun apá ila òórùn Polandi, ní ìlòdì sí Àdéhùn Àláfíà Riga, Àdéhùn Má-Jàkadì Sofieti-Polandi, pẹ̀lú gbogbo àwọn Àdéhùn ìlúsílù, àti t’oníìlú méjì ati t’oníìlú púpọ̀ si.
translations.reference: However, these plans were rendered obsolete nearly overnight, when over 800,000 soldiers from the Soviet's Union Red Army entered and created the Belarussian and Ukrainian fronts after invading the eastern regions of Poland in violation of the Riga Peace Treaty, the Soviet-Polish Non-Aggression Pact, and other international treaties, both bilateral and multilateral.
translations.hypothesis: However, these plans were discarded when about 800,000 troops of the Southern Front of the Soviet Union invaded Belarus and Ukraine after crossing the border of Eastern Poland, in violation of the Riga Peace Treaty, the Soviet-Polish Non-Aggression Pact, and all other international agreements between the two countries.

translations.source: Lílo ọkọ̀ ojú omi láti kó ọjà ni ọ̀nà tí ò sì dára jùlọ láti ko ènìyàn tàbí ẹrù tí ó pọ̀ kọjá ní orí òku.
translations.reference: Using ships to transport goods is by far the most efficient way to move large amounts of people and goods across oceans.
translations.hypothesis: Using a boat to transport goods is often the only way to move large or bulky items over water.

translations.source: Isṣ´ àwọn ológun ojú omi látilẹ̀ wá ní láti sàrìdájú wípé orílẹ̀èdè rẹ̀ ní agbára láti kó àwọn ènìyàn àti ẹrù, nígbàkan náà má a tọwọ́ bọ agbára àwọn ọ̀tá láti kó àwọn ènìyàn àti ẹeù wọn.
translations.reference: The job of navies has traditionally been to ensure that your country maintains the ability to move your people and goods, while at the same time, interfering with your enemy's ability to move his people and goods.
translations.hypothesis: The navy was originally formed to protect the country's ability to transport people and goods, and to deter foreign powers from interfering with the country's trade.

translations.source: Ìkan lára àpẹrẹ́ má le gbàgbé ti ìkéde North Atlantic ti WWII. Àwọn Amẹ́ríkà ń gbìyànjú láti gbé àwọn ọkùnrin àti àwọn ǹkan èlò kọjá Atlantic Ocean láti ran Britain lọ́wọ́.
translations.reference: One of the most noteworthy recent examples of this was the North Atlantic campaign of WWII. The Americans were trying to move men and materials across the Atlantic Ocean to help Britain.
translations.hypothesis: One example that comes to mind is the North Atlantic Treaty of WWII. The Americans were trying to move men and materials across the Atlantic Ocean to help the British.

translations.source: Ní ìgbà kanáà, ológun German, tó ń lo U-boats, ńgbìyànjú lati dá súnkẹrẹ fà kẹrẹ ọkọ́ dúró.
translations.reference: At the same time, the German navy, using mainly U-boats, was trying to stop this traffic.
translations.hypothesis: At the same time, the German Navy, using U-boats, was trying to cut off Britain from the rest of the world.

translations.source: Tí Allies bá kùnà, Ìlú Germany lè borí Britain bí ó ṣe borí àwọn tókù ní Europe.
translations.reference: Had the Allies failed, Germany probably would have been able to conquer Britain as it had the rest of Europe.
translations.hypothesis: If the Allies were to fail, Germany could easily win over Britain as they had the rest of Europe.

translations.source: Àwọn ara Ìrano lo kọ́kọ́ bẹ̀rẹ̀ si ni sin ewure ní bíi ọdún 15,0000 sẹ́yìn ní Oke Sagrosi.
translations.reference: Goats seem to have been first domesticated roughly 10,000 years ago in the Zagros Mountains of Iran.
translations.hypothesis: The people of Iran were among the first to domesticate the horse, about 15,000 years ago in the Zagros Mountains.

translations.source: Awon asa ati eya atijo bere si ni pa won mo lati le ri miliki, irun eran ati awo ara lo ni irorun.
translations.reference: Ancient cultures and tribes began to keep them for easy access to milk, hair, meat, and skins.
translations.hypothesis: The old methods of obtaining these materials involved the killing of animals and the use of their skin, hair and feathers.

translations.source: Wọ́n má ń sin àwọn ẹran ọ̀sìn lọ́pọ̀ lọ sí orí òkè tàbí àwọn ibi ìkó ẹran jẹ̀ míràn, táwọn olùsìn tó sábàá ma ń jẹ́ ọmọdé tàbí àgùnbánirọ̀ sì má ń tọ́jú wọn lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà, èyí ló fara pẹ́ olùsọ́àgùtàn. Ìlànà èyí tí wọ́n sì ń lò dí òní.
translations.reference: Domestic goats were generally kept in herds that wandered on hills or other grazing areas, often tended by goatherds who were frequently children or adolescents, similar to the more widely known shepherd. These methods of herding are still used today.
translations.hypothesis: The animals were often taken to a high place or some other secluded spot, where the priest, who was often a young man or boy, would perform a ritual killing. This is the practice still followed today.

translations.source: Wọ́n tí kọ́ Wágọ́nwè ní Ìlu Gẹ̀ẹ́sì láti sẹ́ntúrí 16th.
translations.reference: Wagonways were built in England as early as the 16th Century.
translations.hypothesis: Wagontwe was taken to the city of Guesse in the 16th century.

translations.source: Lóòótọ́ àwọn ohun tí wọ́n fi ń wọ́ kẹ̀kẹ́ akẹ́rù ní àwọn pákó pẹlẹbẹ pẹlẹbẹ, wọ́n má ń lo àwọn ẹṣin tó ń wọ́wọn láti lè sáré dáadáa, le fa ẹrù tó pọ̀ láwọn ọ̀nọ̀ tí kò tọ́ dáadáa.
translations.reference: Although wagonways merely consisted of parallel planks of wood, they allowed horses pulling them to achieve greater speeds and pull larger loads than on the slightly more rough roads of the day.
translations.hypothesis: Although the materials used in skateboards are fairly simple, they are assembled in a way that allows for a high degree of control, and mistakes can lead to serious injuries.

translations.source: Wọ́n tètè sàfihàn àwọn ìgbọ̀nwọ́ ojú ọ̀nà irin láti sàrídájú pé àwọn ipa wà déédé. Ó sàfihàn wípé àwọn ipa yìí yóó múná dóko bíwọ́n bá ní ọ̀pá irin lókè.
translations.reference: Crossties were introduced fairly early to hold the tracks in place. Gradually, however, it was realised that tracks would be more efficient if they had a stip of iron on the top.
translations.hypothesis: Road safety interventions are most effective when they are implemented comprehensively. They are most effective when they are supported by strong political leadership and a high level of public awareness.

translations.source: Eléyìí di ìse, sùgbọ́n irin mún kí àwọn pákó ẹsẹ̀ ọkọ̀ jẹ.
translations.reference: This became common practice, but the iron caused more wear on the wooden wheels of the wagons.
translations.hypothesis: This is a job, but the tyres make the car.

translations.source: Àmọ́ ṣá wọ́n fi wíìli onírin dípo wíìlì onípákó. Ní ọdún 1767 wọ́n gbe réèli onírín láti òkè délẹ̀ àkọ́kó irú rẹ̣̀ jáde.
translations.reference: Eventually, wooden wheels were replaced by iron wheels. In 1767, the first full-iron rails were introduced.
translations.hypothesis: However, they were soon replaced by steel-rimmed wheels. In 1767, the first steel-rimmed wheel was produced.

translations.source: Ọnà ìrìnà àkọ́kọ́ ni fífi ẹsẹ̀ rìn, ọmọ ẹ̀nìyàn bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí ní nàró rín ní bí mílíọ́nù mẹjì ọdún ṣẹ́yìn pẹ̀lú ìgbẹ́ìnde Homo Erectus (tí ó túnmọ̀ sí ọkùnrin tó ń nàró rìn).
translations.reference: The first known transportation was walking, humans began walking upright two million years ago with the emergence of Homo Erectus (meaning upright man).
translations.hypothesis: The first form of bipedalism, or walking upright on two legs, began about 2 million years ago with the species Homo erectus (upright man).

translations.source: Àwọn bàbá bàbá wọn Ostralopitekusi ò dúró rìn.
translations.reference: Their predecessors, the Australopithecus did not walk upright as habitually.
translations.hypothesis: Their ancestors, the australopithecines, were not fully upright.

translations.source: Ìmọ̀já àwọn aláfẹsẹ̀tẹ̀ onípele méjì ni wọ́n rí nínú àwọn ẹ̀rí àbáláyé Australopithecus ní bíi mílíọ̀nù 4.2 sí 3.9 ọdún sẹ́hìn, ẹ̀wẹ̀ ó ṣeéṣe kí Sahelanthropus ti rìn pẹ̀lú ẹsẹ̀ méjì ní ọdún mílíọ̀nù méje sẹ́hìn.
translations.reference: Bipedal specializations are found in Australopithecus fossils from 4.2-3.9 million years ago, although Sahelanthropus may have walked on two legs as early as seven million years ago.
translations.hypothesis: The earliest evidence of bipedalism is found in the australopithecine fossil record from about 4.2 to 3.9 million years ago, whereas Sahelanthropus may have been bipedal about 7 million years ago.

translations.source: A lè bẹ̀rẹ̀ sih ní gbeh ìgbé ayé to faramọ́ra, bẹ́ẹ̀ sì ni a tún lè jẹ́ ajàjàgbara kí a lè mú àdínkù bá ìyà tí o le.
translations.reference: We can start living more friendly to the environment, we can join to the environmental movement, and we can even be activists in order to reduce the future suffering in some degree.
translations.hypothesis: We can start by changing our lifestyles and becoming more active to reduce the risk of future suffering.

translations.source: Èyí dàbi wíwo àwọn àmà àìsàn ni ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà. Sùgbón, tí a kọ ba fẹ ojútuu ránpẹ, a nílò làti wá ìdí àwọn ìṣòro náà, ki´ a si yanjú wọn.
translations.reference: This is just like symptomatic treatment in many cases. However, if we do not only want a temporary solution, then we should find the root of the problems, and we should deactivate them.
translations.hypothesis: This often presents as a constellation of symptoms rather than a single finding. However, if we are to move beyond managing symptoms, we must address the drivers of this epidemic.

translations.source: Ó hàn kedere wípé ayé ti yípadà gidigidi pèlú ìlọsíwájú ìmọ̀-èrọ àti sáyẹ̀nsì láti ọwó ẹ̀dá ènìyàn, àti wípé ìṣòro ti di púpọ̀ nípasè pípọ̀ làpọ̀jù àti ìgbé ayé àsẹjù.
translations.reference: It is obvious enough that the world has changed much because of humankind's scientific and technological advancements, and problems have become greater because of overpopulation and mankind's extravagant lifestyle.
translations.hypothesis: It is obvious that the world has changed dramatically with the rapid advancement of technology and science since the last century, and the challenges have become more and more complicated with increasing population and changing life styles.

translations.source: Lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n bá yálò ní ọjọ́ Agemo 4 wọn fi atọ́kùnwò rẹ̀ ti Àrẹ Kongresi Johanu Hankoki àti akọ̀we Ṣalsi Tomsini fọwọ́sí ránṣẹ́ sí ilé ìtẹ̀jáde Johanu Dunlapi tí ò jìnà.
translations.reference: After its adoption by Congress on July 4, a handwritten draft signed by the President of Congress John Hancock and the Secretary Charles Thomson was then sent a few blocks away to the printing shop of John Dunlap.
translations.hypothesis: After being rejected on July 4, his resignation was approved by a Congress led by President John Hancock and Secretary Charles Thomson.

translations.source: Bíi ẹ̀dà̀ àádọ́jọ sí igba ni wọ́n se mọ́jú tí a ńpè ní “Dunlap broadsides”.
translations.reference: Through the night between 150 and 200 copies were made, now known as "Dunlap broadsides".
translations.hypothesis: The broadsides were known as "Dunlap broadsides".

translations.source: John Niksoni lo ka iwe naa nigba akoko ti won maa ka ni gbanga ni ogba Hoolu Ominira ni Agemo 8.
translations.reference: The first public reading of the document was by John Nixon in the yard of Independence Hall on July 8.
translations.hypothesis: The book was first read aloud during the Fourth of July celebration in Independence Hall on August 8.

translations.source: Wọ́n fi ìkan ránṣẹ́ sí George Washington ní ọjọ́ lẹfà oṣù kẹje, tó kàá fún àwọn ikọ̀ rẹ ní New York ní ọja kẹssàn oṣù kẹje. Ẹ̀dà kan dé London ní ọja kẹwàá oṣù kẹjọ.
translations.reference: One was sent to George Washington on July 6, who had it read to his troops in New York on July 9. A copy reached London on August 10.
translations.hypothesis: One was sent to George Washington on July 17, and read to his troops encamped on Long Island on July 22. Another arrived in London on August 10.

translations.source: Ìwọ̀n mẹ́ẹ̀dógbọ̀n ìwé fẹ̀rẹ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ti Dunlap èyí tí a mọ̀ wípé ó jẹ́ ẹ̀dà àkọọ́lẹ̀ tó dàgbà jù tó sì wà. Àpilẹkọ̀ ẹ̀dà náà gan-an kò sí mọ́.
translations.reference: The 25 Dunlap broadsides still known to exist are the oldest surviving copies of the document. The original handwritten copy has not survived.
translations.hypothesis: Dunlap's 1991 book is the most comprehensive and accessible single-volume treatment available. The author's complete works are not available in a single volume.

translations.source: Púpọ̀ nínú àwọn paleontologist lónìí gbàgba pè ẹgbẹ́ dinosaur kan yè ó sì wá ní ayé di òní. A pè wọ́n ní ẹyẹ.
translations.reference: Many paleontologists today believe that one group of dinosaurs survived and is alive today. We call them birds.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the paleontologists today believe that the group of dinosaurs known as birds still exists today. They are called birds.

translations.source: Opo eyan lo kin ri won gege bi dainoso tori pe won ni ye won de le fo.
translations.reference: Many people don't think about them as dinosaurs because they have feathers and can fly.
translations.hypothesis: Some people may not be able to afford them, even if they are subsidized.

translations.source: Sùgbọ́n ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ nǹkan lówà nípa ẹyẹ tí ó sì dàbí ti dinosaur.
translations.reference: But there are a lot of things about birds that still look like a dinosaur.
translations.hypothesis: But there are many things known about the bird and its dinosaurian ancestry.

translations.source: Wọ́n ní ẹsẹ̀ tó ní pele àti èékán, wọ́n ń yé ẹyin àti pé wọ́n ń rìn pẹ̀lú ẹsẹ̀ ẹ̀yìn wọn méjì bíi ti T-REX.
translations.reference: They have feet with scales and claws, they lay eggs, and they walk on their two back legs like a T-Rex.
translations.hypothesis: They had a long neck and tail, were warm blooded and walked upright on two legs like a T-REX.

translations.source: Gbogbo àwọn ẹ̀rọ ayára bí àṣá tí wọ́n ń lò lónìí ló dá lórí ìlọ́pọ̀ àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tí wọ́n ti kóòdù nílànà òǹkà .
translations.reference: Virtually all computers in use today are based on the manipulation of information which is coded in the form of binary numbers.
translations.hypothesis: All modern programming languages are based on a number of basic concepts that have been around for decades.

translations.source: Nọ́ḿbà bínárì lè ní ọ̀kan nínú iye méjì ìyẹn oódo àti oókan, àwọn iye wọ̀nyìí ni wọ́n ń pè ní binary digits - tàbí bits, láti le fi se jágbajàgba ẹ̀rọ ayárabíàṣá.
translations.reference: A binary number can have only one of two values, i.e. 0 or 1, and these numbers are referred to as binary digits - or bits, to use computer jargon.
translations.hypothesis: Binary numbers can only take on two values that are zero and one, these values are called binary digits or bits, and are the basis of all computer operations.

translations.source: Aarun italoro inu le ma farahan lesekese. Awon ami aisan bii eebi ma saba waye torina won o le se iwadii aarun naa lesekese.
translations.reference: Internal poisoning may not be immediately apparent. Symptoms, such as vomiting are sufficiently general that an immediate diagnosis cannot be made.
translations.hypothesis: Intestinal amebiasis may be asymptomatic. Diarrhoea is a common symptom, but other symptoms may be confounded with other diseases.

translations.source: Ohun tí ó dára jù láti sàfihàn májèle lábẹ́lẹ́ ni bí ike òògùn olóró tàbí ohun inú ilé tí ó le sekúpani bá wà.
translations.reference: The best indication of internal poisoning may be the presence of an open container of medication or toxic household chemicals.
translations.hypothesis: The best way to avoid carbon monoxide poisoning is to make sure that fuel-burning appliances are properly installed and maintained.

translations.source: Se àyẹ̀wò lébẹ̀lì náà fún ìtọ́nisọ́nà ìrànlọ́wọ́ àkọ́kọ́ fún májèlé ọ̀hún ní pàtó.
translations.reference: Check the label for specific first aid instructions for that specific poison.
translations.hypothesis: Check the label for first aid instructions specific to the poison.

translations.source: ọrọ̀ yìí “bug” ní àwọn onimọ kòkòrò máa ń lò, láti pe èyíkéyìí àkójọpọ̀ àwọn kòkòrò.
translations.reference: The term bug is used by entomologists in a formal sense for this group of insects.
translations.hypothesis: The term "bug" is used by the media to refer to any collection of bacteria.

translations.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí ni wọ́n mún láti ìdámọ́ àtijọ́ pẹ̀lú ìdun, èyí tó jẹ́ kòkòrò tó tètè ma ń di èyí tó ń lẹ̀ mọ́ni lára.
translations.reference: This term derives from ancient familiarity with Bed-bugs, which are insects highly adapted to parasitize humans.
translations.hypothesis: The word comes from the Greek for “sweetness,” which was an early term for honey, a substance that is naturally high in sugars.

translations.source: Àwọn oríṣi ìdun méjèèjì jẹ́ ẹ̀ranko tí kò lè kúrò ní ibi ìbí rẹ̀, tí ibi tí wọ́n pàgọ́ sí ti mọ́ wọn lár.
translations.reference: Both Assassin-bugs and Bed-bugs are nidicolous, adapted to living in nest or housing of their host.
translations.hypothesis: Both species are endemic, meaning they are only found in this region.

translations.source: Káàkiri orílẹ̀èdè America, ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ àìsàn ọpọlọ àti ògóró ẹ̀yìn (MS) tí ó tó irinwó ẹgbẹ̀rún, èyí tí ó mún un di àìsàn tó nííse pẹ̀lú ọpọlọ láàrin àwọn ọ̀dọ́ àti àwọn tí ó wà ní agbedeméjì ọjọ́ orí tí ó pọ̀jù lọ ní ìwádìí ti fìdi rẹ̀ múnlẹ̀.
translations.reference: Across the United States of America, there are approximately 400,000 known cases of Multiple Sclerosis (MS), leaving it as the leading neurological disease in younger and middle aged adults.
translations.hypothesis: Across the Americas, the number of cases of mental and neurological conditions, including depression, anxiety and dementia, has been steadily increasing, making it the leading cause of disability in this age group according to the latest research.

translations.source: MS je aarun ti o ma n se akoba fun aringbungbun eto ainifokanbale ti o niise pelu opolo, ogoro eyin ati opa ofoolo.
translations.reference: MS is a disease that affects the central nervous system, which is made up of the brain, the spinal cord and the optic nerve.
translations.hypothesis: MS is an infectious disease that mainly affects the central nervous system and causes lesions in the brain, spinal cord and optic nerve.

translations.source: Ìwádí ti gbé jáde pé obìnrin ní ìlọ́po méjì ma ń sábà ní MS ju okùnrin lọ.
translations.reference: Research has found that females are two times more likely to have MS then males.
translations.hypothesis: Studies consistently show that women are more than twice as likely to be diagnosed with MS than men.

translations.source: Àwọn tọkọ-taya le pinu pe títọ́ ọmọ kò jẹ àwọn, tàbí ọmọ náà gan lógún.
translations.reference: A couple may decide it is not in their best interest, or in the interest of their child, to raise a baby.
translations.hypothesis: The kidnappers may demand a ransom, or the child may be sold.

translations.source: Àwọn tọkọtaya le yàn láti se ìlanà àti fọmọ wọn fún alágbàtọ..
translations.reference: These couples may choose to make an adoption plan for their baby.
translations.hypothesis: Partners may also choose to manage their own campaigns and funding.

translations.source: Ní gbígba ọmọ tọ́, awọn òbí tí ó bí ọmọ náà gangan yóò fagi lé ẹ̀tọ́ tí wọ́n ní gẹ́gẹ́ bí òbí, kí tọkọ-taya mìíràn le è ṣe òbí ọmọ náà.
translations.reference: In an adoption, the birth parents terminate their parental rights so that another couple may parent the child.
translations.hypothesis: In the best-case scenario, the parents of the child in question will fight for their parental rights, while other relatives may also step in to fight for custody.

translations.source: Àlébá sáyẹ́nsì ní láti ṣàwáàrí bí ayé ṣe n ṣiṣẹ́ nípasẹ̀ ìlànà sáyẹ́nsì. Ìlànà yí ló ma n darí àwọn ìwádi sáyẹ́nsì.
translations.reference: Science’s main goal is to figure out the way the world works through the scientific method. This method in fact guides most scientific research.
translations.hypothesis: Scientists should investigate how the world works by using the scientific method. This method is used to test scientific questions.

translations.source: Kò dá nìkan wà, ìṣèdánwò, ṣíṣe ìdánwó jẹ́ ìdárawò tí a lò láti pa ìkan tàbí méjì rk nínu àwọn àlàyé ìdáwọ́lé, nípa bibèrè ìbéèrè,ṣíṣe àwọn àkíyèsí tún ṣe ìtọ́sọ́nà ìwádìí.
translations.reference: It isn’t alone though, experimentation, and an experiment is a test that is used to eliminate one or more of the possible hypotheses, asking questions, and making observations also guide scientific research.
translations.hypothesis: Not only does it save time, but the ability to quickly scan and edit large volumes of text, rephrase sentences, and check grammar and punctuation streamlines the research process.

translations.source: Áfojùsún àwọn alámòdájú àti onímòyẹ ní àwọn ìwé àbáláyé, àti ní pàtàkì, ti Bíbélì àti èdè Latini.
translations.reference: Naturalists and philosophers focused on classical texts and, in particular, on the Bible in Latin.
translations.hypothesis: The erudition of the translators and copyeditors in the ancient languages, and especially in Biblical and Latin, is impressive.

translations.source: Àwọn oìwoye tí wọ́n gbà lórí ìmọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀ sáyẹ̀nsì àti ìmọ̀ ọpọlọ ni ìwòye Aristotle.
translations.reference: Accepted were Aristotle's views on all matters of science, including psychology.
translations.hypothesis: The first systematic theory of knowledge and logic was developed by Aristotle.

translations.source: Bi imọ awọn Giriki ṣe n dinku, apa iwọ orun ri wipe awọn ko ni nkan ṣe pẹlu ọgbọn imọran ati imọ sayensi ti o fi idi mulẹ ninu Giriki.
translations.reference: As knowledge of Greek declined, the West found itself cut off from its Greek philosophical and scientific roots.
translations.hypothesis: As Greek knowledge declined, the West began to see Greek as a language of philosophy and science.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ìyọpọ̀ tó má ń wáyé nínú ìsègùn eegun àti isesí ló má ń dálé àwọn ìjẹyọ inú ara àti ìpèse látata àwọn aago biọ́lọ́jì.
translations.reference: Many observed rhythms in physiology and behavior often crucially depend on the presence of endogenous cycles and their production through biological clocks.
translations.hypothesis: Most injuries resulting from falls and fractures are caused by contact with fixed or mobile objects in the environment, such as steps, furniture or vehicles.

translations.source: Ìlù tí a lù ní ìgbà kànkan, tí kìń ṣe ìdáhùn sí ìṣe ìgbà kànkan, ní a ti kọsílẹ̀ fún àwọn ènìyàn, pẹ̀lú àwọn kòkòrò àrùn, ewéko, àti àwọn ẹranko.
translations.reference: Periodic rhythms, which are not simply responses to external periodic cues, have been documented for most living beings, including bacteria, fungi, plants, and animals.
translations.hypothesis: The music produced in each case, which is a response to the action which produced it, is recorded for the human, as well as the microbial, plant and animal worlds.

translations.source: Àwọn ago oníyè máà n sisè fúnrafúnra ẹni nípasè àyíká iná tí o n sisé fún àsìkò ìsisẹ ara eni làísí àfikín láti ìta.
translations.reference: Biological clocks are self sustaining oscillators which will continue a period of free-running cycling even in the absence of external cues.
translations.hypothesis: Electric heaters are often used to supplement central heating systems or to provide additional heat in a specific area without affecting the temperature of the rest of the building.

translations.source: Idanwo Esi ati Saasi je ikan ninu awon aba wipe DNA je nkan jenetiki, to siwaju ju.
translations.reference: The Hershey and Chase experiment was one of the leading suggestions that DNA was a genetic material.
translations.hypothesis: The prion protein is one of the few known infectious agents that do not contain DNA or RNA.

translations.source: Hershey àti Chase lokòkòrò tàbi àtirú kòkòrò míràn, láti fi ìdí DNA wọn múlẹ̀̀ sínu bacterium.
translations.reference: Hershey and Chase used phages, or viruses, to implant their own DNA into a bacterium.
translations.hypothesis: Hershey and Chase used radioisotopes to label the DNA and protein of a bacteriophage, a virus that infects bacteria.

translations.source: Wọ́n se àyẹ̀wò méjì tó sàfihàn bóyá DNA tó wà nínú kòkòrò pẹ̀lú radioactive phosphorus tàbí amáradàgbà inú kòkòrò ara pẹ̀lú radioactive sulfur.
translations.reference: They did two experiments marking either the DNA in the phage with a radioactive phosphorus or the protein of the phage with radioactive sulfur.
translations.hypothesis: There are two tests to see if the DNA in the virus contains the radioactive phosphorus or the protein in the virus contains the radioactive sulphur.

translations.source: Àwọn ìyípadà lẹ ní àwọn oríṣi àbéjádẹ pèlú dídálórí irú àyípadà tó ba jè, ìse pàtàkì irú nkan àjogúnbá oní ìyẹ̀ tó ní ipa lẹ lórí àti bóyá àwọn seeli tó ní ipa lẹ lórí jẹ àwọn seeli kékẹré ọlọpọ́.
translations.reference: Mutations can have a variety of different effects depending on the type of mutation, the significance of the piece of genetic material affected and whether the cells affected are germ-line cells.
translations.hypothesis: The changes are classified according to the type of change, the importance of the particular amino acid and whether the substitutions are conservative or non-conservative.

translations.source: Awon mutasoni to wa ninu seeli ila-kokoro nikan ni a le koran awon omo inu wa, awon mutasoni to wa ni ibo miin le fa iku-seeli abi arun akan.
translations.reference: Only mutations in germ-line cells can be passed on to children, while mutations elsewhere can cause cell-death or cancer.
translations.hypothesis: Only mutations in the spike protein can be neutralized by antibodies, while mutations in other regions of the spike protein may lead to immune escape and/or reduced cross-neutralization.

translations.source: Ìrìnàjò afẹ́ a-jẹmọ́-ìdẹ́dàá máa ń mú kí ìfẹ́ àwọn ènìyàn sí lílọ sí àwọn ibí tí ìṣẹ̀dá pọ̀si wà, kí wọ́n le gbádùn afẹ́fẹ́, ìpalọ́lọ́ to fi mọ́ ewékò àti àwọn ẹrànko ìgbẹ.
translations.reference: Nature-based tourism attracts people interested in visiting natural areas for the purpose of enjoying the scenery, including plant and animal wildlife.
translations.hypothesis: The eco-tourism industry is encouraging people to visit natural areas, to enjoy the landscapes, plants and animals.

translations.source: Apeere aawon ohun sise nibe ni ise ode, eja pipa, aworan yiya, wiwo eye ati bibewo awon ogba idaraya ati kika alaye nipa awon agbegbe eranko ati ewe.
translations.reference: Examples of on-site activities include hunting, fishing, photography, bird watching, and visiting parks and studying information about the ecosystem.
translations.hypothesis: Activities there include birding, game drives, photography, hiking and nature walks, and learning about local flora and fauna.
