translations.source: Àpẹẹrẹ síṣe àbèwọ, yíya awòrán, àti kíkọ́ nípa àwọn ìnànkí ní Borneo.
translations.reference: An example is visiting, photographing, and learning about organgatuangs in Borneo.
translations.hypothesis: Sample activities include: guided nature walks, bird watching, photography, and learning about the rainforest.

translations.source: Ni araaro, awon eniyan ma n fi ilu kereje sile pelu oko lati lo si ibi ise, won a si ma pade awon osise yoku ti won n lo se ise nilu ti awon ti kuro.
translations.reference: Every morning, people leave small country towns in cars to go their workplace and are passed by others whose work destination is the place they have just left.
translations.hypothesis: In general, people used to ride their bikes to work, and they would meet up with other workers who had come from farther away.

translations.source: Nínú ọkọ̀ akérò aláràọ̀tọ̀, gbogbo ènìyàn nì ó lọ́pọ̀ àti ìgbárùkùtì, ìlànà ìrìnlọrìnbọ̀ tó dá l´rí àwọn ọkọ̀ aláàdáni.
translations.reference: In this dynamic transport shuttle everyone is somehow connected with, and supporting, a transport system based on private cars.
translations.hypothesis: In a typical private vehicle, there are more passengers and less space, a formula for disaster when compared to personal vehicles.

translations.source: Ìmọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀ sáyẹ̀nsì ti se àfihàn báyìí wípé ọrọ̀ ajé kábọ̀nù tí mún àyípadà bá ibùgbé láti ọ̀kan nínú àwọn ìpínlè rẹ̀ tó dúróo re èyí tó ti ń sàtìlẹyìn fún ìdàgbàsókè ọmọnìyàn láti bí i mílíọ̀nù méjì ọdún sẹ́yìn.
translations.reference: Science now indicates that this massive carbon economy has dislodged the biosphere from one of its stable states that has supported human evolution for the past two million years.
translations.hypothesis: Scientific consensus is that the economic benefits of climate change to some regions outweigh the damages in the short to medium term, which encourages further emissions despite the long-term consequences.

translations.source: Gbogbo àwọn èèyàn ló kópá láwùjọ tí wọ́n tún lo ìlànà ìrìnkèrindò. Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn èèyàn ló ń sàríwísí ìlànà ìrìnlọrìnbọ̀.
translations.reference: Everyone participates in society and uses transportation systems. Almost everyone complains about transportation systems.
translations.hypothesis: All people in the community are involved and use the same referral mechanism. The majority of people use the formal sector.

translations.source: Láwọn orílẹ̀èdè tó ti gògè, kò wọ́pọ̀ láti gbọ́ pé wọ́n ń se àríwísí nípa ìpéye omi tàbí pé afára já lulẹ̀.
translations.reference: In developed countries you seldom hear similar levels of complaints about water quality or bridges falling down.
translations.hypothesis: In drought-stricken countries, it is common to hear of water restrictions or even bans on car washing.

translations.source: Kílódé tó jẹ́ pé esun pipo ma n kan fún étò ìrìn àjò, kílódé to jẹ́ wípé wọ ma n pòfo lójojumo? Àb àwọn enjinia o mọ̀Ṣẹ́ ni àbi nkan miin pataki wa níbẹ̀?
translations.reference: Why do transportation systems engender such complaints, why do they fail on a daily basis? Are transportation engineers just incompetent? Or is something more fundamental going on?
translations.hypothesis: How many of you have ever missed a train because of a signal failure? How many of you have ever been late for work because of a signal failure? Are any of you married to a signal engineer?

translations.source: Lílọ-bíbọ̀ ìrìnnà ní ìwádìí ìrìnkèrindò àwọn awakọ kọ̀ọ̀kan àti ipò òkàn kan sí òmíràn ní agbẹdẹ méjì pélù ìbásẹpọ̀ tí wọn ní sí ara wọn.
translations.reference: Traffic Flow is the study of the movement of individual drivers and vehicles between two points and the interactions they make with one another.
translations.hypothesis: Ride-hailing apps facilitate the connection between riders and drivers through a two-way matching system based on their proximity to each other.

translations.source: Ó seniláànú wípé, kíkọ nípa lílọ bíbọ̀ ọkọ̀ nira nítori ìhùwàsí awakọ̀ kò se é sọ sílẹ̀ pẹ̀lú ìdájú ìdá ọgọ́rùn ún.
translations.reference: Unfortunately, studying traffic flow is difficult because driver behavior cannot be predicted with one-hundred percent certainty.
translations.hypothesis: Unfortunately, driving in the country is difficult because the drivers' attitude is unpredictable by 90%.

translations.source: Ó dára wípé àwọn awakọ̀ ma ń ṣọ́ ìwà wù láàrin ìwọ̀n tó ní ìbámú ; nítorí ìdí èyí, ojú pópó ma ń wà ní ìbámu tí ó tọ́ tí a lefi ìṣirò rọ́pò.
translations.reference: Fortunately, drivers tend to behave within a reasonably consistent range; thus, traffic streams tend to have some reasonable consistency and can be roughly represented mathematically.
translations.hypothesis: It is nice that drivers generally behave well in the presence of a dashcam; for this reason, roads are generally in good order and accidents are relatively rare.

translations.source: Láti tubọ̀ ṣe àfihàn suńkẹrẹ-fàkẹrẹ, wọ́n ṣe àgbékalẹ̀ ìbáṣepọ̀ láàáriń (1) ìsàn (2) ìlóòrin (3) ìsáre.
translations.reference: To better represent traffic flow, relationships have been established between the three main characteristics: (1) flow, (2) density, and (3) velocity.
translations.hypothesis: To better understand the multifaceted nature of this phenomenon, it is helpful to consider the connections between (1) music, (2) dance, and (3) storytelling.

translations.source: Àwọn ìbásòpọ̀ wọ́nyí ma ń gbìyànjú fún ètò ṣíṣe, àrà àkànṣe àrà, àti ìlò ohun èlò ojú ọ̀nà.
translations.reference: These relationships help in planning, design, and operations of roadway facilities.
translations.hypothesis: These networks facilitate policy coordination, technical assistance, and knowledge sharing.

translations.source: Kòkòrò jẹ́ ẹranko àkọ́kọ́ láti gba atẹ́gun. Ipa fífò wọn rànwọ́nlọ́wọ́ láti dojú ìjà kọ àwọn ọ̀tà wọn kí wọ́n sì wá óúnjẹ àti láti bá arawọn sùn dáradára.
translations.reference: Insects were the first animals to take to the air. Their ability to fly helped them evade enemies more easily and find food and mates more efficiently.
translations.hypothesis: The tick is the first host and the bacteria are transmitted to the next host during feeding. The tick's saliva helps the bacteria invade the new host and multiply.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn kòkòrò ní àǹfàní láti ká ìyẹ́ apá won mọ́ ara.
translations.reference: Most insects have the advantage of being able to fold their wings back along the body.
translations.hypothesis: Many bacteria are capable of breaking down hydrocarbons.

translations.source: Eyi ma n fun won ni asayan pupo ibi ti won le ti sa pamo fun eranko to fe pa won je.
translations.reference: This gives them a wider range of small places to hide from predators.
translations.hypothesis: This often gives them more options for where they can store their crypto assets.

translations.source: Lónìí, kòkòrò kan ṣoṣo, tí kò lè ká ìyẹ́ rẹ̀ papọ̀ ni kòkòrò tí a mọ̀ sí dragoni àti Mayflie.
translations.reference: Today, the only insects that cannot fold back their wings are dragon flies and mayflies.
translations.hypothesis: Today, only one species remains that is capable of producing this material, the dragonfly and mayfly.

translations.source: Egberun odun seyin, okunrin ti a n pe ni Aristakusu wipe Ona Orun man yi orun ka.
translations.reference: Thousands of years ago, a man called Aristarchus said that the Solar System moved around the Sun.
translations.hypothesis: About 3000 years ago, a man called Aristarchus suggested that the sun was a star.

translations.source: Àwọn ẹ̀nìyàn kan rò pé ó jàre, ṣùgbọ́n ọ̀pọ̀ ènìyàn gbàgbọ́ nínú òdì kejì; pé ní ṣe niSolar System n yi yípo ayé, tí ó fi mọ́ òòrùn (ati àwọn ìràwọ̀ mìíràn.
translations.reference: Some people thought he was right but many people believed the opposite; that the Solar System moved around the Earth, including the Sun (and even the other stars).
translations.hypothesis: Some people think it's boring, but most people believe the second half of the show is the best part, which includes the recreation of the solar system, complete with planets and moons.

translations.source: Ẹ̀yí mú ọpọlọ wá, torí wípé kò dà bí ẹni wípé pé ayé ń yí, àbí ó dàábẹ̀?
translations.reference: This seems sensible, because the Earth doesn't feel as if it's moving, does it?
translations.hypothesis: This makes sense, because it is not obvious that the world is changing, or is it?

translations.source: Odò Amazon jé odè to gùn jù tósì tóbi jù lórílè áyè. O gba ìlọ́po mẹjọ omi tí odò kejì tó tóbijù lọ gbà.
translations.reference: The Amazon River is the second longest and the biggest river on Earth. It carries more than 8 times as much water as the second biggest river.
translations.hypothesis: The Amazon River is the largest river by volume and the second longest in the world. It discharges more water than any other river in the world.

translations.source: Amasoni ni odò tó fẹ̀ jùlọ ní ile ayé, nígbàmín ó ma n fẹ̀ tò maili mẹ́fà.
translations.reference: The Amazon is also the widest river on Earth, at times six miles wide.
translations.hypothesis: The Amazon is the largest river in the world, and in places it is six miles wide.

translations.source: Ìdá ogún omi tó dà sílẹ̀ nínú àwọn odò ayé sínú òkun wá láti Amazon.
translations.reference: A full 20 percent of the water that pours out of the planet's rivers into the oceans comes from the Amazon.
translations.hypothesis: Twenty percent of the fresh water on Earth comes from the Amazon.

translations.source: Odò Amazon gangan jẹ́ ẹgbẹ̀rún mẹ́fà ó lé ọ̀rìn lé lọ́ọ̀dúnrún ó lè méje kìlómítà (ẹgbẹ̀rún mẹ́rin ó dín ogún máìlì). Ó gba omi láti ẹgbẹ̀lẹ́gbẹ̀ odò kéèké.
translations.reference: The main Amazon River is 6,387 km (3,980 miles). It collects water from thousands of smaller rivers.
translations.hypothesis: The Amazon River is about 6,400 kilometers (4,000 miles) long. It is fed by thousands of tributaries.

translations.source: Lóòótọ̀ àwọn ilé pírámìdì toní òkúta wà títí di òpin ìjọba àkúwórí. píràmìdì Gasa kò jura wọn lọ níye àti ní ìdára ìjìnlẹ̀ kíkọ́ wọn.
translations.reference: Although pyramid-building in stone continued until the end of the Old Kingdom, the pyramids of Giza were never surpassed in their size and the technical excellence of their construction.
translations.hypothesis: The only remaining wonder of the ancient world, the Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest and largest of the three pyramids in the Giza pyramid complex.

translations.source: Ijoba titun Ijipti Atijo kun fun iyalenu fun ohun arabara a=ti asaaju won ti o to bii egberun odun nigba naa.
translations.reference: New Kingdom ancient Egyptians marvelled at their predecessors monuments, which were then well over a thousand year old.
translations.hypothesis: The ancient Egyptian government was a theocracy, ruled by a king who was considered to be a god.

translations.hypothesis: The Al system has been applied in finance, security, transportation, and the military, among other video surveillance applications in many countries.

translations.source: Ìrìnàjò ìwádìí jẹ́ pàtàkì nínú iṣẹ́ yàrá ìkàwé. Lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà olùkọ́ ma ń nífẹ̀ẹ́ láti kó àwọn akẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ rẹ̀ lọ sáwọn ibùdó tí wíwọ ọkọ̀ kò ní jẹ́ àláálẹ̀.
translations.reference: Field trips are a large part of any classroom. Quite often a teacher would love to take her students places to which a bus trip is not an option.
translations.hypothesis: Field research is an important part of the curriculum. Often teachers will take their students to places that are not easily accessible by car.

translations.source: Ọgbọ́n àmúṣe pèsè ọ̀nà àbáyọ pẹlú àwọn ìrìn àjo lọ́ sí pápá. Àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ lè wo àwọn iṣẹ́ ọnà tí ó wà ní ilé ìkó àwọn iṣẹ́ ọnà sí, lọ wo ilé iṣẹ́ ẹja ní ọ̀ṣọ́ sí, tàbí kí wọ́n máa wo àwọn iṣẹ́ ọnà tí ó rẹwà bí wọ́n ṣe wà ní kílásì wọn.
translations.reference: Technology offers the solution with virtual field trips. Students can look at museum artifacts, visit an aquarium, or admire beautiful art while sitting with their class.
translations.hypothesis: The action pedagogy provided a solution with its emphasis on projects leading to real life applications. Students could now visit the library for project works, visit a fish factory in the next town, or watch a documentary on the topic in class.

translations.source: Tí èyan bá pín ìrìn àjò ní orí amóhùnmáwòrán ó jẹ́ ọ̀nà tó dára láti lò fi pín àwọn iriri èyàn pẹ̀lú àkẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ ọjọ́ iwájú.
translations.reference: Sharing a field trip virtually is also a great way to reflect a on a trip and share experiences with future classes.
translations.hypothesis: If you share your journey on social media, it is a great way to inspire others to take control of their future.

translations.source: Fun apẹẹrẹ, ni ọdun kọọkan, awọn akẹkọ lati Ile Iwe Beneti ni Karolina Ariwa, ṣe akanse oju iwe ayelujara nipa irin ajo wọn si olu-ilu, lọdọdun, wọn ma n tun oju-iwe naa ko ṣugbọn won ma n pa awon ti tẹlẹ mọ lati fi ṣe iwe apamowo.
translations.reference: For example, each year students from Bennet School in North Carolina design a website about their trip to the State Capital, each year the website gets remodeled, but old versions are kept online to serve as a scrapbook.
translations.hypothesis: For example, each year students from Bennett College in North Carolina create a website about their spring break trip to Atlanta, Georgia, and then update the site throughout the year with new information and advertisements.

translations.source: Ìtàkùn Blog náà lè se ìrànwọ́ fún ìkọ̀wé àwọn akẹ́ẹ̀kọ́. Nígbàtí àwọn akẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìrírí ìtàkùn blog ti wọn pẹ̀lú ìlo èdè àti àkọtọ́ tó wọ́, wíwà nílẹ̀ àwọn èrò ma ń yí èyí padà.
translations.reference: Blogs can also help improve student writing. While students often begin their blog experience with sloppy grammar and spelling, the presence of an audience generally changes that.
translations.hypothesis: The blogging platform can help improve students' writing skills. When students begin their blogging journey with a simple language and short paragraphs, the consistency in posting helps them improve over time.

translations.source: Nigba ti o ti je pe awon akeeko mma n tako ju, onkowe blogi ma n sa gbogbo agbara lati dara si ki o baa le yera fun itako.
translations.reference: Since students are often the most critical audience, the blog writer begins to strive to improve writing to avoid criticism.
translations.hypothesis: While the competition is expected to be fierce, the blogger said he'll do his best to win.

translations.source: Blogging, “ti kàn án nípá fáwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ láti fẹ ní ìmọ̀ àti òye kíkún nípa ayé tó yí wọn ká” èròǹgbà àti ìlò láti wo ṣàkun ohun tí àwọn olùgbọ́ ń fẹ́ kí wọn sì ṣe e fún wọn ni ó mú kí àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ gbọ́n nínú gbọ́n ní ìlta, tí wọ́n si ń ṣe ohun tó móríyá. (Toto, 2004)
translations.reference: Also blogging "forces students to become more savvy about the world around them." The need to feed the interest of the audience inspires students to be clever and interesting (Toto, 2004).
translations.hypothesis: Blogging, "has enabled students to want to know more and to gain a deeper understanding of the world around them" and the use of blogs to address the needs and interests of the students made the learning more meaningful and enjoyable. (Toto, 2004)

translations.source: Búlọ́gìn jẹ́ ohun èlò tó ń ṣe ìwúrí fún àjọṣepọ̀, tí ó sì ń ṣe ìrànwọ́ fún àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ láti mú ìmọ̀ ẹ̀kọ́ kọjá ilé ẹ̀kọ́.
translations.reference: Blogging is a tool that inspires collaboration, and encourages students to extend learning well beyond the traditional school day.
translations.hypothesis: Blogs are a great way to build a community and help learners take their learning beyond the four walls of the classroom.

translations.source: Lílo ìtàkùn Blog ní ọ̀nà tí ó tọ́ “lè ró àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ní agbára láti di ẹni tó ń wo nǹkan ní àwòfín, tí yóò si lè ṣe ọ̀rínkíniwin rẹ̀; látàrí fífèsì tí ó tọ̀nà sí àwọn nǹkan tí ẹnìyàn ń rí lórí ayélujara, akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ lè sọ nípa ohun tí wọn rò ní pa elọmìíran tàbí sọ èròwọn nípa nǹkan kí nǹkan (Oravec, 2002).
translations.reference: Appropriate use of blogs "can empower students to become more analytical and critical; through actively responding to Internet materials, students can define their positions in the context of others' writings as well as outline their own perspectives on particular issues (Oravec, 2002).
translations.hypothesis: The use of blogs is a great way to encourage students to become active consumers of information, as well as producers of knowledge; by providing a platform for students to voice their opinions on topics of interest to them, they are able to develop their opinions on a topic (Oravec, 2002).

translations.source: Ottawa je ilu ti o re wa ni Canada, olu-ilu elede meji ti o kun fun gbongan isafihan ise owo ati ile iselojo pa mo si ti o n se afihan ana ati oni Canada.
translations.reference: Ottawa is Canada's charming, bilingual capital and features an array of art galleries and museums that showcase Canada's past and present.
translations.hypothesis: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, the second-largest city in the province of Ontario, and the fourth-largest city in Canada.

translations.source: Ní jìnnà jìnnà gúúsù ni Niagra Falls àti ní àríwá ni ilé sáwọn ẹwà àtọrun wá fún Muskoka àti rékọjá rẹ̀.
translations.reference: Farther south is Niagara Falls and the north is home to the untapped natural beauty of the Muskoka and beyond.
translations.hypothesis: Niagara Falls is a world famous attraction to the south and to the north are the many beautiful lakes of Muskoka and the surrounding area.

translations.source: Ohun tí gbogbo èyí ń tọ́ka sí ni pé Ontario ni ohun tí gbogbo ènìyàn ará ìlú mìíràn rí pé Canada n.
translations.reference: All these things and more highlight Ontario as what is considered quintessentially Canadian by outsiders.
translations.hypothesis: This is what makes Ontario what all other provinces in Canada see as the Canadian dream.

translations.source: Àwọn agbègbè tó tóbí nínu àríwá ní àwọn ènìyàn tó pọ̀ tí àwọn kan sí wà ní inú igbó tí kò ṣe gbé inú rẹ́.
translations.reference: Large areas further north are quite sparsely populated and some is nearly uninhabited wilderness.
translations.hypothesis: The largest communities in the north are inhabited by people who live in the forest and are not sedentary.

translations.source: Fun afiwe ti o ma ya awon èèyàn pupo lenu:iye awon ara Ilu Amerika tio wa lati ile Afirika, po ju awon omo bibi ilu Canada lọ.
translations.reference: For a comparison of population that surprises many: There are more African Americans living in the US than there are Canadian citizens.
translations.hypothesis: For the sake of comparison: the average cost of living in the US is higher than in Canada.

translations.source: Àwọn erekùsù ìlà oòrùn adúláwọ̀ wà ní òkun India ní ìlà oòrùn adúláwọ̀.
translations.reference: The East African Islands are in the Indian Ocean off the eastern coast of Africa.
translations.hypothesis: The islands of the Indian Ocean are located in the western Indian Ocean.

translations.source: Ní ti àwọ̀n ẹranko, Madagáskà ló tóbi jù lo tó sì jẹ́ kọ́ntínẹ́ntì tí ó dá wà fún ara rẹ̀.
translations.reference: Madagascar is by far the biggest, and a continent on its own when it comes to wildlife.
translations.hypothesis: In terms of fauna, Madagascar is unique and the island continent is home to a number of endemic species.

translations.source: Ilù olómìnira ní púpọ̀ nínú àwọn erekusu kékèké tàbí kí wọ́n níṣe pẹ̀lú ilẹ̀ Faranse, tí a tún mọ̀ wọ́n gẹ́gẹ́ bí risọ́tì etí òkun onígbádùn.
translations.reference: Most of the smaller islands are independent nations, or associated with France, and known as luxury beach resorts.
translations.hypothesis: Independent nations have many small dishes or plates, often with French names, that are known generically as hors d'oeuvres.

translations.source: Àwọn ara Arabù kọ́kọ́ mú ẹ̀sìn ìsláàmi si ilẹ̀wọ́n dẹ̀ gbagbo gidi ni Komoros ati Mayoneeti.
translations.reference: The Arabs also brought Islam to the lands, and it took in a big way in the Comoros and Mayotte.
translations.hypothesis: Islam first came to the islands with Arab traders in the Comoros and Mayotte.

translations.source: Ìmúnisìn àti ipa àwọn ilẹ̀ Europe bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní sẹ́ńtùrì karùndínlógún, níbi ilẹ̀ Portuga se rin ìlú Vasco da Gama tí wọ́n rí ní Cape Route káàkiri láti Europe lọ sí India.
translations.reference: European influence and colonialism began in the 15th century, as Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama found the Cape Route from Europe to India.
translations.hypothesis: European exploration and colonialism began in the 15th century, when the Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama found a sea route from Europe to India around the Cape of Good Hope.

translations.source: Ní àríwá, Sahel ni ó yí ẹkùn náà ká, omi òkun ní ó yí gúúsù àti ìwọ̀ oòrùn ká.
translations.reference: In the north the region is bounded by the Sahel, and in the south and west by the Atlantic Ocean.
translations.hypothesis: In the north, the region is limited by the Sahelian zone, and by the sea to the south and west.

translations.source: Àwọn obìnrin: wọ́n se àlàkalẹ̀ pé obìnrin kóbìnrin tó bá rìnrìnàjò sọ pé àwọ́n ti sègbáyàwó láìfi irú ipò ẹni bẹ́ẹ̀ se.
translations.reference: Women: It is recommended that any women travellers say that they are married, regardless of actual marital status.
translations.hypothesis: Women: It is said that women who travel alone are more likely to be sexually harassed than women who travel with a male companion.

translations.source: Ó serànwọ́ láti wọ òrùkọ pẹ̀lú (kó kàn má jẹ̀ẹ́ èyí tí ó jẹ́ olówó gọbọi.
translations.reference: It is helpful to also wear a ring (just not one that looks too expensive.
translations.hypothesis: It is easier to get admitted if you are a (not necessarily paying) member.

translations.source: Àwọn obìnrin gbudọ̀ mo pé àwọn ìyàtọ̀ àsà lẹ sẹ okùnfà nkan tó wọn ma kà sí ìyọlénu áti wípé kìí sẹ nkan ti kò wọ́pọ̀ làti ma tèlé, gbígbá lápá mú, àti bẹẹbẹẹ lọ.
translations.reference: Women should realize that cultural differences may result in what they would consider harassment and it is not uncommon to be followed, grabbed by the arm, etc.
translations.hypothesis: Women reported that cultural norms and gender roles influenced their likelihood to engage in physical activity, and that safety concerns, time constraints, and accessibility were additional barriers.

translations.source: Má gbọ̀n tó ba n kọ ọkùnrin mádẹ̀ bẹ̀rù láti gbe ara rẹ (Bí iyato àṣà bá wà àbi kò sí gaan kò túmọ̀ sípe ó dára).
translations.reference: Be firm in turning down men, and don't be afraid to stand your ground (cultural differences or not, it doesn't make it ok!).
translations.hypothesis: Don't be afraid to ask a male friend to help you (cultural differences notwithstanding).

translations.source: Apẹja Berber ní sẹ́ńtúrì kẹwàá ló sèdásílẹ̀ ìlú ìgbàlódé Casablanca, àwọn Phoenicians, Romans àtàwọn Merenidi ló sì lòó gẹ́gẹ́ bí i èbúté tí wọ́n pè ní Anfa.
translations.reference: The modern city of Casablanca was founded by Berber fishermen in the 10th century BCE, and was used by the Phoenicians, Romans, and the Merenids as a strategic port called Anfa.
translations.hypothesis: The Berber Almoravids founded the modern city of Casablanca in the 11th century, while the Phoenicians, Romans and Merenids used it as a port city they called Anfa.

translations.source: Àwọn ara ìlú Portugali parun wọn si tún sẹ àtúnkọ́ rè pélù orúkọ Casa Brance, kó tó di pé wọn tún sẹ àtúnkọ lẹ́yìn ìsẹ̀lẹ̀ ìwárìrì-ilè ní 1755.
translations.reference: The Portuguese destroyed it and rebuilt it under the name Casa Branca, only to abandon it after an earthquake in 1755.
translations.hypothesis: The original Portuguese name was changed to Casa Branca, which was later changed after the earthquake of 1755.

translations.source: Sootani tún ìlú náà kọ gẹ̀gẹ̀ bi Daru I-Badya, àwọn ọlọ́jà ara Speeni to dá ọjà sílè níbẹ̀, sì fún ún ní orùkọ Kasablanka.
translations.reference: The Moroccan sultan rebuilt the city as Daru l-Badya and it was given the name Casablanca by Spanish traders who established trading bases there.
translations.hypothesis: The Moors then took the city, calling it Dar al-Badya, the "Palace of Luxury", and Spanish merchants gave it the name Casablanca.

translations.source: Casablanca je okan lara awon ibi ti o kere ni ife lati raja ni gbogbo orile ede Morocco.
translations.reference: Casablanca is one of the least interesting places to shop in all of Morocco.
translations.hypothesis: Casablanca is one of the least interesting cities in Morocco.

translations.source: Ní àyíká Medina àtijọ́, ó rọrùn láti rí àwọn ibi tí wọ́n ti ń ta àwọn ọjà ìbílẹ̀, gẹgé bi tangines, àmọkòkò. awọ hookah, àwọn onírúurú òdòdó, àmó, gbogbo rẹ̀ jẹ́ fún àwọn arìrìn-àjò..
translations.reference: Around the old Medina it's easy to find places selling traditional Moroccan goods, such as tagines, pottery, leather goods, hookahs, and a whole spectrum of geegaws, but it's all for the tourists.
translations.hypothesis: In the historic Medina, it is easy to find shops selling traditional goods, such as tagines, babouches, hookah pipes, and various spices, but most cater to tourists.

translations.source: Goma jẹ́ ìlú ìrìn ajo nínú Olominira Kongo ní etí apá ìlà orùn lẹ́gbẹ́ Ruwanda.
translations.reference: Goma is a tourist city of the Democratic Republic of Congo in the extreme east near Rwanda.
translations.hypothesis: Goma is a city in eastern Congo, near the border with Rwanda.

translations.source: Ni 2002 Goma parun nitori lafa folkeno Nyiragongo tó ri púpọ̀ nínu títí ìlú pàpà jùlọ ilé ìjọ-ìlú.
translations.reference: In 2002 Goma was destroyed by lava from the Nyiragongo volcano which buried most of the town’s streets, particularly the town centre.
translations.hypothesis: In 2002, Goma was destroyed by lava from the nearby volcano, Mount Nyiragongo, which also killed many of the city's most prominent religious leaders.

translations.source: Nígbàtí Goma wà ní àbò, èyíkèyí àbẹ̀wò ní ìta Goma ní láti ní ìwádìí kíkún láti ní òye ìjà lemọ́lemọ́ ní agbègbè North Kivu.
translations.reference: While Goma is reasonably safe, any visits outside of Goma should be researched to understand the state of the fighting that persists in the North Kivu province.
translations.hypothesis: While Goma is secure, this incursion will have to be fully investigated to understand the escalation of violence in the North Kivu region.

translations.source: Ìlú náà ló tún jẹ́ ibùdó fún gígun ilẹ̀ ríru Nyiragongo pẹ̀lú ìtọpa Oríòkè Gorilla tó dínwó jùlọ nílẹ̀ Adúláwọ̀.
translations.reference: The city is also the base to climb the Nyiragongo volcano along with some of the cheapest Mountain Gorilla tracking in Africa.
translations.hypothesis: The city is also close to Nyiragongo, a volcano and the source of the world's highest concentration of wild gorillas.

translations.source: O lè lo boda boda (tákisí ọks alùpùpù) láti rìn kiri Goma. Iye rẹ̀ gangan ni 500 Congolese France fún ìrìn àjò kékeré náà.
translations.reference: You can use boda-boda (motorcycle taxi) to get around Goma. The normal (local) price is ~500 Congolese Francs for the short ride.
translations.hypothesis: You can use a boda-boda (motorbike taxi) to get out of Goma. The price for a short ride is around 500 Congolese Francs.

translations.source: Pelu pe o soro die lati de be, “Timbuktu” ti di apere ile alailegbe, jinjin.
translations.reference: Combined with its relative inaccessibility, "Timbuktu" has come to be used as a metaphor for exotic, distant lands.
translations.hypothesis: However, it is difficult to reach, and "Timbuktu" has become a byword for a remote place, far away.

translations.source: Lónìí ìlú òtòṣì ní Timbuktu, ṣùgbọ́n ó lorúkọ gẹ́gẹ́ bí ibi tó ma n fẹjúmọ́ àwọn onirinajo, ó sì ní pápá ọkọ̀ òfurufú.
translations.reference: Today, Timbuktu is an impoverished town, although its reputation makes it a tourist attraction, and it has an airport.
translations.hypothesis: The city of Timbuktu, now in Mali, was once a famed center of learning, and a stop on a trans-Saharan trade route.

translations.source: Wọ́n sàfikún rẹ̀ sára àwọn àkọọ́lẹ̀ ibùdó ohun ìní àgbáyé tó wà nínú ewu lọ́dún 1990 látàrí ìdúnkokò àwọn yẹ̀pẹ̀ asálẹ̀.
translations.reference: In 1990, it was added to the list of world heritage sites in danger, due to the threat of desert sands.
translations.hypothesis: It was added to the World Heritage List in 1990 due to the threat of avalanches.

translations.source: Ó jẹ́ ọ̀kan pàtàkì nínú àwọn ibi tí Henry Louis Gates’ PBS ti dúro nígbà tí ó ń wo àrà tí ó wà ní ilẹ̀ adúláwọ̀.
translations.reference: It was one of the major stops during Henry Louis Gates' PBS special Wonders of the African World.
translations.hypothesis: It was one of the stops on Henry Louis Gates' PBS tour of African roots.

translations.source: Ìlú náà yàtọ̀ gédégbé sí àwọn ìlú orílẹ̀èdè yòókù, nítoríwípé ó fara pẹ́ Áràbù ju àwọn adúláwọ̀ lọ.
translations.reference: The city is in stark contrast to the rest of the country's cities, because it has more of an Arabic flair than of an African.
translations.hypothesis: The country is very different from other Arab countries, because it is more European than Middle Eastern.

translations.source: Ibi ìgbafẹ́ tí a mọ̀ sí The Kruger National Park (KNP), wà ni àríwá-ìlà oòrùn ti orílẹ̀ èdè South Africa, tí ó sì lọ títí dé ààla Mozambique ní ìlà oòrun Zimbabwe ni àríwá, àti ni a gúsù ni odò Ọ̀nì wà.
translations.reference: The Kruger National Park (KNP) lies in the north-east of South Africa and runs along the border of Mozambique in the east, Zimbabwe in the north, and the southern border is the Crocodile River.
translations.hypothesis: The area known as Kruger National Park (KNP) is in the northeast of South Africa, bordering Mozambique in the east and Zimbabwe to the north, and is south of the Limpopo River.

translations.source: Àgbègbè ná a bo kìlómítà ẹgbẹ̀rún maọ́kàndínlógún ó lé ẹ̀dẹ́ẹ́gbẹ̀ta ó sì pín sí ̣ dọ́sìnì mẹ́rìnlá ọ̀tọ̀tọ̀, tí ìkọ̀kan ń sagbẹ́tẹrù oríṣìí erankó igbó.
translations.reference: The park covers 19,500 km² and is divided in 14 different ecozones, each supporting different wildlife.
translations.hypothesis: The region covers 16 million km2 and is divided into 44 countries, each with its own unique forest ecosystems.

translations.source: Ó jẹ ìkan lára [wọn ǹkan tó ma ń fa èrò wá sí South Africa ó sì jẹ́ àmì South African National Parks (SANParks).
translations.reference: It is one of the main attractions of South Africa and it is considered the flagship of South African National Parks (SANParks).
translations.hypothesis: It is one of the main reasons for visiting South Africa and is the flagship of the South African National Parks (SANParks).

translations.source: Bí gbogbo Ibi ìgbafẹ́ South Africa, owó ìlẹlé jẹ́̀fẹ́ àwọn oríṣiríṣi ǹkan ló sì wà níbẹ̀.
translations.reference: As with all South African National Parks, there are daily conservation and entry fees for the park.
translations.hypothesis: Like most of Southern Africa, South Africa has a temperate climate and is a land of many different landscapes.

translations.source: Ó tún le se àǹfànní fún ènìyàn láti ra Wild Card, èyí tí yíó pèsè ìwọlé sí bóyá àwọn ibùdó ní ilẹ̀ South Africa tàbí àwọn ibùdó àpapọ̀ tàwọn ènìyàn South Africa.
translations.reference: It may also be beneficial for one to buy a Wild Card, which provides entry to either selections of parks in South Africa or all of the South African National Parks.
translations.hypothesis: It also allows you to buy a Wild Card, which gives you access to both South African and international roaming packages.

translations.source: Irekusu Hon Kongi fun agbegbe Hon Kongi ni oruko re o de je ibi ti abewo pupo ma n dojuko ju.
translations.reference: Hong Kong Island gives the territory of Hong Kong its name and is the place that many tourists regard as the main focus.
translations.hypothesis: Hong Kong Island is the most common area for visitors to Hong Kong.

translations.source: Àwọn àfihàn àwọn ilé tó mún kí ojú òpó Hong Kong rẹwà ni ati fi wé àtẹ tí ó ń dán èyí tó tàn nípa omi Victoria Harbour tó wà nílẹ̀.
translations.reference: The parade of buildings that make the Hong Kong skyline has been likened to a glittering bar chart that is made apparent by the presence of the waters of Victoria Harbour.
translations.hypothesis: The light show is a series of beams of light that are projected from buildings along the Hong Kong harbour and reflected off the water of Victoria Harbour.

translations.source: Láti lè rí Hong Kong dáadáa, fi island sílẹ̀ kí o sì lọ sí ibi omi Kowlon.
translations.reference: To get the best views of Hong Kong, leave the island and head for the Kowloon waterfront opposite.
translations.hypothesis: To get a good view of Hong Kong, take a ride on the Star Ferry and cross over to Kowloon.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀ nínú ìdàgbàsókè tí ó wáyé ní ìgboro erékùsù Hong Kong ni ó wọ́pọ̀ láwọn ilẹ̀ tí ó wà ní àríwá etí òku.
translations.reference: The great majority of Hong Kong Island's urban development is densely packed on reclaimed land along the northern shore.
translations.hypothesis: Much of Hong Kong's development has been constrained by its hilly terrain.

translations.source: Ibi tí àwọn amúnisin mú gẹ́gẹ́ bi tiwọn ni èyí, fún ìdí èyí, tí o bá ń wa ẹ̀rí nípa ìmúnisìn ní àtijọ́, ibi yìí ni ó dára láti bẹ̀rẹ̀.
translations.reference: This is the place the British colonisers took as their own and so if you are looking for evidence of the territory's colonial past, this is a good place to start.
translations.hypothesis: This is the case for many of the earliest known vaccines, and so this is a good place to start if you are interested in the history of vaccination.

translations.source: Sundarbans jẹ́ agbègbè tí igi tí ń wù láàrìn omi tó tóbi jùlọ ní àgbáyé,tó sì gùn dé 80 km (50 mi) sínu Bangladeshi àti ibi tí kò sí omi ní Indian .
translations.reference: The Sundarbans are the largest littoral mangrove belt in the world, stretching 80 km (50 mi) into the Bangladeshi and Indian hinterland from the coast.
translations.hypothesis: The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in the world, and it extends about 80 km (50 mi) into the Bangladeshi and Indian territories.

translations.source: Wọ́n ti kéde Sundarbans gẹ́gẹ́ bí ti UNESCO World Heritage Site. Èyí tó jẹ́ara igbó tówà lẹ́kùn India ní wọn ń pè ní ibùdó àpapọ̀ Sundarbans.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The part of the forest within Indian territory is called Sundarbans National Park.
translations.hypothesis: The Sundarbans has been declared as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This is the largest contiguous mangrove forest in the world, known as the Sundarbans.

translations.source: Awon igbokiji kii se eera mangurufi nikan sa- lara re ni die ninu awon ite igbokiji nla to ku ti o figba kan bo gbogbo ile Gangetiki.
translations.reference: The forests aren't just mangrove swamps though — they include some of the last remaining stands of the mighty jungles which once covered the Gangetic plain.
translations.hypothesis: The glaciers are not just a source of water but also one of the main causes of the high number of floods in the high mountains.

translations.source: Ẹranko tí a mọ̀ sí Sundarbans gba agbègbè kan tí ó ó tó 3,850 km², ní èyí bí ìdámẹ́ta agbègbè náà jẹ́ kìkìdá omi/ir.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans cover an area of 3,850 km², of which about one-third is covered in water/marsh areas.
translations.hypothesis: The Sundarbans area covers approximately 3,850 km2, of which about a third is mangrove forest.

translations.source: Lati 1966, awon Sundabani ti je ile mimo eranko, won daba pe bii ekun Bengali Oloba 400 ati agbonrin alami 30,00 nlo wa ni agbegbe naa.
translations.reference: Since 1966 the Sundarbans have been a wildlife sanctuary, and it is estimated that there are now 400 Royal Bengal tigers and about 30,000 spotted deer in the area.
translations.hypothesis: Since 1966, the Sundarbans have been a designated tiger reserve, and today about 400 Bengal tigers and 30,000 spotted deer live there.

translations.source: Àwọn ọkọ̀ akérò kúrò ní ìbúdò wọ́n (ní ìkọjá odò) láti àárọ̀ títí di alẹ́,ṣùgbọ́n púpọ̀, pàápàá àwọn tó ń lọ sí ilà oòrùn àti Jakar/Bumthang ma ń kúrò láàrín ago mẹ́fà àbọ̀ àti ago méje àbọ̀.
translations.reference: Buses depart the inter-district bus station (across the river) throughout the day, though most, especially those heading to the east and Jakar/Bumthang leave between 06:30 and 07:30.
translations.hypothesis: The vehicles leave the camp (on the other side of the bridge) between 6:00 and 7:00 am, but most, especially those headed for the east and Jakar/Bumthang, leave between 6:30 and 7:30 am.

translations.source: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí àwọn ọkọ̀ akérò làti ẹkùn kan sí òmíràn se ma ń kún lọ́pọ́ ìgbà, ó dárá láti ra tíkẹ̀ẹ̀tì ní ọjọ́ díẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
translations.reference: As the inter-district buses are often full, it is advisable to purchase a ticket a few days in advance.
translations.hypothesis: As the boats are often full, it is best to book in advance.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀ agbè̀gbè ń jẹ àǹfàní ọkọ̀ akérò kékeré ilẹ̀ Japan, àwọn èyí tí o ní ìtura àti ìdúrósinsin.
translations.reference: Most districts are served by small Japanese Coaster Buses, which are comfortable and sturdy.
translations.hypothesis: Many communities are taking advantage of Japan's tiny, fuel-efficient cars.

translations.source: Takisi àjọgbàpọ̀ jẹ́ ọ̀nà tí ó yá tí ó sì rọrùn jùlọ láti rín ìrìn lọ sí àwọn ibi tí kò jìnnà, bíi Paro tí kò jú (Nu àádọ́jọ) lọ àt Punakha ní (Nu igba).
translations.reference: Shared taxis are a quick and comfortable means to travel to nearby places, such as Paro (Nu 150) and Punakha (Nu 200).
translations.hypothesis: The shared taxi is the fastest and easiest way to get to the less-visited places, such as Paro (1.5 hours from Thimphu) and Punakha (2 hours from Thimphu).

translations.source: Afara ori Odo Oyapock je afara odo ti a fi okun gbero. o la odo Oyapock ja o si je isopo awon ilu bi Oiapoque ni Brazil and Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock ni French Guiana.
translations.reference: The Oyapock River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge. It spans the Oyapock River to link the cities of Oiapoque in Brazil and Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock in French Guiana.
translations.hypothesis: The Oyapock River is a natural border river. The Oyapock River forms part of the border between French Guiana and Brazil, between the towns of Oiapoque in Brazil and Saint-Georges-de-l'Oyapock in French Guiana.

translations.source: Awon ile nla mejeji ga to 83 meters, o gun to 378 meters o de ni oju ona meji to fe to 3.50m.
translations.reference: The two towers rise to a height of 83 meters, it's 378 meters long and it has two lanes of 3.50 m wide.
translations.hypothesis: The two towers are 83 metres (272 ft) tall, with a combined 378 metres (1,240 ft) of spire and two skybridges up to 350 m (1,150 ft) above the ground.

translations.source: Gíga ìbú abẹ́ afárá jẹ́ bí i mítà márùndínlógún. Kíkọ́ rẹ̀ parí nínú oṣù kẹjọ ọdún 2011, kò sísílẹ̀ fún ìrìnlọrìnbọ̀ títí di oṣù kẹta ọdún 2017.
translations.reference: The vertical clearance under the bridge is 15 meters. Construction was completed in August 2011, it didn't open to traffic until March 2017.
translations.hypothesis: The height of the tower is 15 meters. Construction was completed in August 2011, but it wasn't open to the public until March 2017.

translations.source: Afára náà ni wọ́n ní yíò bẹ̀rẹ̀ iṣẹ́ nínú osù kẹsàn án ọdún 2017, nígbà ìrètí wà wípé kí ilé-iṣẹ́ asọbodè ilẹ̀ Brazil parí àwọn ẹnubode.
translations.reference: The bridge is scheduled to be fully operational in September 2017, when the Brazilian customs checkpoints are expected to be finished.
translations.hypothesis: The company was scheduled to start operations in October 2017, with the hope of ending the Brazilian postal service's monopoly.

translations.source: Àwọn ènìyàn Guarani ni wọ́n jẹ́ ènìyàn ìbílẹ̀ tó ń gbé ibi tó jẹ́ ìlà oòrùn Paraguay báyìí, wọ́n ń gbé bí i apwọn ọdẹ tí ó tún siṣẹ́ ohun ọ̀gbìn alárojẹ.
translations.reference: The Guaraní were the most significant indigenous group inhabiting what is now Eastern Paraguay, living as semi-nomadic hunters who also practised subsistence agriculture.
translations.hypothesis: The Guarani people are the original inhabitants of what is now eastern Paraguay, and they lived as nomadic hunter-gatherers.

translations.source: Ẹkun ti Chaco jẹ ile fun ọpọlọpọ ẹgbẹ awọn ẹya abinibi bi Guaycurú ati Payaguá, ti o jẹ iṣẹ ọdẹ ṣiṣe ati ẹja pipa ni won yan laayo.
translations.reference: The Chaco region was home to other groups of indigenous tribes such as the Guaycurú and Payaguá, who survived by hunting, gathering and fishing.
translations.hypothesis: The Gran Chaco is home to many indigenous groups such as the Guaycurú and Payaguá, whose traditional way of life is based on hunting and fishing.

translations.source: Ní sẹ́ntúrì kẹrìndínlógún, Paraguay tí wọ́n pè ní “Agbègbè Nlá tí Indíaì” ni wọ́n bií látàrí láti ìpàdé àwọn aṣẹ́gun ilẹ̀ Spain pẹ̀lú àwọn ęgbẹ́ ìbílẹ̀.
translations.reference: In the 16th century Paraguay, formerly called "The Giant Province of the Indies", was born as a result of the encounter of Spanish conquerors with the native indigenous groups.
translations.hypothesis: In the 18th century, Paraguay was known as "La Gran India" due to the Spanish conquerors' confusion with the indigenous groups.

translations.source: Àwọn ará Spain bẹ̀rẹ̀ àkòkò ìsèjọba amúnisìn èyí tó pẹ́ tó sẹ́ńtúrì mẹ́ta.
translations.reference: The Spaniards started the colonization period which lasted for three centuries.
translations.hypothesis: The Spanish began a three-century long colonial rule.

translations.source: Láti ipile Asensioni ní 1537, Paragueti gbìyànjú láti pa púpọ̀ nínú ìwà àti ìyàtọ̀ rẹ̀ mọ́.
translations.reference: Since the foundation of Asunción in 1537, Paraguay has managed to keep a lot of its indigenous character and identity.
translations.hypothesis: Since its founding in 1537, Paraguay has struggled to maintain its sovereignty and independence.

translations.source: A mọ ìlú Argentina nitorí wọ́n ní ẹgbẹ́ polo àti òṣèrè ní àgbáyé.
translations.reference: Argentina is well known for having one of the best polo teams and players in the world.
translations.hypothesis: Argentina is known for its world class polo and tango.

translations.source: Eré ìje tó tóbi jù lọ́dún ma wáyé nínú oṣù kejì ní pápá ìṣeré polo ní Las Can̂itas.
translations.reference: The largest tournament of the year takes place in December at the polo fields in Las Cañitas.
translations.hypothesis: The most important event of the year is the high-goal polo season, which takes place in the second half of the year at the La Canchita polo fields.

translations.source: Idije kekeeke ati opolopo ifigagagba ni o tun le je wiwo ni awon akoko ninu odun miran.
translations.reference: Smaller tournaments and matches can also be seen here at other times of the year.
translations.hypothesis: Smaller regattas and informal races are also held at other times of the year.

translations.source: Fún ìròyìn lórí eré ìje àti bi à ti ra ìwé ìwọlé fún ìdíje polo, lọ wo ẹgbẹ́ Argentina de Polo.
translations.reference: For news on tournaments and where to buy tickets for polo matches, check Asociacion Argentina de Polo.
translations.hypothesis: For more information on the games and how to get tickets to the polo matches, visit the Argentine Polo Team website.

translations.source: Owó Falklands ni pọ́ùn Falklandtí (FKP) èyí tí iye rẹ̀ jẹ́ ìkan pẹ̀lú iye pọ́ùn ilẹ̀ Britain (GBP).
translations.reference: The official Falklands currency is the Falkland pound (FKP) whose value is set equivalent to that of one British pound (GBP).
translations.hypothesis: The currency of the Falkland Islands is the Falkland Pound (FKP), which is equal in value to the British Pound (GBP).

translations.source: Ilé ìfowópamọ́sí tó wà ní erékùsù ní Stanley káàkiri ibi ìtajà ìwọ̀ oòrùn FIC nìkan ni o ti lè pààrọ̀ owó.
translations.reference: Money can be exchanged at the only bank in the islands which is located in Stanley across from the FIC West store.
translations.hypothesis: The only bank in the district, located in Stanley just off the FIC's eastern border, is where you can exchange currency.

translations.source: Ní gbogbo apa irekusu naa, wọ́n ma n gba Pọ́n ìlú Ọba pẹ̀lú ní ibi tí káàdì àwìn àti Dola Ìlú Amerika.
translations.reference: British pounds will generally be accepted anywhere in the islands and within Stanley credit cards and United States dollars are also often accepted.
translations.hypothesis: In most parts of the country, you can only use cash or local debit cards, but in tourist hotspots, credit and US dollar cards are often accepted.

translations.source: Wọn lẹ má gba káàdì àwìn ní àwọn ìrékùsù tó wa ní pípépe, àmọ wọn lẹ gba àwọn owó ìlú Ọba àti ìlú Amèrìká, kọ́kọ́ sẹ àyèwo pèlú àwọn to ni ibè làti mọ nkan tí wọn lẹ gba gẹ́gẹ́ bii ìlànà ìsanwó.
translations.reference: On the outlying islands credit cards will probably not be accepted, although British and United States currency may be taken; check with the owners in advance to determine what is an acceptable payment method.
translations.hypothesis: Credit cards are not widely accepted in the more remote areas, but US dollars and Euros are generally accepted in tourist areas, and it is a good idea to check with your hotel or airline what they will accept as payment.

translations.source: O fee je nkan ti o seese lati paro owo Falklandi nita awon irekusu naa, tori naa paro owo ki o to kuro ni awon irekusu naa.
translations.reference: It is nearly impossible to exchange Falklands currency outside of the islands, so exchange money prior to leaving the islands.
translations.hypothesis: It is easy to exchange Falkland Islands currency for goods in the islands, as the money is only valid there.

translations.source: Níbi ìlú Montevideo se jẹ́ ẹkùn gúúsù ìlà agbede ayé, ó má ń tutù láàkókò ìgbà òtútù ní ẹkùn àríwá àarin róbótó àti ìdàkejì.
translations.reference: Since Montevideo is south of the Equator, it is summer there when it's winter in the Northern Hemisphere and vice versa.
translations.hypothesis: In Montevideo, the southernmost capital city in the Southern Hemisphere, temperatures in the winter are mild compared to those in the northern hemisphere.

translations.source: Montevideo wà ní ilé olóoru; ní àwọn oṣù àkókò eèrùn, ìwọ̀n ooru tó má ń wọ́pọ̀ ni èyí tó ma ń ju +30°C lọ.
translations.reference: Montevideo is in the subtropics; in the summer months, temperatures above +30°C are common.
translations.hypothesis: Montevideo is subtropical; in summer, average temperatures are around +30 °C.

translations.source: Ìgbà òtútù le fẹ́ tutù alárúmọjẹ, àwọn ìwọ̀n òtútù ki sábà kẹ́rẹ́ sí dídì sùgbọ́n afẹ́fẹ́ áti ọ̀rìn nínú òtútù màa ǹ papọ̀ láti mú dàbí pẹ́ ó tutù ju bí èrọ ìgbóná tí se wọ̀n lọ.
translations.reference: The winter can be deceptively chilly: temperatures rarely go below freezing, but the wind and humidity combine to make it feel colder than what the thermometer says.
translations.hypothesis: Cold weather can feel much colder than the thermometer reading, because wind and moisture affect the rate at which heat is lost from the body.

translations.source: Kò sí àsìkò “òjò” àti “ẹ̀rùn” ní pàtó: òjò̀ a máa wáyé yípo ọdún ní ìgbàmìíràn.
translations.reference: There are no particular "rainy" and "dry" seasons: the amount of rain stays roughly the same throughout the year.
translations.hypothesis: There is no real "rainy season" and "dry season" in the tropics: it usually rains every day in the wet season.

translations.source: Lóòtọ́, ó ti mọ́ ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ẹranko tó wà nínú ààyè lára láti má a rí àwọn èèyàn, àwọn ohun abẹ̀mí inú igbó jẹ́ tigbó, tí kò si yẹ kí wọ́n má a fún wọn ní oúnjẹ́ tàbí dàwọn láàmùn.
translations.reference: Though many of the animals in the park are used to seeing humans, the wildlife is nonetheless wild and should not be fed or disturbed.
translations.hypothesis: In fact, most of the animals in the park are used to not seeing humans, and the forest animals are wild and should not be fed or approached.

translations.source: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí àwọn aláṣẹ ibùdó ṣe sọ, jẹ́ kí ó kéré tán ọgọ́rùn ún ọ̀pa ìwọ̀n wà láàárín àgbọ̀nrin àti ìkokò àti ìwọ̀n ọ̀pá márùndínlógún sí àwọn ẹranko ìgbẹ́ tí ó kù!
translations.reference: According to park authorities, stay at least 100 yards/meters away from bears and wolves and 25 yards/meters from all other wild animals!
translations.hypothesis: According to site authorities, at least 100 steps are needed to get from the bottom to the top, and 25 steps to the animal shelters!

translations.source: Ko si bi oju won se le rele to, bisoni, elki, moosi, esi ati gbogbo eranko nla le doju ko en.
translations.reference: No matter how docile they may look, bison, elk, moose, bears, and nearly all large animals can attack.
translations.hypothesis: No matter how thick the fur, bison, elk, moose, caribou and other large mammals can be seen through it.

translations.source: Ní ọdọdún, àwọn àlejo tó tó méjìlá ló ṣèṣe nítorí wọn kò fi àyè sílẹ̀ dáadáa. Àwọn eranko wọ́nyí tóbí, wọ́n sí le gan, wan sí léwu, nítorínà fún wọ́n ní àyè wọn.
translations.reference: Each year, dozens of visitors are injured because they didn't keep a proper distance. These animals are large, wild, and potentially dangerous, so give them their space.
translations.hypothesis: Every year, about 12 million visitors come to Yellowstone, and most of them stay in the park. These animals are large, and some are dangerous, so they are best viewed from a safe distance.

translations.source: NÍ àfikún, mọ̀ pé òórùn ma ń fa béárì àti àwọn ęranko inú igbó mìíràn, torínáà yàgò fún gbígbé tàbi síse àwọn oúnjẹ́ tí ó ní òrùn púpọ̀, jẹ́kí ibi ìpàgọ́ rẹ mọ́ tótó nígbàgbogbo.
translations.reference: In addition, be aware that odors attract bears and other wildlife, so avoid carrying or cooking odorous foods and keep a clean camp.
translations.hypothesis: In addition, I'm sure the sun will cause tension and other outdoor activities, such as sunbathing or eating outdoors, to be more enjoyable, making your gathering more pleasant.

translations.source: Apia ni ipinle agbara Samoa. Ilu naa wa ni irekusu Upolu, o de ni eyan 40,000 o din die.
translations.reference: Apia is the capital of Samoa. The town is on the island of Upolu and has a population of just under 40,000.
translations.hypothesis: Apia is the capital of Samoa. The town is located on the island of Upolu, and has a population of about 40,000 people.

translations.source: Wọ́n dá ìlú Apia sílẹ̀ ní àwọn ọdún 1850, ó sì ti jẹ̀ olú ìlú Samoa láti ọdún 1959.
translations.reference: Apia was founded in the 1850s and has been the official capital of Samoa since 1959.
translations.hypothesis: Apia was founded in the 1850s and has been the capital of Samoa since 1959.

translations.source: Ilé náà ni ó jẹ́ ilẹ̀ táwọn ológun ojú òfúrufú ti ma ń wàákò lọ́dún 1889 nígbàtí ọkọ̀ ojú omi méje ti ilẹ Germany, US àti Britain kọ̀ láti kúrò níbùdó.
translations.reference: The harbor was the site of an infamous naval standoff in 1889 when seven ships from Germany, the US, and Britain refused to leave the harbor.
translations.hypothesis: The base was a strategic island that had been occupied by the US Navy since 1889 when seven German, US and British ships refused to leave the area.

translations.source: Gbogbo ọkọ̀ ojú omi ti wọ omi, àyàfi ti British cruiser. Ó tọ igba ẹ̀mí àwọn ara ìlú Améríkà àti Germany tó ṣòfò.
translations.reference: All the ships were sunk, except for one British cruiser. Nearly 200 American and German lives were lost.
translations.hypothesis: All the battleships except the British cruisers were sunk. It was the end of the American and German sailors' lives.

translations.source: Ni akoko ijagbara fun ominira eyiti Mau se agbateru re, ikorajopo worowo ti o wa ye ni ilu na yori si pipa oloye pataki Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.
translations.reference: During the struggle for independence organised by the Mau movement, a peaceful gathering in the town resulted in the killing of the paramount chief Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.
translations.hypothesis: In the climate of growing calls for independence, which Mau supported, the economic situation worsened under the leadership of Head of State Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ òkun ló wà, látàrí Auckland straddling ti ibùdó ọkọ̀ ojú omi. Àwọn tó gbajúmọ̀ jù wà ní agbègbè méta.
translations.reference: There are many beaches, due to Auckland's straddling of two harbours. The most popular ones are in three areas.
translations.hypothesis: There are many islands, with Auckland straddling a major one. The most popular are in three main areas.

translations.source: Awọn etí àríwá ọ̀sà (ní àríwá èbúté)wà ni Òkun pacific, bẹ́ẹ̀ ni wọ́n nà á láti Long Bay ní Àríwá sí Devonport ni Gús.
translations.reference: North Shore beaches (in North Harbour district) are on the Pacific Ocean and stretch from Long Bay in the north to Devonport in the south.
translations.hypothesis: The North Island's (Northland Peninsula) west coast beaches face west into the Tasman Sea, and run from Long Bay in the north to Devonport in the south.

translations.source: Gbogbo Wọ́n lo fẹ́rẹ̀ jẹ́ òkun-oníyanrin, tó finilọ́kànbalẹ̀ láti lúwẹ̀, tí ó sì ní bòji, èyí tí igi pohutukawa ṣe.
translations.reference: They are almost all sandy beaches with safe swimming, and most have shade provided by pohutukawa trees.
translations.hypothesis: All are used to some extent as timber, though some are too gnarled or twisted to be of much use, and the wood of the kauri pine is highly prized.

translations.source: Àwọn ẹ̀gbẹ́ Omi Ọ̀nà Tamaku wà ní Pápá Ọkọ̀ Ojú Omi Waitemata Harbour, ní òkéọjà àti agbègbè Mission Bay àti St Heliers ní àringbùngbùn Auckland.
translations.reference: Tamaki Drive beaches are on the Waitemata Harbour, in the upmarket suburbs of Mission Bay and St Heliers in Central Auckland.
translations.hypothesis: The waters around Tamaki Makaurau are in the Hauraki Gulf and Waitemata Harbour, just off the North Island of New Zealand.

translations.source: Awon etiosa yi je ti elebi ti ere maa n po si nigba miin, won ni orisirisi oja ni eti oda. Omi wiwe o lewu.
translations.reference: These are sometimes-crowded family beaches with a good range of shops lining the shore. Swimming is safe.
translations.hypothesis: These services are highly variable in quality and often have hidden costs. Bottled water is usually safe.

translations.source: Àkọ́kọ́ ni ọtí abẹ́léjẹ́. Kìí ṣe ọtí tó le púpọ̀ ṣùgbọ́n ó dùn ó n tunilára. Ọtí abẹ́lé ni wọ́n tún pè ní “Mant.”
translations.reference: The main local beer is 'Number One', it is not a complex beer, but pleasant and refreshing. The other local beer is called "Manta".
translations.hypothesis: The first is palm wine. It is not a very strong alcoholic drink but it is pleasant and refreshing. Palm wine is also called "mnan."

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn wáìnì Faranse ló wà láti ni, àmọ ọtí́ ilẹ̀ New Zealand àti Australia rìn jù.
translations.reference: There are many French wines to be had, but the New Zealand and Australian wines might travel better.
translations.hypothesis: Most French wines are affordable, though New Zealand and Australian wines are more expensive.

translations.source: Omi ẹ̀rọ agbègbè dára láti mu, ṣùgbọ́n omi inú ìgò rọrùn láti rí tí o bá bẹ̀rù.
translations.reference: The local tap water is perfectly safe to drink, but bottled water is easy to find if you are fearful.
translations.hypothesis: Public taps provide good drinking water, but bottled water is more readily available.

translations.source: Fún àwọn ara ìlú Australia, àbá coffee “flat white” jẹ́ ti ìlú òkèrè. Dúdú kan sì jẹ́ “espresso” cappuccino wá pẹ̀lú ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ cream (not frotth), àti pé wọ́n bú tea náà láìsí mílíkì.
translations.reference: For Australians, the idea of 'flat white' coffee is foreign. A short black is 'espresso', cappuccino comes heaped high with cream (not froth), and tea is served without milk.
translations.hypothesis: For Australians, the term "flat white" is a generic term for a coffee beverage. The only black coffee is "long black" (espresso with hot water), cappuccino comes with a lot of foam (not froth), and tea is usually served without milk.

translations.source: Ṣokoléètì gbígbóná náà dára tó ní òṣùwọ̀n ti Belgium. Àwọn omi éso gbówó lórí, ṣùgbọ́n wọn dára.
translations.reference: The hot chocolate is up to Belgian standards. Fruit juices are pricey but excellent.
translations.hypothesis: The hot chocolate is a Belgian standard. The orange juice is a bit expensive, but it is good.

translations.source: ọ̀pọ̀ ìrìnàjò lọ sí abẹ́ òkun ni o máa n wáyé yípo ọdún, bẹ́ẹ̀ ni àwọn ìfarapa tí ó wáyé látàrí àwọn ìrìnàjò wọ̀nyí kò pọ̀ rárá.
translations.reference: Many trips to the reef are made all year around, and injuries due to any of these causes on the reef are rare.
translations.hypothesis: Most drownings are predictable and preventable, and the consequences of these deaths are devastating.

translations.source: Sibe si, gba imoran awon alase, ma ru fin gbogbo ami, se akiyesi gbogbo ikilo ipamo.
translations.reference: Still, take advice from authorities, obey all signs, and pay close attention to safety warnings.
translations.hypothesis: In addition, take the advice of the experts, read all the signs, and watch where you step.

translations.source: Ẹ̀ja-jẹ́lì alápòtí ma ń wà ní bèbè odò àti àwọn ibi tó súnmọ́ ẹnú odò ńlá látinú oṣù kẹwàá sí oṣù kẹrin àríwá 1770. Wọ́n tún le rí wọn lẹ́yìn àkókò wọ̀nyí.
translations.reference: Box jellyfish occur near beaches and near river estuaries from October to April north of 1770. They can occasionally be found outside these times.
translations.hypothesis: The annual migration of the jellyfish occurs between October and April in the northern hemisphere and between April and October in the southern hemisphere.

translations.source: Ẹja ṣáàkì wà lóòótọ́ àmọ́ wọn kì í sàkọlù sí ènìyàn. Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ wọn ló bẹ̀rú ènìyàn tí wọ́n yíò sì má a sá fún wọn, lúwẹ̀ẹ́ kúrò lọ́dọ wọn.
translations.reference: Sharks do exist, however they rarely attack humans. Most sharks are scared of humans and would swim away.
translations.hypothesis: There are many species of jellyfish, and most are not dangerous to humans. Most jellyfish stings are painful but not dangerous, and the victim is usually left with only a painful, red rash.

translations.source: Oni Olomiiyo o ki n gbe ninu osa, gan gan, ibudo iseda won ni iyawo odo sinu ile to wa ni apa ariwa lati Rokamptini.
translations.reference: Saltwater Crocodiles do not actively live in the ocean, their primary habitat is in river estuaries north from Rockhampton.
translations.hypothesis: The mayor does not live in the city, and his only connection to the northern city of Roorkee is his wife's ancestral home there.

translations.source: Ríra àyè sílẹ̀ ní inú ọkọ̀ máa ń fún àwọn arìnrìnàjò ní ìbàlẹ̀ ọkàn pé àwọn yóò rí ibi sùn sí tí àwọn bá gúnlẹ̀.
translations.reference: Booking in advance gives the traveller peace of mind that they will have somewhere to sleep once they arrive at their destination.
translations.hypothesis: Booking a ride in advance gives riders peace of mind knowing they have a guaranteed ride when needed.

translations.source: Àwọn tó ma n ṣaájò ìrìn àjò ma n ṣòwò pẹ̀lú àwọn ilé ìtura, biotilejepe o ṣeéṣe ki o gba àyè míìn sílẹ̀, bii ọgbà ikapo, nípasẹ̀ àwọn tó ma n ṣaájò ìrìn àjò.
translations.reference: Travel agents often have deals with specific hotels, although you may find it possible to book other forms of accommodation, like camping grounds, through a travel agent.
translations.hypothesis: Travellers often camp in the shelters, though it is possible to get a bed in the huts, which are run by local people.

translations.source: Àwọn aṣojú Ilé iṣẹ́ arìnàjò máa ń sábà pèsè àwọn ẹ̀dínwó pẹ̀lú oúnje àárọ̀, àwọn ètò ìrìnà lílọ/pípadà láti pápakọ̀ òfuurufú tàbí àkójọpọ̀ èdínwó fífò ọkọ̀ òfuurufú àti ilé ìtura .
translations.reference: Travel agents usually offer packages that include breakfast, transportation arrangements to/from the airport or even combined flight and hotel packages.
translations.hypothesis: Travel agents often provide packages that include meals, transportation/flights and sometimes even pre-booked hotels.

translations.source: Wọ́n tún lè fi ààyè sílẹ̀ fún ọ bí o bá nílò láti ronú lórí ìpèsè tàbí kí o gba àwọn àkọ́ọ̀lẹ̀ mìíran fún ibi tí ò ń lọ (àpẹrẹ. ìwé ìrìnnà).
translations.reference: They can also hold the reservation for you if you need time to think about the offer or procure other documents for your destination (e.g. visa).
translations.hypothesis: They can also allow you to book other travel essentials (e.g., a flight).

translations.source: Koko fi awon atunse tabi ibeere kan kan lo osise aajo irin ajo, ki o to fi lo ile itura naa.
translations.reference: Any amendments or requests though should be coursed through the travel agent first and not directly with the hotel.
translations.hypothesis: Make any necessary changes or requests to your travel agent, before confirming with the hotel.

translations.source: Àwọn míìn to ba lọ fún àwọn ayẹyẹ orin míìn ma n pàgọ́ sí ibi ayẹyẹ náà, púpọ̀ nínú wọ́n gbàgbọ́ wípé ìṣe yí ṣe kókó fún ìrírí náà.
translations.reference: For some festivals, the vast majority of the attendants to music festivals decide to camp on site, and most attendants consider it a vital part of the experience.
translations.hypothesis: Those who attend concerts by this band expect a certain experience, and most of them deliver.

translations.source: Ti o ba fe sunmo ibi ti idije ti n sele o gbodo tete de ibi ipago lati ri aaye si ibi ti o sunmo orin kiko.
translations.reference: If you want to be close to the action you're going to have to get in early to get a camping site close to the music.
translations.hypothesis: If you want to get close to the action, you should head to the pit area early to get a good spot near the fences.

translations.source: Rántí wípé lóòtọ́ orin orí ìtàgé le ti parí, àwọn agbọn ayẹyẹ kan wà tí yí o ma kọrin lọ títí di alẹ́ gẹ̀rẹ́gẹ̀rẹ́.
translations.reference: Remember that even though music on the main stages may have finished, there may be sections of the festival that will keep playing music until late into the night.
translations.hypothesis: Remember that although the concerts are over, there are still parties that go on until the early hours of the morning.

translations.source: Àwọn ọdún ìbílẹ̀ kan wà tí wọ́n ni ibi pàtàkì fún àwọn ẹbí tí wọ́n ni ọmọ láti dé sí.
translations.reference: Some festivals have special camping areas for families with young children.
translations.hypothesis: There are annual cultural events that are of particular interest to families with children.

translations.source: Bí o bá ń kọjá láàrin ẹkùn àríwá Baltic nígbà òtútù, sàyẹ̀wò ibi tí àgọ́ wà, bí ẹni ń la inú yìnyín kọjá se ma ń fa ariwo fáwọn tó sè palára fún jùlọ.
translations.reference: If crossing the Northern Baltic in winter, check the cabin location, as going through ice causes quite horrible noise for those most affected.
translations.hypothesis: If you are traveling through the Baltic countries in winter, check the ice conditions before you go out on the lakes, as the ice can be thin and dangerous in some places.

translations.source: Lára ìrìnkiri Petersburg ni mímọ́ fi àkókó kún ìlú. Àwọn èrò Cruise ni ìyọ̀ǹda àlàkalẹ̀ ìwé ìrìnnà (yẹ̀ẹ́wò).
translations.reference: Saint Petersburg cruises include time in town. Cruise passengers are exempted from visa requirements (check the terms).
translations.hypothesis: In St. Petersburg you should definitely take a canal tour. The boat tours are a great way to see the city.

translations.source: Àwọn ibi ìta tẹ́tẹ́ máa ń gbìyànjú láti ri dájú pé àlékún àsìkò àti owó tí àwọn àlejò wọn ń ná́. Fèrèsé àti ago kìí fi gbogbo ìgbà wà ní ibẹ̀, a sì máa nira láti rí ọnà tí ó jáde sí ìta.
translations.reference: Casinos typically make many efforts to maximize time and money spent by guests. Windows and clocks are usually absent, and exits can be hard to find.
translations.hypothesis: Tourist traps are sometimes hard to avoid, as they are often located in the most convenient and central locations, and are sometimes the only options available. Cars and buses are not always able to reach them, and sometimes the only way to reach them is by boat.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà ni wọ́n máa ń ni oúnjẹ, omi àti ìdánilárayá pàtàkì tí ó yàtọ̀ kí àwọn alejò wọn lè máa dunnu kí wọn si fẹ́ lá ti wà ní sàkáni wọn.
translations.reference: They usually have special food, drink and entertainment offers, to keep guests in a good mood, and keep them at the premise.
translations.hypothesis: They often provide food, water and other essential supplies so that guests may be comfortable and willing to stay.

translations.source: Awo ibo min ma n funyan ni oti mimu lofe. Sugbon, oti amuju ma n dinwo ogbon, ati pe awon to je ogbologbo ninu tete moo pe o se pataki lati ma mu oti.
translations.reference: Some venues offer alcoholic beverages on the house. However, drunkenness impairs judgement, and all good gamblers know the importance of staying sober.
translations.hypothesis: Alcoholic drinks are often socially acceptable and encouraged. However, alcohol is a toxic and psychoactive substance with dependence producing properties that can lead to health and social problems.

translations.source: Ẹnikẹni tó bá ma wakọ̀ sáré tàbí gun orí òkè níláti ro yìnyín tàbí òtútù.
translations.reference: Anyone who's going to drive at high latitudes or over mountain passes should consider the possibility of snow, ice, or freezing temperatures.
translations.hypothesis: Anyone planning a trek or a stay in high mountains should be aware of this risk and take appropriate precautions.

translations.source: Láwọn ọjọ́ tílẹ̀ bá tutù tàbí tí yìnyín ń bọ̀, o kò le sáré bí o bá ń wakọ̀ bì ẹ ni pé o wà lórí ọ̀dà.
translations.reference: On icy and snowy roadways, friction is low and you cannot drive as if you were on bare asphalt.
translations.hypothesis: On cold or wet days, you can't go far on a bicycle if you are on a paved road.

translations.source: Nigba iji-lile, sno to to ha o mo le tete ro.
translations.reference: During blizzards, enough snow to get you stuck can fall in very little time.
translations.hypothesis: During the attack, try to stay as calm as possible.

translations.source: Sno to n fe abi jabo, abi eruku abi yinyin lori ferese moto, le mu ki a ma riran daa daa.
translations.reference: Visibility may also be restricted by falling or blowing snow or by condensation or ice on vehicle windows.
translations.hypothesis: A horn that is too high or too low, or a squeak or rattle from the vehicle, can be annoying.

translations.source: Ní ìdàkejì ẹ̀wẹ̀, ojú ọjọ́ tó ń rọ yìnyín jẹ́ ohun tí ó máa ń ṣẹlẹ̀ lóòrèkóòrè ní àwọn orílẹ̀èdè púpọ̀, bẹ́ẹ̀ sì ni súnkẹrẹ-fàkẹrẹ a máa wà yípo ọdun.
translations.reference: On the other hand, icy and snowy conditions are normal in many countries, and traffic goes on mostly uninterrupted all year round.
translations.hypothesis: On the other hand, extreme temperature events are observed to be increasing in frequency and duration in many regions, and the risk of wildfires has increased.

translations.source: Àwọn safari ló fẹ́rẹ̀ jẹ́ òǹfà ìrìnafẹ́ jùlọ ní ilẹ̀ adúláwọ̀ àti ohun táwọn àlejò ma ń péwò jù.
translations.reference: Safaris are perhaps the greatest tourism draw in Africa and the highlight for many visitors.
translations.hypothesis: Safaris are the most common tourist attraction in Africa and a major draw for many visitors.

translations.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí wọ́n ń pè ní safari túmọ̀ sí ìrìnàjò oríilẹ̀ láti lọ wo àwọn ohun abẹ̀mí inú igbó ilẹ̀ adúláwọ̀ pàápàá jùlọ níbití igi pọ̀sí.
translations.reference: The term safari in popular use refers to overland travel to view the stunning African wildlife, particularly on savanna.
translations.hypothesis: The word safari comes from an Arabic word meaning "journey" or "outing," and it originally referred to a journey into the African interior, especially to view the wildlife.

translations.source: Àwọn ẹranko kan bí i erin àti àgùfọn, má ń súnmọ́ àwọn ọkọ̀ pẹ́kípẹ́kí àti àwọn ohun èlò tóbágbà mun yíò fààyè sílẹ̀ fún wíwò tó dára.
translations.reference: Some animals, such as elephants and giraffes, tend to approach closely to cars and standard equipment will allow good viewing.
translations.hypothesis: Some animals, such as the moose and elk, are more predictable around cars and equipment, and will give you a good look before moving on.

translations.source: Kìnìún, ẹkùn, àti Àmọ̀tẹ́kùn máa ń tijú ní ìgbà mìíràn, àti pé o máa rí wọn dáadáa pẹ̀lú ẹrọ aláwòfín.
translations.reference: Lions, cheetahs and leopards are sometimes shy and you will see them better with binoculars.
translations.hypothesis: The poles, rings, and atmosphere are sometimes best seen with binoculars.

translations.source: Rínrìn nínú ìgbé (tí a tún pẹ ní “ìrìn inú’ igbó”, “Ìrìnsẹ nínú igbó”, tàbí rínrìn “pèlú ẹsè”) pẹ fún irinsé, yálà fún wákàtí díè tàbí ọjọ́ pípé.
translations.reference: A walking safari (also called a "bush walk", "hiking safari", or going "footing") consists of hiking, either for a few hours or several days.
translations.hypothesis: Hiking (also known as "bushwalking", "trail hiking", or "long-distance hiking") is generally a day or overnight activity.

translations.source: Ìdíje paralympics máa wáyé láti ọjọ́ kẹ́rìndínlógún oṣù kẹjọ sí ojọ́ karùn ún oṣù kẹsàn án ọdún 2021. Oríṣìíríṣìí ibi ni àwọn ètò yóò ti máa wáyé jákèjádò Japan.
translations.reference: The Paralympics will take place from 24 August to 5 September 2021. Some events will be held in other locations throughout Japan.
translations.hypothesis: The Paralympic Games will be held from 24 August to 5 September 2021. Events will take place at 23 venues across Japan.

translations.source: Tokio màá jẹ́ ìlú Asia kan soso to sàlejo Olimpiki àkókò ọ̀run méjì torí wọ́́n salejo re ní ọdún 1984.
translations.reference: Tokyo will be the only Asian city to have hosted two summer Olympics, having hosted the games in 1964.
translations.hypothesis: Tokyo will be the first Asian city to have hosted the Olympic Games twice, having hosted in 1964.

translations.source: Tó bá jẹ́ wípé o ti pè fún ìwé ìrìnnà ojú òfúrufú àti iléègbé fọ́dún 2020 kí wọ́n tó kéde ìsúnsíwájú, o lè wà nípò ẹ̀tàn.
translations.reference: If you booked your flights and accommodation for 2020 before the postponement was announced, you may have a tricky situation.
translations.hypothesis: If you applied for visas to enter the Schengen Area in 2020 before the travel ban, you may be in a similar situation.

translations.source: Ofin ifagile wa ni otooto, sugbon ni ipari Erena opo ofin ifagile to dale ori aarun Korona o ni sun de Agemo 2020, igba ti won kosile pe won maa se Olimpiki.
translations.reference: Cancellation policies vary, but as of late March most coronavirus-based cancellation policies don't extend to July 2020, when the Olympics had been scheduled.
translations.hypothesis: Our bubble is still intact, but at the end of March 2020, just before the Olympics were postponed, a few of our bubble had COVID.

translations.source: A ti mọ̀ pé púpọ̀ nínú àwọn tíkẹ́tì fún party ma ń jẹ́ ¥2,500 àti ¥130,000, pẹ̀lú irú tíkẹ́tì kanáà tó jẹ́ ¥7,000.
translations.reference: It's expected that most event tickets will cost between ¥2,500 and ¥130,000, with typical tickets costing around ¥7,000.
translations.hypothesis: We know that most of the party tickets are between 2,500 and 130,000 yen, with an average of 7,000 yen per ticket.

translations.source: Lìlọ àwọn asọ tútù máà n jẹ kí wọn gbẹ. Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ ilé ìtura ní ohun èlò láti lọ asọ fún ẹ̀yáwó, bó tilè jépé ènìyàn o sí nínú yàrá ilé ìtura.
translations.reference: Ironing damp clothes can help them dry. Many hotels have an iron and ironing board available for loan, even if one is not present in the room.
translations.hypothesis: Wearing light-coloured, loose-fitting clothing can help keep you cool. Many hotels provide fans, and if not, ask for one.

translations.source: Bí kò bá sí ẹ̀rọ ìlọsọ àbí tí o bá nífẹ̀ẹ́ sí à ti wọ ìbọ̀sẹ̀ tó bágbà mun èyí ti a ti lọ̀, nígbànáà ní o lè lo ẹ̀eọ ìgbẹrun tó bá wà nílẹ̀.
translations.reference: If an iron isn't available, or if you don't fancy wearing ironed socks, then you can try using a hairdryer, if available.
translations.hypothesis: If you don't have a laptop or if you prefer a more hands-on approach, you can always use a local library.

translations.source: Sọ́ra kí o ma se jẹ́kí aṣọ náà gbóná jù, (èyi tó lè fa ìsúnkì tàbí kó jó tó bá ti pọ̀jù).
translations.reference: Be careful not to allow fabric to become too hot (which can cause shrinkage, or in extreme cases, scorch).
translations.hypothesis: Be careful not to make the garment too tight (this can cause binding or bunching).

translations.source: Orísìí ọ̀nà lówà láti ya omi sí mímọ́, àwọn ọ̀kan lè gbógun ti àwọn ìdúnkokò kọ̀ọ̀kan.
translations.reference: There are different ways of purifying water, some more effective against specific threats.
translations.hypothesis: There are many ways to make water safe to drink, some methods are more appropriate for particular circumstances.

translations.source: Láwọn apá kan, bí wọ́n bá ti gbé omi kaná fún ìṣẹ́jú kan, ó ti tó, à mọ́ láwọn apá míràn wọ́n nílò ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìṣẹ́jú.
translations.reference: In some areas boiling water for a minute is enough, in others several minutes are needed.
translations.hypothesis: In some areas, after just one hour, it is already too hot, while in other areas it may take several hours.

translations.source: Àwọn amóhundára pé orísìírísìí, bí o bá sìní ẹ̀dùn, o lè se àgbéwò à ti ra omi nínú ìgò tí wọ́n ti lẹ̀ láti iléeṣẹ́ tó níyì.
translations.reference: Filters vary in effectiveness, and should you have a concern, then you should consider buying your water in a sealed bottle from a reputable company.
translations.hypothesis: There are many different kinds, and if you're feeling brave, you can even try the local delicacy of drinking palm wine straight from the source.

translations.source: Àwọn arìnrìnàjò lè salábàápàdé àwọn ẹranko ayọnilẹ́nu tí wọn kò dámọ̀ ní agbègbè ilé wọn.
translations.reference: Travellers may encounter animal pests that they are not familiar with in their home regions.
translations.hypothesis: Travellers may encounter animals they do not normally see in their home range.

translations.source: Àwọn kòkòrò lè ba oúnjẹ jẹ́, fa ìríra tàbí tó bá le tán fa ẹ̀hún ara, tí oró rẹ̀ yíó ma káàkiri tàbí ran ẹlòmíràn.
translations.reference: Pests can spoil food, cause irritation, or in a worse case cause allergic reactions, spread venom, or transmit infections.
translations.hypothesis: The bacteria can invade the intestinal wall, causing inflammation or, more rarely, fatal haemorrhage, with the latter being more likely in older people.

translations.source: Ààrùn tó ń ràn gan tàbí àwọn ẹranko burúkú tó lè sèpalára tàbí sekúpa ènìyàn tipatipá kì í sábàá jẹ́ kòkòrò ayọnilẹ́nu.
translations.reference: Infectious diseases themselves, or dangerous animals that can injure or kill people by force, do not usually qualify as pests.
translations.hypothesis: Diseases that are transmitted by mosquitoes or other blood-sucking insects are rarely, if ever, caused by fungi.

translations.source: ìraja Duty free ni àǹfàní láti ra àwọn ọjà tí wọ́n ti yọ owó orí kúrò tí ó sì wà láwọn agbègbè kan.
translations.reference: Duty free shopping is the opportunity to buy goods exempted from taxes and excises at certain locations.
translations.hypothesis: Duty-free shops are allowed to sell goods without paying taxes in certain areas.

translations.source: Àwọn tó ń lọ sí àwọn orílẹ̀ tí wọ́n tí ń sanwó orí gegere nígbà míràn lè fí owó tó pọ̀ pamọ̀, pàápàá lórí ìpèsè bí i ọtí, ẹlẹ́rìndòdò àti tábà.
translations.reference: Travellers bound for countries with heavy taxation can sometimes save a considerable amount of money, especially on products such as alcoholic beverages and tobacco.
translations.hypothesis: Travellers to countries where alcohol is more expensive may save money, particularly on items such as beer, wine and spirits.

translations.source: Ààyè tí ó wà láàrin Point Marion àti Fairmont se àfihàn àwọn ìpènijà àwọn awakọ̀ ní ojú ọ̀nà márosẹ̀ Buffalo-Pittsburgh, ní gbogbo igbà tí wọ́n bá gba àwọn ojú òpó tó dáwà kọjá.
translations.reference: The stretch between Point Marion and Fairmont presents the most challenging driving conditions on the Buffalo-Pittsburgh Highway, passing frequently through isolated backwoods terrain.
translations.hypothesis: The area between Point Marion and Fairmont showed the most driver difficulty on the Buffalo-Pittsburgh Pike, mainly because of the steep grades.

translations.source: Tí wíwa ọks kò bá ma ẹ lára ní òpópónà , má sọ̀rọ̀ nípa ǹkan tí o lè ṣe. àwọn ọ̀nà tó lọ sókè tó tun lọ sílẹ̀, àwọn ọ̀nà tóró, àti ọ̀nà tó tẹ̀ borí.
translations.reference: If you're not used to driving on country roads, keep your wits about you: steep grades, narrow lanes, and sharp curves predominate.
translations.hypothesis: If you don't feel comfortable walking on the beach, there are many other activities available. There are boat tours, horseback riding tours, and ATV tours.

translations.source: Òsùwọ̀n eré sísá tí a má ń kà sáàba má n kéré ju tàwọn agbọn àtẹ̀yìnwá lọ- lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà ó ma ń jẹ́ láàrin máìlì márùndínlógójì sí ogóji wákàtí kan (56mẹ́rìndínlọ́gọta-mẹ́rìnlélọ́gọ́ta kìlómítà wákàtí) - ati pe igboran pípe sí i se pàtàkì ju àìgbọ́ràn lọ.
translations.reference: Posted speed limits are noticeably lower than in previous and subsequent sections — commonly 35-40 mph (56-64 km/h) — and strict obedience to them is even more important than otherwise.
translations.hypothesis: The typical duration of a marathon is slightly longer than the previous record - about 2 hours 15 minutes (42.195 kilometres or 26.2 miles) - and the ability to run a sub-2 hour marathon is highly unlikely.

translations.source: Ìyàlẹ́nu ló jẹ́ ná pé iṣẹ́ ẹrọ alágbèéká ṣiṣẹ́ dáadáa ní ibíyìí ju ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn agbègbẹ̀ mìíràn lọ, bíi Aginjù Pennsylvania.
translations.reference: Curiously, though, mobile phone service is much stronger here than along many other stretches of the route, e.g. the Pennsylvania Wilds.
translations.hypothesis: Interestingly, cellular service here is better than in many other areas, including central Pennsylvania.

translations.source: Àwọn páfuj Jamani dáa àti ní Baferia, wọ́n ki wọ́n dẹ̀ pe oríṣi , bíi tí Ostria tó wà lẹ́gbẹ́ wọn ní apá guusu.
translations.reference: German pastries are quite good, and in Bavaria, are quite rich and varied, similar to those of their southern neighbor, Austria.
translations.hypothesis: The German-speaking areas are well off, and Bavaria is rich, while Austria is poorer in the south.

translations.source: Èso apple ni wọ́n má ń fi se àfúnpọ̀ èso júlọ yípo ọdún, nígbà tí wọ́n má ń lo èso ṣẹrí àti púlọ̀mù lákòókò ooru.
translations.reference: Fruit pastries are common, with apples cooked into pastries year round, and cherries and plums making their appearances during the summer.
translations.hypothesis: Apples are the most common fruit grown, while citrus and pomegranates are in season during the winter.
