translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ọjà German ni almonds, lpà, àti àwọn ẹ̀pa orí igi wà nínú rẹ̀. Àwọn àkàrà òyìnbó tí a mọ̀ dáadáa ní a lè jẹ́ pẹ̀lú ife coffee.
translations.reference: Many German baked goods also feature almonds, hazelnuts, and other tree nuts. Popular cakes often pair particularly well with a cup of strong coffee.
translations.hypothesis: Many German breads and buns contain nuts, dried fruits and seeds. The famous pretzels are also a good option for a snack.

translations.source: Tí o bá fẹ́ àwọn ǹkan dídùn tó sì kún fún èròjà, gbìyànjú rẹ̀ wò ṣùgbọ́n ó dá lórí agbègbè bí Berliner, Pfannkuchen tàbí Krapfen.
translations.reference: If you want some small though rich pastries, try what depending on region are called Berliner, Pfannkuchen or Krapfen.
translations.hypothesis: If you are after something more substantial and filling, then you should try one of the local specialities such as Berliner, Pfannkuchen or Krapfen.

translations.source: Korri je isebe ti a se pelu ewe ati egbo, pelu okan ninu eran ati ewebe.
translations.reference: A curry is a dish based on herbs and spices, together with either meat or vegetables.
translations.hypothesis: A kori is a dish made with fish and vegetables, with one or more types of meat and vegetables.

translations.source: kọrí lè ‘’gbẹ” tàbí kí ó “lómi” ó dá lórí iye om.
translations.reference: A curry can be either "dry" or "wet" depending on the amount of liquid.
translations.hypothesis: The ability to "hear" or "feel" depends on the amount of energy.

translations.source: Ní ẹkùn abẹ́lé ti ìhà Àríwá India àti Pakistan, wọn a máa lo yúgọ̀tì̀ ninú kọrí; ni ọ̀pọ̀ ògbà; ni ìhà Gúsù India àti àwọn agbègbè coastal tó kù, omi àgbọn ní wọ́n sábà máa ń lò.
translations.reference: In inland regions of Northern India and Pakistan, yogurt is commonly used in curries; in Southern India and some other coastal regions of the subcontinent, coconut milk is commonly used.
translations.hypothesis: In the subtropical highlands of northern India and Pakistan, yoghurt is often eaten plain; in the Middle East; and in the Indian subcontinent and surrounding coastal regions, it is often consumed as lassi.

translations.source: Níbí a se ní láti yàn nínú erékùsù ẹgbẹ̀rín mẹ́tàdínlọ́gbọ̀n, oúnjẹ àwọn ènìyàn ilẹ̀ Indonisia ni ó jẹ́ àkórí fún gbogbo àwọn oúnjẹ agbèaè tí ó wà káakkiri orílẹ̀èdè náà.
translations.reference: With 17,000 islands to choose from, Indonesian food is an umbrella term covering a vast variety of regional cuisines found across the nation.
translations.hypothesis: From the 36 regions, the cuisine of Central Java is the most representative of the country's cuisine in general.

translations.source: Sugbon ti a ba lo o laini alaye siwaju si, o ma n saba tumo si ounje iwase lati awon apa aaringbungbun ati ila oorun irekusu Java gangan.
translations.reference: But, if used without further qualifiers, the term tends to mean the food originally from the central and eastern parts of the main island Java.
translations.hypothesis: But if you're using the information above, you'll most likely be pointed towards restaurants in the downtown core and the eastern suburbs of Java.

translations.source: Niisin ounje Jafa wa kaakiri asipelago, ekun re ni asayan ounje ti a se loso feere, awon ajasa ti o tayo julo je epa, ata, suga (paapa julo suga agbon) ati ajasa orisirisi.
translations.reference: Now widely available throughout the archipelago, Javanese cuisine features an array of simply seasoned dishes, the predominant flavorings the Javanese favor being peanuts, chillies, sugar (especially Javanese coconut sugar) and various aromatic spices.
translations.hypothesis: Typical of the cuisine of the islands, the most common ingredients are coconut, taro, breadfruit, yams, potatoes, sweet potatoes, plantains, rice, corn, beans, pumpkin, squash, pineapples, mangoes, papayas, bananas, and sugarcane.

translations.source: Stirrups wa láti pèsè ìrànwọ́ fún èýkéyìí ẹsẹ̀ ẹni tí o ń wa kẹ̀kẹ́.
translations.reference: Stirrups are supports for the rider's feet that hang down on either side of the saddle.
translations.hypothesis: Stirrups are available to assist any disabled person to ride a bicycle.

translations.source: Wọ́n sàgbékalẹ̀ ìdúró tó ga fún àwọn awakọ̀ àmọ́ wọ́n lè ní ààbò látarí pé ó se é se fáwọn awakọ̀ láti há sínú wọn.
translations.reference: They provide greater stability for the rider but can have safety concerns due to the potential for a rider's feet to get stuck in them.
translations.hypothesis: There are high barriers to entry for drivers and they are unlikely to be poached by competitors.

translations.source: Bí wọ́n bá ju ẹni tó ń gun eṣin láti oríirẹ̀, à mó tí o fi ẹṣẹ̀ walẹ̀, wọ́n lè wọ́ tuurutu bí ẹṣin bá sálọ. Láti lè mún àdínkù bá ewu, ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìlànà ààbò ni wọ́n lè gbé.
translations.reference: If a rider is thrown from a horse but has a foot caught in the stirrup, they could be dragged if the horse runs away. To minimize this risk, a number of safety precautions can be taken.
translations.hypothesis: If the person is bitten on an arm or leg, the wound is more likely to be contaminated by the dog’s saliva. To reduce the risk, several prevention strategies can be implemented.

translations.source: Lákòókò ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn agunkèké máà n wọ bàtà gíga pèlú ìtèlè bàtà tọ dan tọ si tínrín.
translations.reference: First, most riders wear riding boots with a heel and a smooth, quite narrow, sole.
translations.hypothesis: During the summer most of the population wears light shoes or sandals with a very thin sole.

translations.source: Lẹ́yìn náà, àwọn gààrì pàápàá jùlọ àwọn gààrì ilẹ̀ Geesi ní ọ̀pá ààbò tí ó fi ààyè sílẹ̀ fáwọ láti subú kúrò lórí gààrì bí olùwà tó fẹ́ subú bá fàá sẹ́yì.
translations.reference: Next, some saddles, particularly English saddles, have safety bars that allow a stirrup leather to fall off the saddle if pulled backwards by a falling rider.
translations.hypothesis: However, most modern cars, especially European ones, have seatbelts which allow the occupant to move forward slightly in the event of a head-on collision.

translations.source: Cochamó Valley - Gbajúgbajà òkè ni Chile, tí a tún mọ̀ sí Yosemite ti Gúsù Amẹ́ríkà, pẹ̀lú onírúurú ògiri akọ òkúta àti òkúta sóńsó.
translations.reference: Cochamó Valley - Chile's premier climbing destination, known as the Yosemite of South America, with a variety of granite big walls and crags.
translations.hypothesis: Cochamó Valley - A deep valley in the Lake District of Chile, also known as the Yosemite of South America, with a great variety of rock and ice climbing.

translations.source: Àwọn òkè téńté pèlú àwọn ìwòye tó wúni lòrì láti àwọn igun tó ga lókẹ̀. Àwọn agùnkè láti gbogbo àgbáyé ń fi gbogbo ìgbà wá ọ̀nà titun láára àwọn ògìri.
translations.reference: Summits include breath-taking views from peaks. Climbers from all parts of the world are continually establishing new routes amongst its endless potential of walls.
translations.hypothesis: The high peaks offer stunning views from the many trails that wind through the mountains. Hikers from all over the world are drawn to the region by its many trails.

translations.source: Àwọn ẹrẹ́ ìdárayá orí yìnyìn ta án sọ̀kalẹ̀ láti orí òké, bíi fífò lóri yìnyìn àti wíwa ọkọ̀ lóri yìnyìn, wón gbajúmọ̀ tó ní ṣe pẹ̀lú pé eyàn a yọ́bọ̀ láti orí òkè tí yìnyìn ti bò pẹ̀lú skii tàbí bọ́ọ̀dì lábẹ́ ẹsẹ̀.
translations.reference: Downhill snowsports, which include skiing and snowboarding, are popular sports involving sliding down snow-covered terrain with skis or a snowboard attached to your feet.
translations.hypothesis: The most common form of downhill skiing is alpine skiing, also known as downhill skiing, which consists of skiing down a snow-covered slope on skis with the heels of the boots fixed to the skis.

translations.source: Fífò jẹ́ iṣẹ́ gbòógì fún ìrìn àjò pẹ̀lú ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn adárà tí ó sábàá má ń jẹ́ “ski bums” tí wọ́n gbìmọ̀ gbogbo ìsinmi yíká fífò ní àwọn ibùdó kan gbòógì.
translations.reference: Skiing is a major travelling activity with many enthusiasts, occasionally known as "ski bums," planning entire vacations around skiing at a particular location.
translations.hypothesis: Backcountry touring is a more athletic form of skiing with a few more "ski bums" who love to ski powder in the backcountry.

translations.source: Ọjọ́ ti lọ lórí èrò yíyọ̀ lórí yìnyín — kíkun ihò ilẹ̀ sàfihàn àwọn arin yìnyín tó ti wà láti bí i 5000 BC!
translations.reference: The idea of skiing is very old — cave paintings depicting skiers date back as far as 5000 BC!
translations.hypothesis: The day is dedicated to the exploration of caves — cave paintings are the oldest known works of art, dating back to 5000 BC!

translations.source: Ṣiṣe ski lati oke giga delẹ, ti wa gẹgẹ bi ere idaraya lati bii sẹnturi 17th ati pe ni 1861, awọn ara Nọwe da ẹgbẹ ski idaraya akọkọ ni Ọstrelia.
translations.reference: Downhill skiing as a sport goes back to at least the 17th century, and in 1861 the first recreational ski club was opened by Norwegians in Australia.
translations.hypothesis: Skiing has been around since the 17th century and in 1861, the Norwegians established the first ski club in Australia.

translations.source: Irinkiri pelu Apo agbekoyin lati owo Ski: Eto yi ni a tun da pe ni ski ti odi ilu, irinkiri ski tabi irinse ski.
translations.reference: Backpacking by ski: This activity is also called backcountry ski, ski touring or ski hiking.
translations.hypothesis: Cross-country skiing: This is also known as Nordic skiing, or just skiing.

translations.source: Ó farapẹ́ra ṣùgbọ́n ní ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà kií lọ pẹ̀lú àrà ski alpine tàbí òkè gígùn, èyí tí ó kẹ́yìn máa wáye ní òkè tó ń yọ̀ tí ó sì nílò ohun tó tọ́ àti búùtù púpọ.
translations.reference: It is related to but usually not involving alpine style ski touring or mountaineering, the latter ones done in steep terrain and requiring much stiffer skis and boots.
translations.hypothesis: It is more difficult but often more rewarding than alpine skiing or snowboarding, and is more likely to be found at high-altitude resorts and requires specialized equipment and clothing.

translations.source: Ronú ọ̀nà ìfò bí i ọ̀nà ìwàkè tí o mọ̀.
translations.reference: Think of the skiing route as of a similar hiking route.
translations.hypothesis: Think of a way to phrase it as a question you would ask.

translations.source: Ní ipò tó dáa wàá lé de ibi tí ęsẹ̀ ò lè dé - ṣùgbọ́n kìí ṣe gbogbo ìgbà lo ma ri eré skiini kaa kiri ilu láìsí báàgì àgbékọ́ tó kún fún ojú ọ̀nà tí a ti ṣe lọ́ṣọ́.
translations.reference: In good conditions you will be able to cover somewhat greater distances than walking – but only very seldom you will get the speeds of cross country skiing without a heavy backpack in groomed tracks.
translations.hypothesis: In good conditions you can go far on a normal bike - but you will not be able to ride your bike on the trails without a suspension.

translations.source: Yúróòpù jẹ àkójọpò àwọn orilé-ẹ̀dẹ tó kèrè jọjọ sùgbọn pèlú ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ orilé-ẹ̀dẹ olómìnira. Níwọn bí o ti yẹ kó rí, rírin ìrìn-àjò kàkàkiri ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ àwọn orilé-ẹ̀dẹ yìí túnmọ̀ sí gbígba ohun èlò ìwé ìwọ̀lú àti ìsàkóso ìwé ìrìnnà ní ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ ìgbá.
translations.reference: Europe is a continent that is relatively small but with many independent countries. Under normal circumstances, travelling through multiple countries would mean having to go through visa applications and passport control multiple times.
translations.hypothesis: Europe is a continent made up of many small countries, but also many independent countries. As you might expect, traveling around many of these countries means going through immigration and customs check points several times.

translations.source: Agbegbe Sengeni, sugbon o n sise bii ilu oto ni owo yi.
translations.reference: The Schengen zone, however, works somewhat like one country in this respect.
translations.hypothesis: Sengeni is a small town, but it has a good range of services.

translations.source: Nìwọ̀n ìgbà tí o bá dúró sí agbègbè yí, o lè rékọjá àwọn ẹnubodè láìsí àwọn àyẹ̀wò ìsakóso ìwé̀ ìrìnnà.
translations.reference: As long as you stay in this zone, you can generally cross borders without going through passport control checkpoints again.
translations.hypothesis: Once you are in the Schengen area, you can cross the borders without any passport control.

translations.source: Bákanáà, nípa níní ìwé ìrìnnà Schengen , o kò nílò láti bèèrè fún ìwé ìrìnnà lọ sí àwọn orílẹ̀èdè tó jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ Schengen lọ́ọ̀tọtọ̀, nítorínà, wàá lè pa àkókò, owó àti àwọn àkójọ ìwé mọ́.
translations.reference: Similarly, by having a Schengen visa, you do not need to apply for visas to each of the Schengen member countries separately, hence saving time, money and paperwork.
translations.hypothesis: Besides, with a Schengen visa, you will not have to apply for individual visas to the Schengen member states, thus saving time, money and paperwork.

translations.source: Kò sí ìtumọ̀ tí gbogbo èrò gbà àwọn ohun àkànṣe tí a lè pè ní ohun ini àtijọ́. Àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ owó orí ma ń sọ pé àwọn ohun ìni tóti pẹ́ tó ọdún 100.
translations.reference: There is no universal definition for which manufactured items are antiques. Some tax agencies define goods older than 100 years as antiques.
translations.hypothesis: There is no consensus on what constitutes an antique. Antique dealers often say an item must be at least 100 years old.

translations.source: Àlàyé náà ní ìyàtọ̀ agbègbè, nibití ọjọ́ orí le kéré láwọn agbègbè bí i àríwá Amẹ́ríkà jú ti Yúròpù lọ.
translations.reference: The definition has geographic variations, where the age limit might be shorter in places such as North America than in Europe.
translations.hypothesis: The statistics also vary by region, with the average age at diagnosis being about 10 years younger in North America and Europe than in other regions.

translations.source: Àwọn àgbéjáde iṣk ọwọ́ ni a lè pè ní ẹ̀ṣọ́ ilé, ṣùgbọ́n wọ́n kéré ju àwọn ọjà tó jọra wọn.
translations.reference: Handicraft products might be defined as antiques, though they are younger than similar mass-produced goods.
translations.hypothesis: The finished product can be called a homebrew, but it is less potent than its commercial equivalent.

translations.source: Sínsin ẹranko Reindeer jẹ́ pàtàkì sí ìgbésíayé àwọn Sami àti àṣà tó yí ìtajà ká náà se pàtàkì fọ́pọ̀ tó ní iṣẹ́ mìíràn.
translations.reference: Reindeer husbandry is an important livelihood among the Sámi and the culture surrounding the trade is important also for many with other professions.
translations.hypothesis: The reindeer is of great cultural and economic importance to the Sami people and reindeer herding is an important secondary activity.

translations.source: Kódà nínú ìse pàápàá, kìí se gbogbo Sami ló ti lọ́wọ́ nínú ọ̀sìn aládàńlá ẹranko reindeer, sùgbọ́n wọ́n ń gbé láti pípẹja, ọdẹ síse àti ohun tí ó jọ èyí , níní Reindeer gẹ́gẹ́ bí eranko ìpamọ́.
translations.reference: Even traditionally, though, not all Sámi have been involved in big scale reindeer husbandry, but lived from fishing, hunting and similar, having reindeer mostly as draft animals.
translations.hypothesis: Even among the Sami, not all were involved in reindeer herding, but they lived off the land in other ways, such as trapping, fishing and hunting, and keeping reindeer as pack animals.

translations.source: Lóni ọ̀pọ̀ Sámì n ṣiṣẹ́ ní òwò ìgbàlódẹ́. Òwò ìbẹ̀wò jẹ́ owó pàtàkì tón wọlé ní Sapmi, agbègbè Sámì.
translations.reference: Today many Sámi work in modern trades. Tourism is an important income in Sápmi, the Sámi area.
translations.hypothesis: Many Sámi work in the tourism industry. Tourism is an important source of income in Sapmi, the Sámi region.

translations.source: Lóòótọ́ ni pé wọ́n ń lò ó káàkiri, pàápàá láàárín àwọn tí kìí ṣe Romani, ọ̀rọ̀ yìí “Gypsy” ní wọ́n máa ń ri bí ọ̀rọ̀ àbùkù, nítorí bí o ti ṣe so pọ̀ mọ́ ìgbàgbọ́ àtọwọ́dọ́wọ́ tí kò dára àti ojúwòye tí kò tọ̀nà tí wọn fi ń wo àwọn ará Romani
translations.reference: Though it is widely used, especially among non-Romani, the word "Gypsy" is often considered offensive because of its associations with negative stereotypes and inaccurate perceptions of Romani people.
translations.hypothesis: Although the word is used widely, even by non-Roma people, this word "Gypsy" is considered pejorative, due to its association with negative stereotypes and the inaccurate image of Roma people.

translations.source: Ti orile ede ti o ba fe se abewo si ba je eyi ti won ti se imoran irin ajo fun, o le koba eto adojutofo ti ilera tabi ti fifagi le irinajo re.
translations.reference: If the country you will be visiting becomes subject to a travel advisory, your travel health insurance or your trip cancellation insurance may be affected.
translations.hypothesis: If your final destination is in a country with a risk of polio, consider getting a polio booster dose at least one month before you travel.

translations.source: O tún lè fẹ́ láti bèèrè fún ìmọ̀ràn ìjọba yàtọ̀ sí tìrẹ, sùgbọ́n àmọ̀ràn wà fún àwọn ará ìlú.
translations.reference: You may also wish to consult the advice of governments other than your own, but their advice is designed for their citizens.
translations.hypothesis: You may also wish to request additional government consultation, but the consultation is primarily for citizens.

translations.source: Fun apere, awon omo ilu Amerika ni Apa Ila Orun Arin le ni iriri to yato si ti awon ara Yuropi tabi Arabu.
translations.reference: As one example, American citizens in the Middle East might face different situations from Europeans or Arabs.
translations.hypothesis: For example, the experience of African Americans is quite different from that of white Europeans or Arabs.

translations.source: Ìmọ̀ran jẹ̀ ìjúwé ránpé ọ̀rọ̀ òṣèlú ní ìlú.
translations.reference: Advisories are merely a brief summary of the political situation in one country.
translations.hypothesis: The concept of a nation-state is a relatively modern political idea.

translations.source: Àwọn ìwòye tí wọ́n gbé kalẹ̀ lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà kì í kún tó, ó má ń jẹ́ ti gbogbogbò tàbí kó ti rọrùn jù tí a bá gbé e ti àwọn àlàyé tó kún rẹ́rẹ́ níbòmíràn.
translations.reference: The views presented are often cursory, general and oversimplified compared to the more detailed information available elsewhere.
translations.hypothesis: The quality of available statistics is often uneven, and general-purpose statistics are often too aggregated or disaggregated to be of use for specific purposes.

translations.source: Oju ọjọ́́ tomu gidi ni oruko ti a n pe gbogbo kàyéfì oju ojo to lewu to le fa ìjàmbá pupo, da àwùjọ rú, tàbí fa ìpàdánù ẹ̀mí.
translations.reference: Severe weather is the generic term for any dangerous weather phenomenon with the potential to cause damage, serious social disruption, or loss of human life.
translations.hypothesis: Severe weather refers to any dangerous meteorological phenomenon that has the potential to cause damage, disruption, or death.

translations.source: Ojú ọjọ́ tóle lè Ṣẹlẹ̀ níbikíbi ní ayé ó dẹ̀ pé orísí o dá lórí bi agbègbè naa Ṣe rí, bí iyẹ̀pẹ̀ Ṣe rí àti bí afẹ́fẹ́ Ṣe rí.
translations.reference: Severe weather can occur anywhere in the world, and there are different types of it, which can depend on geography, topography, and atmospheric conditions.
translations.hypothesis: Tropical cyclones can occur anywhere in the world, although they are most common in the tropics and subtropics.

translations.source: Iji lile, yinyin, ojo arooroda, ina inu papa jijo je orisi ona ti a fi n se afihan aida oju ojo, beeni ara sisan, efuufu, omi seleru ati afefe lile.
translations.reference: High winds, hail, excessive precipitation, and wildfires are forms and effects of severe weather, as are thunderstorms, tornadoes, waterspouts, and cyclones.
translations.hypothesis: Heat, humidity, sunburn, heat exhaustion and heat stroke are all possible effects of exposure to solar ultraviolet radiation, as well as dry eyes, skin ageing, cataracts, and increased risk of skin cancer.

translations.source: Agbègbè àti àkókò ojú ọjọ́ tó lágbára nínú èyí ti ìjì líle, yìnyín àti ìji eléruku wà.
translations.reference: Regional and seasonal severe weather phenomena include blizzards, snowstorms, ice storms, and dust storms.
translations.hypothesis: The region and climate in this area is very rugged, with high winds, cold temperatures, and snow and ice.

translations.source: Wọ́n tí gba àwọn arìnrìn àjò ní mọ̀ràn láti ṣọ́ra fún ewu ojú ọja tó lè ní ipa ní agbègbè wọ́n nítorí ó lè ní ipa fún ènikẹni tó bá ní ètò láti rìnrìn àjò.
translations.reference: Travellers are strongly advised to be aware of any risk of severe weather affecting their area as they may affect any travel plans.
translations.hypothesis: Travellers should be advised to take precautions against insect bites in endemic areas as this may affect their travel plans.

translations.source: Ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó bá ń gbèrò láti ṣeré lọ sí ìlú tí a lè pè ní ojú ogun gbọdọ̀ ní imọ̀ ọ̀tọ̀ gbá.
translations.reference: Anyone planning a visit to a country that could be considered a war zone should get professional training.
translations.hypothesis: Anyone planning to hike in a mountainous area should have some mountaineering experience.

translations.source: Ìwárí lórí íntánẹ̀ẹ́tì fún 'ẹ̀kọ́ agbègbè' ma pèsè àdírksì ilé iṣẹ́ agbègbè.
translations.reference: A search of the Internet for 'Hostile environment course' will probably provide the address of a local company.
translations.hypothesis: A search online for "community school" will provide you with the addresses of community schools.

translations.source: Ètò ẹ̀kọ́ kan yíò kárí gbogbo ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí wọ́n pẹ̀kẹ́lù níbí fún ẹ̀kúnrẹ́rẹ́ tó ga, lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà pẹ̀lú ìrírí oníse.
translations.reference: A course will normally cover all the issues discussed here in far greater detail, usually with practical experience.
translations.hypothesis: A curriculum covers all aspects of the topic in great detail, often with practical exercises.

translations.source: Ẹ̀kọ́ ma n lọ fún ọjọ́ 2-5 o dẹ̀ ma n ní eré àpẹrẹ ṣíṣe, ìwòsàn àkókò púpọ̀ àti ẹkọ́ irin ogun nígbà miin.
translations.reference: A course will normally be from 2-5 days and will involve role play, a lot of first aid and sometimes weapons training.
translations.hypothesis: Courses last anywhere from 2 to 5 days and include workshops, bootcamps, and hackathons.

translations.source: Àwọn ìwé àti ìwé magasini tó níṣe pẹ̀lú yíye aginju wọ́pọ̀ ṣúgà itejade tó níṣe pẹ̀lú agbègbè ogun ò pọ̀.
translations.reference: Books and magazines dealing with wilderness survival are common, but publications dealing with war zones are few.
translations.hypothesis: There are few books and magazines about diabetes and very few resources in military languages.

translations.source: Àwọn arìnrìn àjò tí wọ́n ṣètò láti ṣe sex reassignment surgery ní òkè òkun ma ridájú pé wọ́n mú àwọn ìwé àkọsílẹ̀ tó péye dáni fún àti padà wálé.
translations.reference: Voyagers planning sex reassignment surgery abroad must ensure they're carrying valid documents for the return trip.
translations.hypothesis: Travellers who have had gender reassignment surgery should ensure that they carry copies of their surgical records with them and keep them in their possession at all times.

translations.source: Ìmúrasílè àwọn ìjọba láti fàyè gba ìwẹ́ ìrinnà tí kò sàfihàn bóyá akọ yálà abo (X) tàbí àwọn ìwẹ isẹ́ tó pójúòsùwòn ní ìbámu pèlú orúko àti takọ-tabo yàtọ̀.
translations.reference: The willingness of governments to issue passports with gender not stated (X) or documents updated to match a desired name and gender varies.
translations.hypothesis: Governments are urged to allow the issuance of gender-neutral identity documents (i.e. passports and/or national identity documents) regardless of the person’s self-identified gender or sex assigned at birth.

translations.source: Ìfẹ́ ìjọba ilẹ̀ òkèrè láti yẹ́ ìwé àṣẹ yìí sí kìí ṣe nǹkan bàbàr.
translations.reference: Willingness of foreign governments to honour these documents is just as widely variable.
translations.hypothesis: The international community’s willingness to grant this waiver is unprecedented.

translations.source: Ṣíṣe àyẹ̀wò ní ibi ìdádúró àwọn ọlọ́pàá náà ti wá di àyọjúràn gbáà in sáà ọjọ́ kọkànlá, lẹ́yìn – osù kọkànlá, ọdún 2001.
translations.reference: Searches at security checkpoints have also become far more intrusive in the post-September 11, 2001 era.
translations.hypothesis: The checkpoint was destroyed in a suicide bombing on Saturday, October 25, 2003.

translations.source: Àwọn èèyàn tó ń dúró fún iṣẹ́ abẹ ìpàrọ̀ ẹ̀dá má se retí àti kọjá ẹ̀rọ àyẹ̀wò pẹ̀lú iyì àti àdámọ́ wọn.
translations.reference: Pre-operative transgender people should not expect to pass through the scanners with their privacy and dignity intact.
translations.hypothesis: People waiting for organ transplants are not screened for HIV and other diseases.

translations.source: Ìjì omi jẹ́ ṣíṣàn omi tó n padà láti ríru omi tó já bò láti etí ọ̀sà, sába ní rífù àbí bákanáà.
translations.reference: Rip currents are the returning flow from waves breaking off the beach, often at a reef or similar.
translations.hypothesis: A tsunami is a series of powerful ocean waves that are produced by large, rapid displacements of the sea floor, typically caused by undersea earthquakes.

translations.source: Torí topọ́lọ́jì abẹ́ omi ṣíṣàn padàwá dárogún sí àwọn apá kán tó jìn, ṣíṣàn tó ṣe kía lọ sí omi jíjìn lè dáwà síbẹ̀.
translations.reference: Due to the underwater topology the return flow is concentrated at a few deeper sections, and a fast current to deep water may form there.
translations.hypothesis: Because flood waters often contain sewage and agricultural/industrial runoff, water that has been in contact with flood waters may be contaminated.

translations.source: Agara látàrí ìgbìyànjú láti lúwẹ̀ pada ṣẹ́yìn, ní ẹ̀yí tó ṣe é́ ṣe kó se okùnfà ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ikú.
translations.reference: Most deaths happen as result of fatigue trying to swim back against the current, which may be impossible.
translations.hypothesis: The risk of drowning is amplified by the risk of hypothermia, which can cause loss of consciousness and lead to death.

translations.source: Ní kẹ́tẹ́ ti o ba ti kúrò nínú ìjì, wíwẹ odò padà kí jé ìnira mo lọ̀pọ́ ìgbà.
translations.reference: As soon as you get out of the current, swimming back is no more difficult than normally.
translations.hypothesis: Once you are out of the wind, the cold becomes much more of a problem.

translations.source: Gbìyànjú kí o fi ojú sun ibìkan tí wọ́n kò ti ní ká ọ mọ́ tàbí lórí ipa rẹ àti lórí bóyá wọ́n lè se àkíyèsí rẹ, o lè dúró fún ìdóòlà.
translations.reference: Try aiming somewhere where you are not caught again or, depending on your skills and on whether you have been noticed, you might want to wait for rescue.
translations.hypothesis: If you're curious about something you don't understand or its effect on you and want to be more aware, you can become more observant.

translations.source: Àtún gbéwọlé lójijì ma ń tètè wáyé ju ǹkan òjijì lọ (abala ìgbádùn lẹ́yìn ìgbeyàwó kò pọ̀) ó ma ń pẹ́, ò sì ma ń le.
translations.reference: Re-entry shock comes on sooner than culture shock (there's less of a honeymoon phase), lasts longer, and can be more severe.
translations.hypothesis: Rebound is slower than the initial crash (the post-wedding bliss fades), and it's harder.

translations.source: Àwọn arìnrìnàjò tó rọrùn fún láti sàmúnlò àṣà tuntun, nígbà míràn wọ́n má a ni àkókò lile láti lè sàmúnlò àṣà ìbílẹ̀.
translations.reference: Travellers who had an easy time adjusting to the new culture sometimes have a particularly hard time readjusting to their native culture.
translations.hypothesis: Tourists are more likely to adopt new trends, while locals may take longer to adapt to new trends.

translations.source: Bi o se n pada lo ile leyin to ti gbe oke okun, o ti yiwa pada si asa titun o de ti padanu awon isesi re to wa lati asa ile re.
translations.reference: When returning home after living abroad, you've adapted to the new culture and lost some of your habits from your home culture.
translations.hypothesis: As you acclimatize to life back home after a long time away, you begin to notice the little things that you miss about your home culture.

translations.source: Tí o bá lọ sí ilẹ̀ òkèrè fún ìgbà àkọ́kọ́, àwọn ènìyàn lè ṣe sùúrù pẹ̀lú ẹ, nítorí wọn mọ̀ pé àwọn arìnrìnàjò ní orílẹ̀ èdè tuntun nílò láti farasinl.
translations.reference: When you went abroad at first, people were probably patient and understanding, knowing that travellers in a new country need to adapt.
translations.hypothesis: If you go to a foreign country for the first time, people are more likely to help you, because they know that foreigners need to figure things out.

translations.source: Àwọn ènìyàn lè má ms pé ṣùúrù àti ìmọ̀ jẹ́ ǹkan pàtàkì fún àwọn tó rìnrìn àjò bọ̀ wá sílẹ̀.
translations.reference: People may not anticipate that patience and understanding are also necessary for travellers returning home.
translations.hypothesis: People may also be interested in the history and culture of the area they are visiting.

translations.source: Ìró pírámìdì àti àfihàn iná jẹ́ òkan lára àwọn ǹkan tó múnú àwọn ọmọdẹ́ dùn jù lágbàgbẹ̀ yí.
translations.reference: The pyramid sound and light show is one of the most interesting things in the area for kids.
translations.hypothesis: The pyramids and the Sphinx are among the most impressive things that attract the attention of the youth.

translations.source: O lè rí àwọn pírámìdì yìí nínú òkùnkùn o sì tún le rí wọn ní ídákérọ́rọ́ kí eré náà tó bẹ̀rẹ̀ .
translations.reference: You can see the pyramids in the dark and you can see them in silence before the show begins.
translations.hypothesis: You can see the pyramids in the background and in the intro before the game begins.

translations.source: O ma ń gbọ́ ìró àwọn oníràn afẹ́ àtàwọn òǹtàjà. Ìtàn ohun àti iná dàbi ìwé ìtàn.
translations.reference: Usually you always here the sound of tourists and vendors. The story of the sound and light is just like a story book.
translations.hypothesis: You'll hear stories of survivors and the rescuers. The history of the item and the story behind it are just as important as the item itself.

translations.source: Sphinx ni a lò fi se ìtàgé àti olùsọ ìtàn tó gùn.
translations.reference: The Sphinx is set as the backdrop and the narrator of a long story.
translations.hypothesis: Sphinx is used to create a virtual tour guide and storyteller.

translations.source: Àfihàn àwọn ìwòye di mímọ̀ lórí àwọnn pírámìdì àti wípé onírúurú pírámìdì ma ń tan iná sóke.
translations.reference: The scenes are displayed on the pyramids and the different pyramids are lit up.
translations.hypothesis: The exhibition displays interactive models of the pyramids and how the different pyramids were built.

translations.source: Erekuṣu Guusu Shetland, eyi ti a ṣe awari rẹ ni 1819, ni ọpọlọpọ orilẹ ede sọ wipe awọn ni awọn ni ti wọn si ni ipile ti o pọ ju, pẹlu bi mẹrindinlogun ṣe n ṣiṣẹ ni 2020.
translations.reference: South Shetland Islands, discovered in 1819, are claimed by several nations and have the most bases, with sixteen active in 2020.
translations.hypothesis: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, which were discovered in 1819, are claimed by several nations but are administered by the United Kingdom, which had a permanent population of 20 in 2020.

translations.source: Awon asipelago wan i 120 km apa Arewa Peninsula. Irekusu Oba Jooji to tobi ju wa ni ile Ile Nla La Estrelasi.
translations.reference: The archipelago lies 120 km north of the Peninsula. The largest is King George Island with the settlement of Villa Las Estrellas.
translations.hypothesis: The islands are about 120 km north of the peninsula. The largest is the island of King George, which is home to the capital, Stanley.

translations.source: Apeere awon omiran je Irekusu Livinstini ati Etan ibi yi kldera fokeno to si n sise pese ebute abayeda to je iyalenu.
translations.reference: Others include Livingston Island, and Deception where the flooded caldera of a still-active volcano provides a spectacular natural harbour.
translations.hypothesis: Other attractions include the Liechtenstein Princely Castle and the numerous museums and galleries.

translations.source: Ile Eliswori ni ile to wa ni apa guusu Irekusu, tii Okun Belingisausini yika.
translations.reference: Ellsworth Land is the region south of the Peninsula, bounded by the Bellingshausen Sea.
translations.hypothesis: The Elswyth Estate is a property located in the south of the River Thames, in the Borough of Bexley.

translations.source: Àwọn òkè ilẹ̀ Peninsula ti darapọ̀ di to ní ìpele, ó tún wá parapọ̀ di òkè alásopọ̀ ti oníkìlómítà ọ̀tàlélọ́dọ̀ọ́rún ti àwọn òkè Elisworth, èyí tí Minnesota Glacier pín sí méjì.
translations.reference: The mountains of the Peninsula here merge into the plateau, then re-emerge to form the 360 km chain of the Ellsworth Mountains, bisected by the Minnesota Glacier.
translations.hypothesis: The peninsula's rocky headlands have been carved by the lake into a series of cliffs, the most prominent of which is the 13-mile (21 km) long Pictured Rocks escarpment, the result of the glaciation of the Minnesota River Valley.

translations.source: Ní apá Àríwá tàbí Sentinel Range ni Antarctica tí ó jẹ́ àwọn òkè tí ó ga jù, Vinson Massif, ga to ìwọ̀n maili ọ̀rìnlé ní ẹgbẹ̀rún mẹ́rin àti méjìléláàdórùn ún Òke Vinson.
translations.reference: The northern part or Sentinel Range has Antarctica's highest mountains, the Vinson Massif, peaking at 4892 m Mount Vinson.
translations.hypothesis: In the North or Sentinel Range in Antarctica are some of the highest mountains, the Vinson Massif, whose highest point is 4,892 metres (16,050 ft) above sea level.

translations.source: Ní àwọn ìgbèríko láìsí ẹ̀rọ alágbèéká, fóònù ẹ̀rọ sátálàìtì lè jẹ́ ọ̀nà kan ṣoṣo fún ọ.
translations.reference: In remote locations, without cell phone coverage, a satellite phone may be your only option.
translations.hypothesis: In areas without cell service, a satellite phone may be your only option.

translations.source: Ero ibanisoro oni satelaiti ko wa lati dipo ero ibanisoro adagbe nigbagbogbo, nitori pe o ni lati wa nita gbangba koo de ma foju ri satelaiti bayi, ki o to le fi pe.
translations.reference: A satellite phone is not generally a replacement for a mobile phone, as you have to be outdoors with clear line of sight to the satellite to make a phone call.
translations.hypothesis: Satellite Internet is not a replacement for traditional Internet, because you need a direct line of sight to the satellite, and it is not very mobile.

translations.source: Ìgbọ́jàlọ ló ma ń lo ìpèsè náà dáadáá, pẹ̀lú pleasure craft, àti ìrín àjò tó ní détà àti ohùn.
translations.reference: The service is frequently used by shipping, including pleasure craft, as well as expeditions who have remote data and voice needs.
translations.hypothesis: The service is used by everyone from casual boaters to commercial fishermen, and even guided tours with music and announcements.

translations.source: O ye ki alamojuto ero ibanisoro re ni agbegbe ibile re le fun o ni alaye to kuna nipa lilo eto won.
translations.reference: Your local telephone service provider should be able to give more information about connecting to this service.
translations.hypothesis: It is likely that your local library can provide you with a wealth of information on the use of their facilities.

translations.source: Àwọn ohun tí àwọn ènìyàn ń ṣe jùlọ̀ báyìí, ìyẹn fún ẹni tí ó bá ní ìpinnu láti ní ìsinmi àárín ọdún ní láti rín ìrìn àjò, kó sì kẹ́kọ̀ọ.
translations.reference: An increasingly more popular option for those planning a gap-year is to travel and learn.
translations.hypothesis: The best thing to do, for those who have the opportunity to take a gap year, is to travel and learn.

translations.source: Èyí ló gbajúmọ̀ jù láàrin àwọn tó ti fi iléẹ̀kọ́ sílẹ̀, èyí tó fún wọn láàyè àti gba ààyè ọdún kan sáájú iléẹ̀kọ́ gíga fásitì,láláì gbégirénà ètò ẹ̀kọ́ wọn.
translations.reference: This is especially popular with school leavers, allowing them to take a year out before university, without compromising their education.
translations.hypothesis: This is mostly popular among undergraduates, who get a year to themselves before starting university, without the pressure of continuing with their education.

translations.source: Ni opolopo igba, fifi oruko sile fun iwe kika olodun kan ni ilu oba le je ona si igbega lati koja si ile iwe giga nigba to ba pada si orile’de abinibi re.
translations.reference: In many cases, enrolling on a gap-year course abroad can actually improve your chances of moving into higher education back in your home country.
translations.hypothesis: In many cases, applying for a year-long reading program in the capital city is a prerequisite for getting into a good university when you go back to your home country.

translations.source: Lóní déédé, owó ikẹ́ẹ̀kẹ́ yíò wà lórí àwọn ètò ẹ̀kọ́ wọ̀nyí.
translations.reference: Typically there will be a tuition fee to enroll in these educational programs.
translations.hypothesis: Today, these qualifications are available in select learning centres.

translations.source: Finlandi jẹ ibi tó dára fún wíwa ọkọ̀ ojú omi. Ilẹ̀ tó ní ègbègbé odò kékeré ó ní ègbegbè irékùsù náà, ní àwọn odò kékeré àti ní asipelago elété omi.
translations.reference: Finland is a great boating destination. The "Land of a thousand lakes" has thousands of islands too, in the lakes and in the coastal archipelagos.
translations.hypothesis: Finland is a great place for boating. The country is made up of thousands of lakes and islands, and has a long and varied coastline.

translations.source: Nínu archipelagos àti lakes, o kò fi taratara nílò yacht.
translations.reference: In the archipelagos and lakes you do not necessarily need a yacht.
translations.hypothesis: In the archipelagos and lakes, you don't really need a yacht.

translations.source: Lóòótọ́, àwọn etí òkun archipelagos àti omi adágún tó tóbi jùlọ tóbi lóòótọ́ fún ọkọ̀ ìgbafẹ́ ojú omi, àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi kéékèké tàbí pé ó ń pèsè ìrírí ọ̀tọ̀.
translations.reference: Although the coastal archipelagos and the biggest lakes are indeed big enough for any yacht, smaller boats or even a kayak offer a different experience.
translations.hypothesis: Of course, the tropical islands and the big blue sea are best explored by boat, and a small cruise ship or a sailing yacht offers a unique experience.

translations.source: Wíwọ ọkọ̀-ojú omi jẹ ìsẹẹsí àsèyìnwá ní Orílè-èdè Finland, pèlú ọkọ̀-ojú omi kan si ènìyàn mẹjẹ tàbí mẹjọ.
translations.reference: Boating is a national pastime in Finland, with a boat to every seven or eight people.
translations.hypothesis: Car ownership in Finland is a relatively rare event, with most people using public transportation or biking.

translations.source: Èyí sẹ déédéé pẹ̀lú ilẹ̀ Norway, Sweden àti New Zealand, àmó ó jẹ́ alílẹ́gbé (fún àpẹẹrẹ bí nọ́mbà Netherlands nàa jé ọkan sí ọgójì).
translations.reference: This is matched by Norway, Sweden and New Zealand, but otherwise quite unique (e.g. in the Netherlands the figure is one to forty).
translations.hypothesis: This is broadly similar to Norway, Sweden and New Zealand, but slightly higher (for example the Netherlands’ score was 1.1).

translations.source: Púpọ̀ nínú àwọn àpẹrẹ gbòógi ọkọ̀ ìgbafẹ ojú omi Baltic ni àlékún ìdúró ní St. Petersburg, Russia.
translations.reference: Most of the distinct Baltic Cruises feature an extended stay in St. Petersburg, Russia.
translations.hypothesis: The most common example of Baltic Sea shipworm is the increase in corrosion in St. Petersburg, Russia.

translations.source: Eyi tumọ si wipe o le lọ ri ilu onitan naa fun ọjọ meji dọgba to ba de waa pada ninu ọkọ oju omi lalẹ ti o tun maa sun sibẹ.
translations.reference: This means you can visit the historic city for a couple of full days while returning and sleeping on the ship at night.
translations.hypothesis: This means that you can visit the neighboring country for a maximum of two days and return to the ship and sleep in your cabin.

translations.source: Bí o bá má ń lo apwọn ohun ìrìnnà ojú omi nìkan lọ sí ìlà omi, o kò ní lílò ìwé ìrìnnà mọ̀tọ̀. (fún ọdún 2009.
translations.reference: If you only go ashore using shipboard excursions you will not need a separate visa (as of 2009).
translations.hypothesis: If you are only taking a boat to the islands, you do not need a passport. (as of 2009).

translations.source: Àwọn ọkọ̀ ìgbafẹ́ ojú omi sàfihàn ìlú Berlin, Germany nínú ìwé ìléwọ́. Gẹ́gẹ́ bí o ti ríi nínú áwòrán atọ́ka ayé, Ìlú Berlin kò sí ní agbègbè òkun àti pé ìbẹ̀wò sí ìlú náà kò sí nínú owó ọkọ̀ ojú omi.
translations.reference: Some cruises feature Berlin, Germany in the brochures. As you can see from the map above Berlin is no where near the sea and a visit to the city is not included in the price of the cruise.
translations.hypothesis: The Berlin WelcomeCard offers free travel on public transportation. As you can see in the world map, Berlin is not located near the sea and a visit to the city is not part of a sea voyage.

translations.source: Ìriìn àjò nínú ọkọ̀ òfuruufú lẹ jẹ ìrírí ìjayà fún èyàn lóórẹkóórẹ, pàápàá júlọ tó bá jẹ pé wọn kò tìí fò télè tàbí wọn ti ní ìrírí tó banilérù.
translations.reference: Travelling by plane can be a scary experience for people of all ages and backgrounds, particularly if they've not flown before or have experienced a traumatic event.
translations.hypothesis: Turbulence is a normal part of air travel and is almost never dangerous, even when it is severe.

translations.source: Kìi ṣe nkan ojútíti: kò yàtọ̀ sí àwọn ẹ̀rù bíbà àti ìkórira tí àwọn èyàn púpọ̀ ma n ní.
translations.reference: It is not something to be ashamed of: it is no different from the personal fears and dislikes of other things that very many people have.
translations.hypothesis: It is not a personality trait: it is no more a choice than is being overweight or having diabetes.

translations.source: Fún àwọn kan ẹ̀kọ nípa bí àwọn ọkọ̀ ofurufu kan ṣe má n ṣiṣẹ́ pẹ̀lú nkan tó ma n ṣẹ́lẹ̀ nígbàtí ó n fò, lè bá wọn ṣẹ́gun ẹ̀rù bíbà tí ìpilẹ̀ rẹ̀ jẹ́ nkan àìmọ̀ tàbi àìlèṣàkóso.
translations.reference: For some, understanding something about how aircraft work and what happens during a flight may help to overcome a fear which is based on the unknown or on not being in control.
translations.hypothesis: For some, learning about how airplanes can fly upside down or do loop-de-loops can be a little scary, but it's all about the laws of physics.

translations.source: Àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ tó ń fi ọjà/ẹrù ránṣẹ́ maha ń pa owó iyebíye láti fi nǹkan ránṣẹ́ ní kíakía. Lọ́pọ̀ ìgbà àsìkò ṣe pàtàkì púpọ̀ pẹ́lù àwọn ìwé ìdókowò, ọjà tàbí àwọn ẹ̀yà ara tí wọ́n fi tún nǹkan ṣe ní kíákíá.
translations.reference: Courier companies are well paid for delivering things quickly. Frequently, time is very important with business documents, merchandise or spare parts for an urgent repair.
translations.hypothesis: The shipping industry is responsible for a large portion of global emissions. Often time is of the essence with documents, goods or even body parts needing to be transported quickly.

translations.source: Ní àwọn òpópónà kan, àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ńlánlá ní ọkọ̀ ojú òfurufú wọn, ṣùgbọ́n ní àwọn òpópónà míràn àti ní àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ kékèké, wàhálà wà.
translations.reference: On some routes, the larger companies have their own planes, but for other routes and smaller firms there was a problem.
translations.hypothesis: In some cases, large companies have their own private jets, but in other cases and especially for smaller companies, there are problems.

translations.source: Tí wọ́n bá fi ǹkan ránṣẹ́ nípa lílo ọkọ̀ òfurufú, ní àwọn ọ̀nà kan o lè gbà ọjọ́ díẹ̀ láti gbà ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn ọlọ́pàá ojú ọ̀nà ìrìn àjò.
translations.reference: If they sent things by air freight, on some routes it may have taken days to get through unloading and customs.
translations.hypothesis: If you are shipping by air, you may need to obtain a few documents from the airline.

translations.source: Ona kan soso ti a le fi tete gbe wa ni ki a firanse gege bii eru ti won ti yewo. Awon ofin oko ofurufu o ni je ka fi eru ranse lai si onirinajo, ibe ni iwo ti ma buy.
translations.reference: The only way to get it through faster was to send it as checked luggage. Airline regulations will not allow them to send luggage without a passenger, which is where you come in.
translations.hypothesis: The only way to get them is to buy them from the vendors who are licensed to sell them. There are no legal ways to get them without a prescription.

translations.source: Ọ̀nà tí ó hànde jù láti gbé ọkọ̀ ojú òfúrufú fò ní kílàsì àkọ́kọ́ tàbí to ní olókoòwò ni láti mún owó tó jọjú jáde fún àǹfàní náà (tàbí èyí tí ó dára jù ni kí ó jẹ́ kí ilé iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ kó bá a se).
translations.reference: The obvious way of flying in first or business class is to fork out a thick wad of money for the privilege (or, better yet, get your company to do it for you).
translations.hypothesis: The best way to get a ride in a ride-hailing service is to pay for the service (or have your company pay for it).

translations.source: Síbèsíbè, èyí kò jẹ olówó póókú: gẹ́gẹ́ bí òfin oríowó, ní ìrètí làti san tó ìlọ́pó mẹrin ówó ìrinàjò mèúnù fún ti onísòwò, áti ìlọ́po mọ́kànlá fún ìpín kínní.
translations.reference: However, this does not come cheap: as rough rules of thumb, you can expect to pay up to four times the normal economy fare for business, and eleven times for first class!
translations.hypothesis: However, this is not the case for all trips: according to the fare policy, you are expected to pay four times the normal fare on a business ride and 1.5 times the normal fare on a regular ride.

translations.source: Lákòótán, kòsí ǹkankan nínu wíwá ẹ̀dínwó fún òwò tàbí ìjókòó olówó ńlá ní ọkọ̀ òfurufù tó ń lọ tààrà láti A sí B.
translations.reference: Generally speaking, there is no point in even looking for discounts for business or first-class seats on direct flights from A to B.
translations.hypothesis: Basically, there's nothing more to it than finding a ride in a car going from A to B.

translations.source: Àwọn ilẹ́ isẹ́ ọkọ̀ òfurufú mọ̀ dájú wípẹ́ àwọn ẹgbẹ́ arìnrìn àjò òfurufú tí wọ́n setán láti san ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ owó dọ́là fún ànfànì láti dẹ ibikíbi ní kíákíá àti pèlú ìrọ̀rùn, wọn si máà n gba ìdẹ́yẹlẹ́ tó bójúmu.
translations.reference: Airlines know well that there is a certain core group of flyers who are willing to pay top dollar for the privilege of getting somewhere fast and in comfort, and charge accordingly.
translations.hypothesis: Airlines are increasingly relying on third parties to handle their frequent flyer programs, paying them a commission for each flight booked and often receiving valuable data in return.

translations.source: Ìpínlẹ̀ Moldova jẹ́ Chisinau. Èdè abínibí wọn ni Romanian, ṣùgbọ́n wọ́n ma ń lo èdè Russia jù.
translations.reference: The capital of Moldova is Chişinău. The local language is Romanian, but Russian is widely used.
translations.hypothesis: The capital of Moldova is Chisinau. Their official language is Romanian, but Russian is more commonly used.

translations.source: Moldova jẹ olómìnira ílu tó ní ọ̀pọ̀ èyà tí o tí dojúkọ ìjà ẹléyàmẹ̀yà.
translations.reference: Moldova is a multi-ethnic republic that has suffered from ethnic conflict.
translations.hypothesis: Moldova is a small European country that has faced many challenges.

translations.source: Ní ọdún 1994, ìjà yìí yọrí sí ìdásílẹ̀ ilẹ̀ olómìnira Transnistrialẹ́kùn gúúsù Moldova, èyí tó ní ìjọba tara rẹ̀ àti owó wọn, àmọ́ orílẹ̀ tó jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ àjọ UN.
translations.reference: In 1994, this conflict led to the creation of the self-proclaimed Transnistria Republic in eastern Moldova, which has its own government and currency but is not recognised by any UN member country.
translations.hypothesis: In 1994, this conflict led to the secession of Transnistria, a self-declared independent republic within Moldova, which has its own government and currency, but is not recognised by the UN.

translations.source: Àtúnṣe ti wà fún okùn tó so ètò ọrọ̀ ajé ọnà méjì tí Moldova pín sí, láìbìkítà nípa pé ìṣòro ìdúnàdúrà òṣèlú wà nílẹ̀.
translations.reference: Economic links have been re-established between these two parts of Moldova despite the failure in political negotiations.
translations.hypothesis: The amendment to Moldova's law on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing was approved despite concerns over its vague wording.

translations.source: Ẹ̀sìn gbòógì tó wà ní Moldova ni ẹ̀sìn kìrìsìsítíẹ́nì elérò tótọ́.
translations.reference: The major religion in Moldova is Orthodox Christian.
translations.hypothesis: The predominant religion in Moldova is the Orthodox Christian faith.

translations.source: Ismir ni ìlú tó Tobi jùlọ ní Toki pẹ̀lú èyàn bíi mílíọ́nù 3.7, o ní ebute tó tóbi jù lẹ́yìn Istanbuli àti ile iṣẹ́ ìrìn àjò tó dáa.
translations.reference: İzmir is the third largest city in Turkey with a population of around 3.7 million, the second biggest port after Istanbul, and a very good transport hub.
translations.hypothesis: Izmir is Turkey's third-largest city with a population of 3.7 million, has the second-largest economy after Istanbul and a well-developed infrastructure.

translations.source: Nígbà àtijó ìlú Smyrna, ní báyìí ó jẹ ibùdó ìgbàlódé, ìdàgbàsókè tí o kún fún ìṣòwò, tí a yíká pẹ̀lú omi àti àwọn òkè.
translations.reference: Once the ancient city of Smyrna, it is now a modern, developed, and busy commercial center, set around a huge bay and surrounded by mountains.
translations.hypothesis: In ancient Smyrna, now a modern resort town, development has expanded to fill the coastal plain between the sea and the hills.

translations.source: Àwọn boulevard to fe, ile ti o ni jigi ni iwaju ati oja igbalode ni a fi aja oni taili pupa seso won, oja senturi kejìdílógún, ati awon mọ́ṣáláṣí ati ṣọ́ọ̀si, biotilejepe ilu naa ni afefe to ile Yuropi Mediteraniani ju ile Turkeyi ibile lo.
translations.reference: The broad boulevards, glass-fronted buildings and modern shopping centers are dotted with traditional red-tiled roofs, the 18th century market, and old mosques and churches, although the city has an atmosphere more of Mediterranean Europe than traditional Turkey.
translations.hypothesis: The boulevards, lined with trees, cafes, and shops, are pedestrianized for the most part, with traffic limited to buses, taxis, and delivery vehicles, though the city is much windier than the traditional Mediterranean resort towns.

translations.source: Abúlé Haldarsvikṣe àfihàn ìwòye nítòsí erékùsù Eysturoy o sì tún ní ilé ìjọsìn onígun mẹjọ tí kò̀ wọ́pọ̀.
translations.reference: The village of Haldarsvík offer views of the nearby island Eysturoy and has an unusual octagonal church.
translations.hypothesis: The village of Haldorsvik shows a view to the north of Eysturoy and has a unique octagonal church.

translations.source: Ní àgbàlá ilé ìjọsìn, àwọn àwòrán dídán tò ní àdàbà tó yani lẹ́nu wà lórí àwọn ibojì kan.
translations.reference: In the churchyard, there are interesting marble sculptures of doves over some tombs.
translations.hypothesis: In the temple, there are some murals with erotic scenes.

translations.source: O tó ìdajì wákàtí kan láti rin abúlé ìyàlénu já.
translations.reference: It's worth half an hour to stroll about the intriguing village.
translations.hypothesis: It took almost an hour to get to the hospital.

translations.source: Sí àríwá àti láàrín àwọn ibi tí kò nù ni a ti rí ìlú Sintra tí ó rẹwà fún ìfẹ́ tí ó sì jẹ ojú ní gbèsè, ní èyí tí ó di gbajúgbajà fún àwọn ènìyàn láti ilẹ̀ òkèrè lẹ́yìn tí Lord Byron kọ nípa rẹ.
translations.reference: To the north and within easy reach is the romantic and fascinating town of Sintra and which was made famous to foreigners after a glowing account of its splendours recorded by Lord Byron.
translations.hypothesis: North and inland are the historic and charming town of Sintra, which became popular with foreigners after Lord Byron wrote about it.

translations.source: Boosi Skotobi 403 ma n rin irin ajo deede lo si Sintra o ma n duro ni Kabo da Roka.
translations.reference: Scotturb Bus 403 travels regularly to Sintra, stopping at Cabo da Roca.
translations.hypothesis: The 403 Bus to Sintra usually stops at Cabo da Roca.

translations.source: Ẹ̀wẹ̀, sàbẹ̀wò sí ẹkùn àríwá ni ilé ìsìn Our Lady of Fatima (ojúbọ), ibi tó gbajúmọ̀ káàkiri àgbáyé fún nnkan abàmì.
translations.reference: Also to the north visit the great Sanctuary of Our Lady of Fatima (Shrine), a place of worldwide famous Marian apparitions.
translations.hypothesis: Yes, visit the northern region and the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Fátima (nearby), a world-renowned place of pilgrimage.

translations.source: Jọ̀wọ́ rántí pé ó pandandan kí o ṣàbẹ̀wò sí ilé ìsìnkú tó tóbí, bí ilẹ̀ tó ní ìtumọ̀ sí abala àwọn ènìyàn tó wà ní ilé ayé.
translations.reference: Please remember that you are essentially visiting a mass grave site, as well as a site that has an almost incalculable meaning to a significant portion of the world's population.
translations.hypothesis: Please note that it is necessary to visit a large, reputable funeral home, such as those in well-established residential areas.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ọkùnrin àti obìnrin ló sì wà láyé tí wọ́n móríye àkókò wọn níbí, àti ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn mìíràn tí wọ́n ní àwọn olólùfẹ́ wọ́n tí wọ́n sekúpa tàbí tí wọ́n siṣẹ́ kú níbẹ̀, àwọn Jew àti àwọn tí kìí se Jew rí bákanáà.
translations.reference: There are still many men and women alive who survived their time here, and many more who had loved ones who were murdered or worked to death there, Jews and non-Jews alike.
translations.hypothesis: There are many people alive today who remember that time, and many others who were loved ones of people who were killed or injured in the attacks, both Jewish and non-Jewish.

translations.source: Jọ̀wọ́ fi tọ̀wọ̀tọ̀wọ̀ ṣe pẹlú ilẹ̀ náà, pẹ̀lẹ́pẹ̀lẹ́, sùúrù àti ọ̀wọ̀. Ẹ má ṣe fi Holocaust tàbí Nazis ṣe yẹ̀yẹ.
translations.reference: Please treat the site with all of the dignity, solemnity and respect it deserves. Do not make jokes about the Holocaust or Nazis.
translations.hypothesis: Please treat each other with respect, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender or other factors. There will be zero tolerance for Holocaust or Nazi references.

translations.source: Máṣe bá ojú òpó náà jẹ́ nípa ṣíṣà mí si tàbí àwòrán tó wà ní ogiri.
translations.reference: Do not deface the site by marking or scratching graffiti into structures.
translations.hypothesis: Do not stare at the sun through any optical devices such as telescopes or binoculars.

translations.source: Àwọn èdè ìṣẹ́ Barcelona ní Catalan àti Spanish. Bí ìdajì wọn ló fẹ́ràn láti sọ Catalan, ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ló mọ èdè náà , àti wípé gbogbo ènìyàn ló fẹ́ ẹ̀ mọ èdè Spain.
translations.reference: Barcelona's official languages are Catalan and Spanish. About a half prefer to speak Catalan, a vast majority understands it, and virtually everyone knows Spanish.
translations.hypothesis: The official languages of Barcelona are Catalan and Spanish. As the majority of the population prefers to speak Catalan, most people are fluent in the language, and everyone speaks Spanish.

translations.source: Ṣùgbọ́n púpọ̀ nínú àwọn ìkìlọ̀ ní wọ́n fi Katalani kọ torí oun ní òfin kọ́kọ́ fi ṣe ede gbendek.
translations.reference: However, most signs are indicated only in Catalan because it is established by law as the first official language.
translations.hypothesis: But many signs were written in Catalan because it was the official language.

translations.source: Béèni èdè Spaniṣi ni wọ́n lò ní ọkọ̀ ayọ́kẹ́lẹ́ ti ìjọba àti àwọn ohun èlò míìn.
translations.reference: Yet, Spanish is also widely used in public transport and other facilities.
translations.hypothesis: Spanish is the official language of the country and is used in government and media.

translations.source: Èdè catalan nìkan ni wọ́n máa fi ń ṣe ìkéde lásán ní agbègbè, ṣùgbọ́n àwọn ìkéde pàjáwìrì ni wọ́n máa n ṣe pẹlú oríṣìíríṣìí èdè bí i Spanish, English, French, Arabic àti Japanes.
translations.reference: Regular announcements in the Metro are made only in Catalan, but unplanned disruptions are announced by an automated system in a wide variety of languages including Spanish, English, French, Arabic and Japanese.
translations.hypothesis: Only Catalan is used in local signage, but emergency announcements are made in several languages including Spanish, English, French, Arabic and Japanese.

translations.source: A mọ Parisian fún orúkọ ,bí wọ́n ṣe jẹ́ aláìlẹ́kọ̀ọ́ wọ́n sì tùn ní ìgbéraga.
translations.reference: Parisians have a reputation for being egocentric, rude and arrogant.
translations.hypothesis: The Parisians are known by their name, as they are considered to be rude and arrogant.

translations.source: Níwọ̀n ìgbà tí èyí kìí se ìwòye tó se déédéé ní gbogbo ìgbà, ọ̀nà tó dára jùlọ láti sẹ dáradára ní Paris ni láti jé ọmọlúwàbí ní ìhùwàsí bí ẹni tó gbẹ́ẹ̀kọ́ ilé. Èyí máa jẹ kí lílọ káàkiri seése ní ìrọrùn.
translations.reference: While this is often only an inaccurate stereotype, the best way to get along in Paris still is to be on your best behavior, acting like someone who is "bien élevé" (well brought up). It will make getting about considerably easier.
translations.hypothesis: While this isn't always the case, the best way to get around Paris is often on foot. This will make getting around very easy.

translations.source: Abuku gbangba awon ara Parisia ni yio poora ti o ba ni awon iwe iteriba kookan.
translations.reference: Parisians' abrupt exteriors will rapidly evaporate if you display some basic courtesies.
translations.hypothesis: The public debt of the French Republic is bound up with the national debt.

translations.source: Ọgbà Ìdárayá Ìlú ti Odò Plitfisi kún fún igbó pẹ̀lú ẹ̀gbẹ́ omi, igi sprusi àti igi fígì àti àdàpọ̀ ewé Alpini àti Mẹditereniani.
translations.reference: The Plitvice Lakes national park is heavily forested, mainly with beech, spruce, and fir trees, and features a mixture of Alpine and Mediterranean vegetation.
translations.hypothesis: Plitvice Lakes National Park is a forest landscape with lakes, streams and waterfalls, and a rich flora and fauna of the Alpine and Mediterranean regions.

translations.source: A Ṣàkíyèsí púpọ̀ pe ọ̀pọ̀ ayika ewe nítorí maikroklaimeeti rẹ̀ tó pọ̀, yẹ̀pẹ̀ tó yàtọ̀ ati ìṢesí afẹ́fẹ́.
translations.reference: It has a notably wide variety of plant communities, due to its range of microclimates, differing soils and varying levels of altitude.
translations.hypothesis: We find most tropical rainforests to be very noisy because of the many sounds of life, including the sounds of insects, birds, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, and the wind.

translations.source: Agbègbè náà jẹ́ bí ilé fún àwọn ẹranko àti ẹye.
translations.reference: The area is also home to an extremely wide variety of animal and bird species.
translations.hypothesis: The area is home to a wide variety of animals and plants.

translations.source: Àwọn ẹranko tí kò wọ́pọ̀ bí i ti béárì aláwọ̀ búráwùn, ìkokò, idì, òwìwí, ológìnní ijù àti capercaillie ti ilẹ̀ Europe la lè rí pẹ̀lú àwọn ẹ̀yà ẹranko tó wọ́pọ̀ míràn.
translations.reference: Rare fauna such as the European brown bear, wolf, eagle, owl, lynx, wild cat and capercaillie can be found there, along with many more common species
translations.hypothesis: Less common species such as the blue bear, bison, lynx, wolverine, elk and European capercaillie can also be seen in their natural habitats.

translations.source: Lákòkò àbẹ̀wò síléègbé àwọn mọ́ǹkì, wọ́n ní káwọn obìnrin wọ yẹ̀rì tó bòwọ́n lẹ́sẹ̀, kí wọ́n sì bo èjìká wọn pẹ̀lú.
translations.reference: While visiting the monasteries, women are required to wear skirts covering the knees and have their shoulders covered, too.
translations.hypothesis: During visits to monasteries, women were required to wear long skirts and cover their heads.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ilẹ́ ìdáwà máà n pẹ̀sẹ̀ asọ ìrọ̀rùn fún àwọn obìnrin tí o ba mùra dada sìlẹ ki wọn tọ wá, sùgbọn ti o bá mú tirẹ lọwọ, paapaa julọ eyi to ni awọ didan, ẹrin in arakunrin tabi arabinrin yo fi gba ọ wole lẹnu ọna.
translations.reference: Most of the monasteries do provide wraps for women who come unprepared, but if you bring your own, especially one with bright colors, you'll get a smile from the monk or nun at the entrance.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the two-star hotels cater to a more casual crowd, and while they're usually fine if you're a woman traveling alone, you're better off staying elsewhere, especially if you're a man or a couple.

translations.source: Ní ọ̀rọ̀ kánáà, wọ́n ti ní káwọn ọkùnrin má a wọ ṣòkòtò tó bó orúnkún wọn.
translations.reference: Along the same line, men are required to wear trousers covering the knees.
translations.hypothesis: In most cases, men are circumcised to fulfill a religious requirement.

translations.source: Èyí náà lè jẹ́ yíyá nínú àkójọ tó wà ní ẹnu ọ̀nà àmọ́ wọn kò fọ àwọn aṣọ wọ̀nyí nígbà tí wọ́n lò ó tán, ara rẹ lé má se dáradára láti wọ́ àwọn yẹ̀rì yìí. Ọ̀kan ti se rẹ́gí fáwọn ọkùnrin!
translations.reference: This too can be borrowed from the stock at the entrance but that clothing isn't washed after every user so you may not feel comfortable wearing these skirts. One size fits all for men!
translations.hypothesis: This is probably due to the fact that the ones available in the streets around them are not made to last, and your average tailor is not well equipped to make these items. One is for the guys!

translations.source: Ìlànà ìdáná àwọn Majorcan bí i ti àwọn tó wà ní agbègbè omi, ló dá lórí búrẹ́dì, ẹ̀fọ́ àti ẹran (pàápàá jùlọ ẹran ẹlẹ́dẹ̀), tí wọ́n si ma ń lo òróró ólìfù.
translations.reference: Majorcan cuisine, like that of similar zones in the Mediterranean, is based on bread, vegetables and meat (specially pork), and uses olive oil throughout.
translations.hypothesis: The traditional diet of the Mallorcan people, typical of the Mediterranean area, is based on vegetables, legumes and meat (mainly pork), using olive oil as the main source of fat.

translations.source: Oúnjẹ alẹ́ tí ó gbajúgbajà pàápàá jùlọ ní àkókò yìí ni Pa amb Oil: búrẹ́dì pẹ̀lú olive oil, tòmátì, ati èyíkéyì ohun tí ẹnu ń jẹ́ bí i wàrà, ẹja tuna abbl.
translations.reference: A simple popular dinner, especially during the summer, is the Pa amb Oli: Bread with olive oil, tomato, and any available condiments such as cheese, tunafish, etc.
translations.hypothesis: The most common foods during this period were a sort of porridge made from barley or wheat, dates, figs, and whatever else the local cuisine provided, such as fish, cheese, or legumes.

translations.source: Gbogbo ọ́rọ́ orúkọ pèlú ọ́rọ́ Sie fun ọ, nígbogbo ìgbà bẹ̀rẹ̀ pèlú lẹ́ta ńla, kò baa sẹ ní ààrin gbólohùn.
translations.reference: All nouns, alongside the word Sie for you, always begin with a capital letter, even in the middle of a sentence.
translations.hypothesis: All words starting with a capital letter, followed by a colon, are acronyms.

translations.source: Ona to se patakilati fi mo iyato ninu awon oro ise ati oro oruko to n gba is.
translations.reference: This is an important way to distinguish between some verbs and objects.
translations.hypothesis: The best way to learn the differences is by reading a lot of sentences and words in context.

translations.source: A lè jiyan pe o ma n mú kí ìwé kíkà rọrùn si, ṣùgbọ́́n ìwé kika ṣòro tori Èyàn níláti wadi bóyá ilo ọ̀rọ̀ ìṣe àti ọ̀rọ̀ ìjúwe lọ́́nà tó fi ifiyesi ha.
translations.reference: It also arguably makes reading easier, though writing is somewhat complicated by the need to find out whether a verb or adjective is used in a substantivized form.
translations.hypothesis: We can argue that it makes reading easier, but reading is hard because the human brain is not designed to process words and sentences in the way they are presented.

translations.source: Gbigbe oro jade fi be rorun pelu ede Itili nigba to je pe bi won se pe bee na ni won se ko
translations.reference: Pronunciation is relatively easy in Italian since most words are pronounced exactly how they are written
translations.hypothesis: The text is easy to read and understand in English, even though the original was in Yoruba.

translations.source: Awon oro ti o se koko lati se akiyesi ni c ati g, nitori pipe won da le awon faweli wonyi.
translations.reference: The main letters to watch out for are c and g, since their pronunciation varies based on the following vowel.
translations.hypothesis: The letters c and g are the most common to be confused because of their similar shapes.

translations.source: Bákanáà, se àrídájú pé o pe r ati rr lọ́tọ́ọ̀tọ̀: caro túmọ̀ sí ọ̀wọ́n nígbàtí carro túmọ̀ sí kẹ̀kẹ́ ẹṣin.
translations.reference: Also, make sure to pronounce r and rr differently: caro means dear, whereas carro means chariot.
translations.hypothesis: By the way, be careful to distinguish between "caro" and "carro": caro means "dear" while carro means "car".

translations.source: Èdè Persia ni gírámà tó rọrùn díẹ̀ tó sì tún ní ìlànà jọjọ.
translations.reference: Persian has a relatively easy and mostly regular grammar.
translations.hypothesis: The Persian language has a relatively simple and regular morphology.

translations.source: Fun idi eyi, kika iwe girama yi yio fun ọ ni anfani lati mọ nipa girama Persian ati ki oriṣiriṣi gbolohun le ye ọ daada.
translations.reference: Therefore, reading this grammar primer would help you learn much about Persian grammar and understand phrases better.
translations.hypothesis: For this reason, reading this book will give you a good overview of Persian grammar and vocabulary.

translations.source: Láìsí àní àní, bí o bá mọ èdè Róòmù, yí ó rọrùn fún ọ láti kọ́ èdè ilẹ̀ portugal.
translations.reference: Needless to say, if you know a Romance language, it will be easier for you to learn Portuguese.
translations.hypothesis: Of course, if you know Romanian, it will be easy for you to learn Portuguese.

translations.source: Àmọ́ṣá, àwọn ènìyàn tó ma èdè ilẹ̀ Spain díẹ̀ lè tètè sọ wípé èdè ilẹ̀ Portugal súnmọ́ ra nítorínà kò nílò pé ènìyàn ń kọ́ ọ.
translations.reference: However, people who know a little Spanish may hastily conclude that Portuguese is close enough that it need not be studied separately.
translations.hypothesis: However, some Spanish speakers may find it easy to understand spoken Portuguese because of the similarities between the two languages.

translations.source: Àwọn àkíyèsí ayé àtijó lọ́pòlọpọ̀ ìgbà kò ní ìwúlò lónìí, àti wípé wọn wà bi ilé ìkó iṣẹ́ ọnà sí tàbí àyè ikẹẹ̀kọ. .
translations.reference: Pre-modern observatories are usually obsolete today, and remain as museums, or sites of education.
translations.hypothesis: Many historical landmarks are no longer functional, and serve only as tourist attractions or educational resources.

translations.source: Torípé ìṣòro ẹ̀gbin iná óyàtọ̀ sí bó ṣe wà lónìí, wọ́n ma n sábà wà ní ilu tàbí ọgbà ilé ìwé, o rọrùn láti débẹ̀ jú àwọn tí a kọ́ ní igbalode lọ.
translations.reference: As light pollution in their heyday was not the kind of problem it is today, they are usually located in cities or at campuses, easier to reach than those built in modern times.
translations.hypothesis: While the inconvenience of gas stoves is obvious to anyone who's used one, the benefits of an induction cooktop are more subtle.

translations.source: Ọpọ̀ àwọn ẹ̀ro ìwòyẹ ìgbàlódẹ fún ìwádìí jẹ àwọn ohun ẹ̀lò títóbi jọjọ ní àwọn agbẹ̀gbẹ̀ ọ̀nà jiínjín to ni àwọn ọjú ọjọ́ dáradára.
translations.reference: Most modern research telescopes are enormous facilities in remote areas with favorable atmospheric conditions.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the best-studied model organisms are multicellular eukaryotes with relatively simple genomes.

translations.source: Hanami, tí í ṣe ìwò-cherry-tí-ó-rẹwà ti wà nínú àṣà àwọn Japan láti Sẹ́ńtúrì kẹjọ.
translations.reference: Cherry blossom viewing, known as hanami, has been a part of Japanese culture since the 8th century.
translations.hypothesis: Cherry blossom viewing, known as hanami, has been a popular pastime in Japan since the Nara period (710–794).

translations.source: Láti orílèèdè China ni èrò àtinúdá náà ti wá, níbi tí èso igi púlùmù ti jẹ́ òdòdó tí ó yááyì jùlọ.
translations.reference: The concept came from China where plum blossoms were the flower of choice.
translations.hypothesis: The idea for the product was from China, where the paper cutting is a very popular folk art.

translations.source: Ní orílẹ̀èdè Japan, àwọn olórí nìkan ni ó má ń sayẹyẹ èso ṣẹ́ẹ́ẹ́rì fúnra ara wọn àtàwọn èèkàn nídí iṣẹ́ ọba mìíran nínú ìgbìmọ̀ ọba mìíràn.
translations.reference: In Japan, the first cherry blossom parties were hosted by the emperor only for himself and other members of the aristocracy around the Imperial Court.
translations.hypothesis: In Japan, only the Emperor and the Empress may wear the chrysanthemum symbol on their own person, while other members of the Imperial Family may only wear it when undertaking official duties.

translations.source: Àwọn ewéko máa ń rẹwà nígbà tí wọ́n bá wà ní ààyè wọn, fún ìdí èyí yẹra fún fífọwọ́ kan àwọn ewéko wọ̀nyí.
translations.reference: Plants look their best when in a natural environment, so resist the temptation to remove even "just one" specimen.
translations.hypothesis: The plants are very sensitive to their environment, so any attempt to domesticate them has so far been unsuccessful.

translations.source: Ti o ba lo gba specimeni nigba ti o ba lo be ogba ti won ti to, won maa le e kuro lai koko ba e soro.
translations.reference: If visiting a formally arranged garden, collecting "specimens" is also going to get you ejected, without discussion.
translations.hypothesis: If you use a specimen collection bag, it can be easily disposed of after use.

translations.source: Singapore jẹ́ ibi tó ní àbò jùlọ láti wà ó sì rọrùn láti lọ kiri, o sì lè ra gbogbo ǹkan tí o bá dé ibẹ̀.
translations.reference: Singapore is generally an extremely safe place to be and very easy to navigate, and you can buy almost anything after arriving.
translations.hypothesis: Singapore is the safest place to be and is easy to get around and purchase anything you may need.

translations.source: Ṣùgbọ́n tí wọ́n bá fi é sí “ilẹ̀ oru òkè” ni apá arewa ikwetọ̀ oru (nígbà gbogbo) àti òrùn tóle (nígbà tí ọjọ́ bá dá, kìí fibẹ́ wáyé) lo ma bá fàá.
translations.reference: But being placed in the "high tropics" just a few degrees north of equator you will need to deal with both heat (always) and strong sun (when the sky is clear, more rarely).
translations.hypothesis: But if it is in the "hot zone" in the north of the country (almost always) and the sun is shining (when it is not cloudy) it can be very hot.

translations.source: Àwọn ọkọ́ akérò díẹ̀ tó ń lọ sí àríwá sí Hebron, ìsìnkú náà wáyé ní Biblical patriarch Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, àti àwọn ìyàwó wọn.
translations.reference: There are also a few buses going north to Hebron, the traditional burial place of the Biblical patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and their wives.
translations.hypothesis: The bus was headed north towards Hebron, a city revered by the Biblical patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and their wives.

translations.source: Yẹ̀wò bóya boosi to fẹ́ wọ̀ ma dé Hebroni kii ṣe ilẹ̀ Ju itosi ibe Kiriyati Arba.
translations.reference: Check that the bus you are thinking of taking goes into Hebron and not just to the nearby Jewish settlement of Kiryat Arba.
translations.hypothesis: Check if your passport is valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

translations.source: Àwọn ojú ọ̀nà omi abẹ́lé lè jẹ́ àkolé tó dára láti gbé ìsinmi lẹ́nu iṣẹ́ lé lórí.
translations.reference: Inland waterways can be a good theme to base a holiday around.
translations.hypothesis: Natural waterways can be a good base from which to launch a career break.

translations.source: Fún àpẹrẹ sísé àbẹ̀wò sí ilé ńlá iLoire, àfonífojì ti Rhine àbí wíwá ọkọ̀ ojú omi kekeré sí àwọn ibi tí a nífẹ̀ẹ́ sí ní Danube àbí wiwa ọkọ̀ ojú omi kọjá Erie Canal.
translations.reference: For example visiting castles in the Loire Valley, the Rhine valley or taking a cruise to interesting cites on the Danube or boating along the Erie Canal.
translations.hypothesis: For example, take a cruise on the Loire, a Rhine River cruise or a small ship cruise to the highlights of the Danube or a cruise through the Erie Canal.

translations.source: Wọ́n tún sàlàyé ọ̀nà fún pípọ́n òkè àti ojú ipa ìyípo.
translations.reference: They also define routes for popular hiking and cycling trails.
translations.hypothesis: They also described the process of mountain building and the effects of volcanism.

translations.source: Kẹ́rẹ́sìmẹsì jẹ́ ọ̀kan lára ìsinmi tó se pàtàkì jùlọ nínú ẹ̀sìn Krìstẹ́nì, ó sì tún jẹ́ àjọyọ ọjọ́ ìbí Jẹ́sù.
translations.reference: Christmas is one of the most important holidays of Christianity, and is celebrated as the birthday of Jesus.
translations.hypothesis: Christmas is one of the most important holidays in the Christian faith, and it is the celebration of Jesus Christ's birth.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ìṣe tó yí ìsinmi ká ní àwọn tí kìí ṣe onígbàgbọ́ láwọn orílẹ̀èdè àwọn ọmọlẹ́yìn Kristi àti àwọn tí kì í ṣe ọmọlẹ́yìn Kristi lágbàáyé.
translations.reference: Many of the traditions surrounding the holiday have been adopted also by non-believers in Christian countries and non-Christians around the world.
translations.hypothesis: Most of the actions to stop FGM are led by non-religious people in both Christian and non-Christian communities around the world.

translations.source: Àṣà kan wà láti se àìsùn ní alẹ́ ọjọ́ àj.
translations.reference: There's a tradition to pass the Easter night awake at some exposed point to see the sunrise.
translations.hypothesis: There is a curfew in effect every night.

translations.source: Àlàyé ẹ̀kọ́ inú ẹ̀sin kìrìsìtẹ́nì mẹ̀rin ló wà fún ìse yìí, àmọ́ ó lẹ̀ jẹ́ àkókò tí ẹ̀sin kìrìsìtẹ́nì ò tí ì dé àti ìrúbọ ìbímọ.
translations.reference: There are of course Christian theological explanations for this tradition, but it may well be a pre-Christian Spring and Fertility ritual.
translations.hypothesis: There are four Christian accounts of the event, though they differ in some details.

translations.source: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ṣọ́ọ̀ọì ni wọn má a ń ṣe ìṣọ́-òru ọdún àjíǹde ni alẹ́ ọjọ́ Àbámẹ̀ta òpin ọ̀sẹ̀ àjíǹde. Ní ọ̀gànjọ́ òru, àwọn ọmọ ìjọ a má a fò fún ayọ̀ nítorí àjíǹde Krístì.
translations.reference: More traditional churches often hold an Easter Vigil on Saturday night during the Easter weekend, with the congregations often breaking into celebration at the stroke of midnight to celebrate Christ's resurrection.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the concerts are held on Friday night or Saturday night. On Saturday, the youth of the church often put on a concert to celebrate Christ's love.

translations.source: Wiwẹ, fifo loju ofurufu ati fifo loju omi ni ọna ti gbogbo ẹranko ti o koko de awọn irukusu gba debi.
translations.reference: All animals that originally arrived in the islands came here either by swimming, flying or floating.
translations.hypothesis: Finally, the deposition of dust and ash is the means by which all other forms of life are blanketed in the aftermath of the eruption.

translations.source: Látàrí ọ̀nà jínjìn láti kọ́ńtìnẹ̀ntì, àwọn ẹranko abìyẹ́ kò lè bá ìrìnàjò,èyí tó mún kí ìjàpá ńlá jẹ́ ẹranko ìwá oúnjẹ nínú Galapagos.
translations.reference: Due to the long distance from the continent mammals were unable to make the journey making the giant tortoise the primary grazing animal in the Galapagos.
translations.hypothesis: Due to the great distances between the continents, the animals could not migrate, so the giant tortoises became the largest animals on the Galapagos.

translations.source: Látìgbà tí ọmọnìyàn ti dé sí Galapagos, ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ẹranko abìyẹ́ ni wọ́n ti se àfihàn nínú èyí tí àwọn ewúrẹ́, ẹṣin, màálù, eku, ológìnní, àti àwọn ajá.
translations.reference: Since the arrival of man to the Galapagos, many mammals have been introduced including goats, horses, cows, rats, cats and dogs.
translations.hypothesis: Since humans have arrived in the Galapagos, many species have been introduced including pigs, goats, cats, dogs, rats and mice.

translations.source: Bí o bá se àbẹ̀wò sí agbègbè Arctic tàbí Antarctic nínú otútù, wà á ní ìrírí alẹ́ pólà, èyí tó túmọ̀ sí wípé òòrùn kì í yọ lókè ọ̀rún.
translations.reference: If you visit the Arctic or Antarctic areas in the winter you will experience the polar night, which means that the sun doesn't rise above the horizon.
translations.hypothesis: If you visit the Arctic or Antarctic regions during winter, you will experience the polar night, which means that the sun does not rise above the horizon.

translations.source: Eyi fu ni ni aye to dara lati ri ati ri Aurora borealis, nitori pe oju orun maa dudu ni gbogbo igba.
translations.reference: This offers a good opportunity to see the Aurora borealis, as the sky will be dark more or less around the clock.
translations.hypothesis: This is also a good time to see the Aurora Borealis, as the sky is often dark enough.

translations.source: Bí àdúgbò náà ti ní èrò, àti tí iná sì pọ̀, torí náà kìí sí ìṣòro ní ọ̀pọ̀ ìgbà, o tún máa lè gbádùn ìràwọ̀.
translations.reference: As the areas are sparsely populated, and light pollution therefore often not a problem, you will also be able to enjoy the stars.
translations.hypothesis: As a group we had a good time, and although the light was poor, it was still possible to make out the details.

translations.source: Aṣa ibi iṣẹ Japanisi kun fu oye ati iṣedeede ju nkan to ti mọ awọn ara Oke Okun lar.
translations.reference: Japanese work culture is more hierarchical and formal that what Westerners may be used to.
translations.hypothesis: Japanese work culture is more formal and hierarchical than what you may be used to in the West.

translations.source: Súùtù jẹ́ aṣọ okoòwò àwọn alájọse sì ma ń fi orúkọ ìdílé tàbí àpèlé iṣẹ́ perawọn.
translations.reference: Suits are standard business attire, and coworkers call each other by their family names or by job titles.
translations.hypothesis: Suits are business attire and are often worn with a family name or job title on them.

translations.source: Ìbáṣepsọ̀ ní ibi iṣẹ́ ṣe pàtàkì, títẹnumọ́ àkitiyan ẹgbẹ́ ju kí wọ́n ma gboríyín ǹkan tí oníkálùkù ti gbé ṣe.
translations.reference: Workplace harmony is crucial, emphasizing group effort rather than praising individual accomplishments.
translations.hypothesis: Teamwork is essential, amplifying the collective over individual accolades.

translations.source: Ó yé kí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ ma gba ìfọwọ́sí láti ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn ọ̀gá wọn fún ìpinu tí wọ́n bá ṣe, ó sì yẹ kí wọ́n gbọ́nràn sí àwọn ọ̀gá wọn lẹ́nu láì bèrè ìbéèrè.
translations.reference: Workers must often get their superiors' approval for any decisions they make, and are expected to obey their superiors' instructions without question.
translations.hypothesis: Employees should receive approval from their supervisors for any breaks they take and should communicate with their supervisors about their breaks.
